Teleports the player when they acquire a certain amount of coins.
Includes a define to invert the condition.

packages.name: smwblocks-teleport-on-event-passed
packages.title: Teleport on Event Passed
packages.description:
Teleports the player depending on in an overworld event has been triggered.

Includes a define to invert the condition.

packages.name: smwblocks-teleport-on-lives
packages.title: Teleport on Lives
packages.description:
Teleports the player if they have a certain amount of lives.

Includes a define to invert the condition.

packages.name: smwblocks-teleport-on-powerup
packages.title: Teleport on Powerup
packages.description:
Teleports the player if they have a certain powerup.

Includes a define to invert the condition.

packages.name: smwblocks-teleport-on-sprite-touch
packages.title: Teleport on Sprite Touch
packages.description: Teleports the player when touched by a specific sprite.

packages.name: smwblocks-teleport-on-switch
packages.title: Teleport on Switch
packages.description:
Teleports the player if a switch (blue or silver P-Switch, ON/OFF, switch palace, or even a custom free RAM switch) is active.

Includes a define to invert the condition.

packages.name: smwblocks-teleport-on-time
packages.title: Teleport on Time
packages.description:
Teleports the player depending on the time limit.

Includes a define to invert the condition.

Note that this uses decimal mode and due an old bug in the SD2SNES/FXPak, issues might occur when using SA-1 in this flash cart. The newest firmware doesn't have this issue, so use that.

packages.name: smwblocks-teleport-on-yoshi-coins
packages.title: Teleport on Yoshi Coins
packages.description:
Teleports the player if they have a certain amount of Yoshi coins.

Includes a define to invert the condition.

packages.name: smwblocks-teleport-on-yoshi-riding
packages.title: Teleport on Yoshi Riding
packages.description:
This block will teleport the player only if he is riding Yoshi.

Includes a define to invert the condition.

packages.name: smwblocks-teletimer-block
packages.title: Teletimer block
packages.description: This block will teleport you if you hit it exactly when the timer is (specified in ASM file).

packages.name: smwblocks-ten-seconds-then-shatter
packages.title: Ten Seconds Then Shatter
packages.description:
This block will add 10 seconds to the level time and then shatter.
Requested by shreerocks1324

packages.name: smwblocks-thermal-block
packages.title: Thermal Block
packages.description:
When you hit this block with a fireball it will "heat up" (change into the next Map 16 page tile) for a certain amount of times, then when it is at its max heat, it will hurt Mario and kill sprites, and "cool down" (change into the last Map 16 page block). Once again I apologize Vanya for the misunderstanding...

PM me if you find any bugs.

packages.name: smwblocks-throw-blocks-pack
packages.title: Throw Blocks Pack
packages.description:
This block pack contains 5 blocks:

-a block, when pressing dash, will spawn a throw block while the block itself still there (unlike smw). Its called "infinite_throwblk.asm". When using this, you can forget about using reset doors, since it reduces "stuck problems".

-a "brick" that can only be shattered by throw blocks, and if mario *KICKS* it into them will pierce through them. Its called "shatter_throwblk.asm".

-a bumper that bounces the throw block without shattering it.

-a solid block that only allows a throw block to pass

-and a "Stopper & preserver" that traps the throw block on contact and keeps its "dissipates" timer at #$FF

This is useful for puzzles.

Have fun.

packages.name: smwblocks-thwomp-crush-block
packages.title: Thwomp Crush Block
packages.description:
This block will break when Thwomp comes into contact with it. Read the readme for more and better details.
Act-like recommended to be 130.

Update: It now checks the sprite status of normal/custom Thwomp sprites and the type of brick shatter can now be specified in the asm file.

packages.name: smwblocks-tightrope
packages.title: Tightrope
packages.description:
Done at S.N.N. request.

Mario may travel on this block if he is slow (walking), but will fall off if he is running.

packages.name: smwblocks-time-block
packages.title: Time Block
packages.description: If you reach this block before a certain amount of time has passed in the level, it will give you a prize. There are three blocks included: one that will spawn a normal sprite, one that will spawn a custom sprite, and one that will turn into the next Map16 tile. Made by request.

packages.name: smwblocks-timer-change
packages.title: Timer Change
packages.description:
Sets the timer to a fixed time -- in this case, 040 (40 SMW seconds left).

timeonce.asm only runs once per level, which means it will not set the timer to said fixed time a second time.
timehold.asm runs continuously when touched and as such, the timer will stay the same while touching the block.

packages.name: smwblocks-titlescreen-reset-block
packages.title: Titlescreen Reset Block
packages.description: A block that brings you back to the titlescreen when touched. It also plays SFX.

packages.name: smwblocks-tower-of-heaven-fan
packages.title: Tower of Heaven Fan
packages.description:
Not to be confused with the simple blocks that DEC/SEC : SBC your $96 Y position to make you float.

This is a fan block that sends the player flying upwards in an acceleration-based momentum gradually unlike traditional boost blocks (which changes your momentum instantly). The longer or lower you are touching this block, the higher the player is sent. Inspired by the propellers from Tower of Heaven by askiisoft.

packages.name: smwblocks-toxic-block-v1
packages.title: Toxic Block v1.01
packages.description:
This block will activate a timer when it is touched by Mario, and then hurt/kill Mario when the timer runs out. The timer resets every time Mario isn't touching a toxic block. Also an 8x8 sprite indicator will appear near Mario when the timer is close to running out.
Depending on the "Act as", you could make toxic water, air, cement, etc.

The zip contains two files: one is the block asm, which contains some parameters that can be edited to what you want and then it must be inserted with GPS, and the other must be inserted with UberASMTool (as level asm or gamemode asm) to make the blocks work properly. More information can be found in those files.

Update v1.01: the exclamation mark is now drawn accordingly to the direction that Mario is facing.

packages.name: smwblocks-trampoline-block-v1
packages.title: Trampoline Block v1.2
packages.description:
Acts as 025 or 130.

Inspired by NSMB's Bouncy Mushrooms in World 1-5.

Unlike all other boost blocks, in order to bounce high, it requires the player to tap and hold the jump/spinjump button the instant they land on top of the block rather than also requiring just to hold the jump/spinjump button before landing.

Uses 3 bytes of freeram:
-!FreeRam_TimedJump is the margin of error range that allows the player to press a button within the window of time when bounced.
-!FreeRam_Ylow and !FreeRam_Yhi is a fix to prevent slightly higher jump.

packages.name: smwblocks-tricky-item-blocks
packages.title: Tricky Item Blocks
packages.description:
Do you know when there is a couple of question/turn blocks, and most of them have coins and only one of them has an item? With this block, you can make that so the item will be always in the last block the player hits!

You can define which item the last block will have into, how many blocks are in the couple, and even if they're either question or turn blocks!

Remember to set up everything correctly in the ASM file. Have fun!

packages.name: smwblocks-vertical-and-horizontal-wrap-blocks
packages.title: vertical and horizontal wrap blocks
packages.description:
Similar or imspired to the Horizontal Level Wrap and the vertical level wrap but in block instead of sprite generator. Making it useful if you want a generator and a wrap in the same level. Or have a pit and a horizontal level wrap in the same level.

differences:
-horizontal wrap block does not require mario to be offscreen before warping, making getting to the bottom of the screen from the top easier. It also fix the glitch where mario can go inside the wall and die (as small mario/crouching big mario) at the top edge of the screen.

-vertical wrap block does not stop the player's x speed when mario hits the side of the screen (meaning that after he warps, his x speed is zero for the sprite generator sometimes)

-both these blocks does not work for sprites that does not interact with blocks (flying winged koopa, bullet bill etc.)

Thanks to JackTheSpades for finding out the sprite's position so if warps block-interacting sprites.

Read the How_to_setup.png to find how to place the blocks correctly. Also in vertical level, make sure mario is on the far left possible, or the screen isn't on the correct spot when mario enter the vertical level.

packages.name: smwblocks-vertical-warp-door
packages.title: vertical warp door
packages.description:
This is a door that, when entered will instantly warp mario a few blocks up or down depending on the block you are using. To change the number of blocks of how far mario will teleport is just under the list of offset on the top. Please read the readme before using.

This is useful if you are making a place with multiple of floors and use these doors as a "floor switching maze". Or used in castles in a vertical level.

Added to this block:
-check if mario is holding a sprite and in the air.
-center mario (in the middle) when he enter the door so mario don't have possibility of entering the door on the edge and warp inside of the block when placed next to the area where mario exits.

packages.name: smwblocks-vertical-wind-blocks
packages.title: Vertical Wind Blocks
packages.description: This package contains 3 blocks: One pushes you up, one pushes you down and one pushes you up, and when you press down, you fall.

packages.name: smwblocks-vine-entrance-block
packages.title: Vine Entrance Block
packages.description: This block makes the player automatically start on the vine upon entering a level, as long as the player isn't able to touch ground at the same time. Credit not needed, but it would be nice. Block changes to standard vine tile after touching it.

packages.name: smwblocks-vvvvvv-gravity-physics-v1-0
packages.title: VVVVVV Gravity Physics v1.0.1
packages.description:
A gimmick from VVVVVV that replaces the jump button with a switch gravity and white lines also switch gravity.

Note that the instructions for insertion and usage differ slightly if you're using Callisto.

packages.name: smwblocks-wall-run-activated-block
packages.title: Wall Run Activated Block
packages.description:
This is a block that is triggered upon wall running. Credit unnecessary, but appreciated.

In order to specify the block type that gets activated during the wall run, set the act as to whatever the original block's map16 number is. For example, if you want coin blocks to activate upon the wall run, set the act as of this block to 124.

Note that this block is incompatible with layer 2 and blocks such as the on/off switch and note blocks will revert to their vanilla state after being triggered once. This is due to how the hit animation restores the block to its original map16 form, rather than the custom form. These will likely be updated in the future, but for single-use blocks such as coins and powerups, this works quite well.

packages.name: smwblocks-walljump-blocks
packages.title: Walljump Blocks
packages.description:
A set of walljump blocks with the following features:
- The player cannot rear back early, with the left/right D-pad controls disabled temporarily so they cannot gain more height on the same wall.
- It changes the player's left/right facing direction while the timer is running.

packages.name: smwblocks-wario-dash-breakable-block
packages.title: Wario Dash Breakable Block
packages.description:
A block which only shatters when the player is performing the Wario Dash into them. To be used in conjunction with the Wario Dash uberASM

Requested by Galactic Spear.

Credit is always appreciated.

packages.name: smwblocks-warp-block-pack
packages.title: Warp Block Pack
packages.description:
This pack contains blocks that warp you to a certain level - you can define them yourself in the .asm file - depending on either the 1s or 10s of the coin counter, or the 1s, 10s or 100s of the timer. For each of these, there is a version for a teleport block, pipe block and door block.
Credit not needed.

packages.name: smwblocks-warp-with-message-change-block
packages.title: Warp With Message Change Block
packages.description:
A modified version of Maxx's Teleport Block. It works the same, but it also changes the current msg settings to match. Works correctly if the level destination can be mapped to the overworld. Primary screen exits only.

Fixed so that it works better with vertical levels.

packages.name: smwblocks-water-level-block
packages.title: Water Level Block
packages.description: These blocks enable or disable water level flag and sprite buoyancy.

packages.name: smwblocks-water-level-ice-level-block
packages.title: Water Level/Ice Level Block
packages.description:
This block will change your level into either an ice level or a water level, depending on the ON/OFF Switch. If the switch is "ON", your level becomes an ice level. If the switch is "OFF", your level becomes a water level. This block will also enable sprite buoyancy for water level and disable it for ice level.

Demonstration Video: https://youtu.be/ecSMalNbYG0

Credit not needed, but appreciated. Just don't claim as your own.

packages.name: smwblocks-wind-blocks
packages.title: Wind blocks
packages.description:
Unlike other blocks in the blocks section, this one is much better:

-No wall-clipping and dying
-regardless of how many collision points is touching each part of the wind block will not "combine" and pushes Mario faster (this happens if you have the block itself increments or decrements Mario's position).

It requires uberasm in order to function.

packages.name: smwblocks-winged-yoshi-area
packages.title: Winged Yoshi Area
packages.description:
My first custom block.
Yoshi gets wings, but only while touching this block.

packages.name: smwblocks-x-up-pack
packages.title: X-Up Pack
packages.description:
A pack of three blocks that add a number of lives to the life counter.

-One spawns a 1-Up mushroom out of a block and changes to the next Map16 tile
-Another simply adds 6 lives and then shatters
-Yet another adds 5 lives by one at a time each and disappears in a glitter.

The amount of lives is adjustable.

packages.name: smwblocks-xy-overworld-position-blocks-version
packages.title: XY Overworld Position Blocks, Version 4
packages.description:
This block sets the player's X and Y position on the overworld, allowing you to warp to a new location after you leave the level.

This update fixes a bug in previous versions that failed to update level names (Thanks, Romi!), adds support for Luigi and gives the option to instantly warp to the overworld.

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-boost-block
packages.title: Yoshi Boost Block
packages.description:
This block will do nothing if the player is alone, but will shoot the player into the air (as in, bounce up, not going to level C8 or 1C8) if he is riding on Yoshi.
ASM is commented and easily customizable with a sound and the boost height!

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-coin-block

This block is a question mark block that contains a Yoshi coin.


v1.0 2019/08/02
submit.

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-color-switch
packages.title: Yoshi color switch
packages.description:
This switch will change yoshi's color when stepped on.

Requested by The Koopa Resistance

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-drums-on-off
packages.title: Yoshi Drums On/Off
packages.description: These blocks enable or disable the "Yoshi Drums" channel when touched.

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-purchase-block-v1
packages.title: Yoshi Purchase Block v1.2
packages.description:
This block allows you to purchase a Yoshi. It can be set up to purchase with either coins, lives, or a hybrid of either (lives if not enough coins, coins if not enough lives). You can also customize the cost for each payment method. Different colour Yoshis, with their respective abilities, can be spawned by changing the block's Y position.

Includes simple, optional ExGFX graphics. Palettes 5, 6 and 7 are suitable for the Green, Yellow and Blue Yoshis. Palette 3 is acceptable for Red Yoshi when set to FG palette 1, though a custom palette that uses pure red would be better. It is up to you to match the block's palette with the Y position you place it at; block colour is not linked to Yoshi colour.

Uses 1 byte of freeram as a flag related to removing baby Yoshi under certain conditions.

Yoshi is a tool to be used and discarded, and so is my block - Credit not necessary (but appreciated).

Update v1.2:
- Fixed a bug with the code that quantizes the block's X position.
- Fixed a bug where a baby Yoshi could be still removed even if the Yoshi spawn failed.
- Removed the egg hatching, since it was limited to certain sprite graphic sets. Yoshi now spawns directly from a puff of smoke, and falls to your feet.
- The block can now be triggered by kicked sprites, both horizontally and vertically.
- Taste the rainbow! The block can now spawn all 4 Yoshi colour types depending on it's Y position.

Update v1.1:
- Added an inverse hybrid method (lives, or coins if not enough lives).
- The coins/lives/hybrid/inverse method the block uses is now determined by the block's X position. You can now use all methods without needing to insert near-duplicates of the block.
- Added a check for a spawned baby Yoshi. Unlike a spawned adult Yoshi which will make the block do nothing, a spawned baby Yoshi will simply be deleted for the block to run.
- Added several other basic block designs to the ExGFX for you to use.

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-s-island-colored-bricks
packages.title: Yoshi's Island Colored Bricks
packages.description:
These blocks are designed to mimic the colored bricks found in Yoshi's Island. (They appear in 4-4, 4-8, and 6-8, as far as I know.) Each color takes a certain number of hits with a thrown sprite to destroy, and they change color when you hit them.

DrAnas update: Converted all blocks to SA-1 and made the tiles and SFX more customizable!

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-s-island-crumbling-block
packages.title: Yoshi's island Crumbling block
packages.description:
this block is Yoshi's island block.
This block breaks down.
Works with cape and sprite.

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-s-stomp-blocks
packages.title: Yoshi's Stomp Blocks
packages.description:
A small set of blocks that can be activated by yoshi's stomp (ground pound):
-A simple breakable block
-A couple inverted ?-blocks

Also compatible with Ground Pound, Yoshi's Stomp Effect.

Credit is optional. Requested by Zuluna.

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-shell-combiner
packages.title: Yoshi Shell Combiner
packages.description:
This block can consume a Yoshi and a shell of any colour, and combine them to produce a Yoshi with the colour of the shell it was fed. It can retain the Yoshi and/or shell it was fed across sublevels, and will only accept the first Yoshi/shell it's given until a Yoshi has been spawned. It will also refuse to spawn a Yoshi if there is already a Yoshi or Baby Yoshi in the level.

Note that it will not work with the special "double hit" green shell (sprite #$DF).

Uses 1 byte of freeram.

Includes an optional exanimated AN2 file and an UberASM to control the exanimation trigger (uses custom trigger 0 by default).

Credit is unnecessary but appreciated.

packages.name: smwblocks-yoshi-state-block
packages.title: Yoshi State Block
packages.description:
This block acts differently for Mario when he is on Yoshi and when he is not. I thought it might be useful as a contraption or level gimmick. Can also be used to de-cheese levels, like by preventing bringing a Yoshi back through a pipe. Includes a function that removes Yoshi if Yoshi is inside the block. By default it acts as a cement block when riding Yoshi, and an air block when not.

This version optimises the code and adds SA-1 support.

packages.description:
This is my third pack of 32x32 sprite graphics! Again, it's a bunch of sprites that have 2 walking frames, ready to reskin pretty much any 32x32 sprite out there. Autisticsceptile requested these as well, using them as graphics for the ultimate noob sprite. I'm gonna list them but you can just look at them below

This tileset works best in a Layer 2 level with the interactive parts on layer 2 with priority off and the foreground on layer 1 with priority on. In the first screenshot and the sample level, the green parts are on Layer 1 and the yellow parts are on layer 2.

If I am missing something or have any more questions/doubts, please leave them in the comment section.

Doesn't use custom palettes; works with vanilla palettes 3, 5, 6 and 7.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser
packages.title: ActRaiser 2 - Lovaous Palace (Exterior)
packages.description:
A very beautiful icy background from ActRaiser 2. A great fit for towns (the background has a town in far distance), ice and / or castle themed levels.

Includes two sample levels. One is the original game tilemap and has background scrolling to NONE, NONE. The other one is an improvised loop I did with the original background, removing part of the land part.

Updated to use the background HDMA. Special thanks to Donut, which coded the effect to be as close as possible to the original. Insert it with the UberASM tool.

Credit would be great, but is optional.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-aitos-act
packages.title: ActRaiser - Aitos (Act 2 ~ Boss Room)
packages.description:
A cave background that contains creepy demon statues, from ActRaiser. Adapted for SMW usage.

A good fit for caves or boss battle arenas.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-bloodpool-act
packages.title: ActRaiser - Bloodpool (Act 1)
packages.description:
The second action stage of Actraiser, a poisonous swamp.

Just like the original game, using parallax scrolling in this background is highly recommended.

UPDATE: Reripped from scratch. Much more accurate to the source material, at the cost of an extra palette row. It's now extremely optimized, having a lot of free space in BG2 now. Palette and map 16 are also better organized. Background loops properly now.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-death-heim-boss-rush
packages.title: ActRaiser - Death Heim (Boss Rush)
packages.description:
One of Death Heim's backgrounds, seen while The Master is refighting the main bosses of the game.

Use it with parallaxing scrolling to make the best use of this background.

The eclipse uses the back area color, so it can be used with layer 3 behind the layer 2.

A good fit for mountain levels.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-death-heim-final-boss
packages.title: ActRaiser - Death Heim (Final Boss)
packages.description:
One of the backgrounds seen during the final level of ActRaiser. The original game uses distortion effects to make it look even more amazing. Should be very easy to loop and adjust.

A good fit for space levels, in general.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-death-heim-stage-cleared
packages.title: ActRaiser - Death Heim (Stage Cleared)
packages.description:
The background seen when you finally clear ActRaiser. Compared to the original game, I took some liberties and lmade it loop, so it can be better used in SMW. The water itself is perfect for parallax scrolling.

A good fit for beach / ocean levels, in general.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-fillmore-act
packages.title: ActRaiser - Fillmore (Act 1)
packages.description:
Part of the forest seen in the first action stage of ActRaiser. The complete tilemap is quite a nightmare to assemble, so I had to adapt it to fit with SMW standards. It's a quite big background, surprisingly.

I added some extra map 16 tiles to help users to vary the background a tiny bit. Its height is easy to adjust and it can even fit vertically scroll enabled levels.

A good fit for forests. Even spooky ones, perhaps.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-font
packages.title: ActRaiser - Font
packages.description:
The font used in ActRaiser.
In the original game, letters have 2 colors, but I also add a version with only one color (because '2 colors' version looks weird with original overworld palettes).

It includes two GFX2A files. I added new characters such as 8, 9, double quotes, which are not in the original gfx (they replace unused tiles), # (not in Act Raiser), and also 'ILLUSI', Yoshi's footprint and 'YELLOW' if needed.

Mod note: for best results, change these colors to make the level names look better.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-kasandora-act
packages.title: ActRaiser - Kasandora (Act 1)
packages.description:
The backgrounds seen in the desertic of Kasandora, from ActRaiser.

There's two versions of the background, which are seen on different parts of the level in the original game. They should be easy to adjust vertically, as well.

The first half uses palette row 3, but only has desert dunes and clouds.

Meanwhile, the second half uses palette rows 0 and 3, but has desert dunes, a big abyss and clouds. More GFX space is used, though.

Pick the one you like more.

A good fit for deserts, in general.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-marahna-act
packages.title: ActRaiser - Marahna (Act 2 ~ Boss Room)
packages.description:
The background seen in the Act 2 of Marahna, from ActRaiser. Adapted and looped for usage in SMW Hacks. It's very simple to adjust the position of each element. Can be looped vertically too, if needed.

Due to it heavily relying in the black color, I've made it use the back area color.

Good fit for temples or castles, in general.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-northwall-acts-1
packages.title: ActRaiser - Northwall (Acts 1 & 2)
packages.description: Background used in the first and second acts of Northwall in ActRaiser. The clouds can be used with parallaxing scrolling,  much like how it's done in the original game.

packages.name: smwgraphics-actraiser-sky-palace
packages.title: ActRaiser - Sky Palace
packages.description:
The sky background that's seen in the Sky Palace menu of the game. Due to how the background is laid out in-game, I did my best to reduce the cutoff a tiny bit, shouldn't be too hard of adjusting, though. Works very well with parallax scrolling.

A good fit for sky levels.

packages.name: smwgraphics-alternate-redrawn-styled-piranha-plant-pack
packages.title: Alternate Redrawn Styled Piranha Plant Pack
packages.description:
Alternate redrawn-style graphics meant for many variations of the well known Piranha Plant enemy which sport a slightly tweaked head and a new stem design.

As a whole, this pack includes new graphics for:
* SMW Vanilla Piranha Plants (sans the propeller stem from the jumping ones).
* Imamelia's Custom Piranha Plant and Venus Fire Trap sprites.
* mikeyk & Davros' Giant Piranha Plant sprites.
* The Biob's Jumping Giant Piranha Plant sprite.
* Koopster's Fat Piranha Plant sprite.
* Dahnamics's Giant Piranha Boss sprite.

There are two different variations for the graphics: one where the Piranha Plants look like in newer games (as in, with red/green heads), and another in which their head is brown-ish and their lips is green/red, which meant to invoke their look from the Super Mario 64 - Mario Party 6 era of games. On a related note, the Venus Fire Trap have two extra variations: one in which their head is dark-brown like the Super Mario 3D Land/World; and another where they blow fire rather than... spew it by opening their mouths.

The palette included covers all the sprites covered in the pack. From those, only the Giant Piranha Boss uses palettes E and F while it's fire projectiles use palette A.

Credit's not required but hugely appreciated nonetheless.

packages.description:
Step right up and behold a true marvel of modern science and evolutionary choices! It's Yoshi, but he's got no arms! That's right, ladies and gents, NO ARMS!

Watch in amazement as he runs, jumps, and flutters using nothing but grit and pure leg power! How does he eat? That's the mystery, friends, that's the magic!

This incredible specimen uses the standard vanilla palette and replaces GFX33. Drop him into your game and give your players a sight they won't soon forget! Get your armless Yoshi today!

packages.name: smwgraphics-arrows-and-item-indicators
packages.title: Arrows and Item Indicators
packages.description:
This is a pack of tiles intended to be used as item indicators. Essentially, they were made as a way to show where the player should throw/drop/use an item.
Think of it as in those kaizo levels where a coin is used to indicate where a shell should be thrown.
It also comes with arrow graphics in all 8 directions and "correct" and "wrong" symbols, so hopefully it can be useful in a variety of situations.

Note: This uses a handful of palette rows to accomodate for the palettes of all different sprites, but uses the right side of them, so the only palette that is overwritten is the Pink Berry's.
If you don't use all indicators, you might not need all the palettes. (The readme contains detailed information on palette usage)

Original description by Skewer - "A city that is on fire, features some ruined buildings with animated fire and an animated Layer3 on fire as well; the fire has subtle animation so as to not pull the eye too much. Commissioned by StrikeForcer for MaGL contest; submitted upon his request."

packages.name: smwgraphics-blues-brothers-electricity
packages.title: Blues Brothers - Electricity
packages.description:
The electric shocks from the Blues Brothers SNES game. Comes with both palettes (the file uses rows 2 and 3), a Map16 file, a YY-CHR graphics file, and a sample level with ExAnimation inserted. The tiles are currently treated as black piranha plant tiles, but you'll be able to make them into whatever you want, like maybe a custom block that instantly kills the player, just like the electricity from the Blues Brothers game.

The game itself is said to be bad and of course has nothing to do with the original 1980 R-rated movie, but in my opinion, the graphics look great. Hopefully, we can get some more graphic rips from this game in the future.

This didn't take much effort, so giving credit to me is an option, especially since I'm a skeptic and anticipate that you might not anyway.

packages.name: smwgraphics-chocobo
packages.title: Chocobo
packages.description:
The Chocobo is a large, (usually) flightless bird from the Final Fantasy series that comes in many colors, famously yellow. I drew this Super Mario World-styled as a Yoshi replacement - it replaces Yoshi eggs and Yoshi-related signage as well. It does not require a custom palette. The hex edit needed to fix the lower half of the overworld sprite's palette is included for convenience, but can also be referenced in the ROM map. The tail feathers aren't so large and upright like much of the source series's material, but since this is within Yoshi's native framework, I'm not sure I can pull that off except with the credit Yoshies.

Anyone is welcome to expand or improve upon it and submit updates or variants without my permission.

packages.name: smwgraphics-chrono-trigger-death-peak-mountains
packages.title: Chrono Trigger - Death Peak (Mountains)
packages.description:
A background seen while climbing the Death Peak, from Chrono Trigger. Unlike Denadoro variant, this one has some different details, like ruins of civilization nearby in the horizon. A good fit for snow or mountainous levels, in general.

Background scrolling must be disabled.

Credit would be great, but it is optional.

packages.name: smwgraphics-chrono-trigger-death-peak-sky
packages.title: Chrono Trigger - Death Peak (Sky)
packages.description:
The gorgeous background that appears in the summit the Death Peak, from Chrono Trigger. Could be used for a cutscene, boss arena or maybe, a title screen. It will get odd if looped, so it's recommended to use only for one screen.

UPDATE: Optimized gfx files, map 16 and palette, in general. For the red variant, at least.

Added another variant, which is a blue sky, seen when Crono is revived. Both of them have the eclipse area using the back area color.

The blue variant uses a bit more tiles, due to slightly different tiles near the bottom.

Credit would be great, but is optional.

packages.name: smwgraphics-chrono-trigger-flea-battle
packages.title: Chrono Trigger - Flea Battle
packages.description:
This is the background of the Flea battle from Chrono Trigger. Pretty small and simple background, nice for space levels, I think.
ExGFX104 -> BG1

Credit is not needed.

packages.title: Chrono Trigger - Font

packages.name: smwgraphics-chrono-trigger-giga-gaia

packages.description: The gorgeous set of the Giga Gaia boss fight from Chrono Trigger. Good for boss battles or cutscenes.

packages.name: smwgraphics-chrono-trigger-guardia-castle-outside
packages.title: Chrono Trigger - Guardia Castle (Outside)
packages.description:
A very nice background from the outside of the Guardia Castle in Chrono Trigger, one of my favorites RPG.

Note: The background scrolling must be disabled.

Update: Fixed background like in the Chrono Trigger original game.

packages.name: smwgraphics-chrono-trigger-moon
packages.title: Chrono Trigger - Moon
packages.description: The moon, used in a cutscene in Chrono Trigger. Could be used in night levels.

packages.name: smwgraphics-chrono-trigger-prehistoric-mountains
packages.title: Chrono Trigger - Prehistoric Mountains
packages.description: A cool background from Chrono Trigger that can be used in mountainous levels.

packages.name: smwgraphics-chrono-trigger-zenan-bridge
packages.title: Chrono Trigger - Zenan Bridge
packages.description:
An ocean-view Background that appears in various places (but most notably, the Zenan Bridge) from Chrono Trigger. There's three variations of this Background, being them:

Zenan Bridge
North Cape/West Cape (West Cape's the same of the North Cape, but with the Zenan Bridge colors)
Dactyl Nest (I've changed a little and added some more clouds to fill the BG empty spaces).

Both North Cape and Dactyl Nest doesn't have Horizontal Scroll.

There's also an alternative palette of the Sea from Zenan Bridge seen on the Tidal Wave cutscene's Palette Row.

Originally Requested by isaix.

packages.title: Chuck Rock - Cave
packages.description:

The palette the colors from the Chuckya are on is palette B.

No credit needed though you might want to credit "mirror" whose spritesheet I based the graphics off.

packages.name: smwgraphics-city

A custom city foreground. Can be used for urban themed levels.

Give credit if you feel like it, but don't claim it as your own. I'm watching you.

This is some buildings GFX I drew in my spare time. Please give credit if used, because this took a while to make :P

Enjoy!

packages.name: smwgraphics-city-panorama

packages.description: It´s an original background made be me. There is palette for normal, night, red painted houses, chocolate and snow. You don´t need to give credit, but it would be nice.

packages.name: smwgraphics-city-park
packages.title: City Park
packages.description: My entry to the 2014 Summer ExGFX Contest. Credit is not necessary, but would be appreciated.

packages.name: smwgraphics-city-town
packages.title: City/Town
packages.description: A simple city/town set with ground, buildings you can stand on top of, streetlights, and doors that can either be closed or open.  This would be great for hub worlds in more RPG-styled hacks.

packages.name: smwgraphics-cityscape
packages.title: Cityscape
packages.description: Autisticsceptile1993 suggested that I make a cityscape background, so I did.  This background is highly versatile in how the buildings can be arranged.

packages.name: smwgraphics-clarence-s-big-chance-generic-company
packages.title: Clarence's Big Chance - Generic Company
packages.description:
Graphics from stage 3 of the titular flash game. I decided to rip this because I've only found one other office-themed submission. Usable for offices and skyscrapers.

Note: Meant to be used with a Layer 2 level.

Credit not needed.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-athletic
packages.title: Classic Athletic 2021
packages.description: Here's an athletic grassland set mostly inspired by SMB3.  It requires no custom palette and looks best with FG Palette 6.  Palette 5 might also look good if you want to use this in an ice world, but don't use the red Mushroom Platform if you do that.  Vanilla Line Guides are also included so you can use line-guided sprites with this.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-beach
packages.title: Classic Beach 2021
packages.description: This tropical tileset includes plenty of beach-themed setpieces and uses vanilla Palette 0.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-bonus
packages.title: Classic Bonus
packages.description: Classic Foreground #14 is a colorful tileset perfect for bonus rooms or Switch Palaces.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-candy-clouds
packages.title: Classic Candy Clouds
packages.description: Here's a sweet candy/cloud tileset that uses vanilla Palette 5.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-castle
packages.title: Classic Castle 2021
packages.description:
Here's a fully-loaded castle set with climbing nets, Bowser banners, spikes, skewers, and ExAnimated Amps that can either act like Munchers, turning into coins with a Silver P-Switch, or be used with ON/OFF hurt blocks from this pack.It might also be a good idea to use these for the spikes if you're using them in the same room as the Muncher Amps.

I've also included an alternate GFX03 that replaces the moving castle block sprite graphics with some that better match this tileset. Neither of these need custom palettes.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-cave
packages.title: Classic Cave 2021
packages.description: This is a fairly versatile general-purpose cave set that requires no custom palettes.  It looks best with Palettes 3, 5, and 7.  Palette 4 will also work, but you probably shouldn't use the crystals that use Palette Row 3 unless you want brown crystals.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-crystal-cave
packages.title: Classic Crystal Cave
packages.description: Here's a crystalline cave FG built around FG Palette 06.  05 will also work if you want an icier look.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-desert
packages.title: Classic Desert 2021
packages.description:
Here's a desert tileset that includes SMB2-style pots, cacti based on the Pokey sprite, and several pieces that can be used with custom blocks. These include:
* Animated Quicksand
* SMB2-Style diggable sand
* Cracked Stone Block

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-factory
packages.title: Classic Factory 2021
packages.description: Here's a factory background based on FG Palette 2 (4 and 7 will also look pretty decent).  The electric barriers do nothing by default, but feel free to use some custom hurt blocks with them.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-forest
packages.title: Classic Forest 2021
packages.description: Here's a lush forest foreground based on vanilla Palette 0.  It doesn't need a custom palette, but I included an optional autumn-themed palette in case you want to do an autumn forest stage.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-forest-temple
packages.title: Classic Forest Temple 2021
packages.description: Here's a forest/jungle temple set with a bit of Dino-Rhino theming.  The open-mouthed statues could be used with a one-way sprite shooter if desired.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-futuristic-highway
packages.title: Classic Futuristic Highway
packages.description: Here's a Sonic-inspired futuristic city/highway set based on FG Palette 2.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-ghost-house
packages.title: Classic Ghost House 2021
packages.description: Here's a spooky ghost house tileset based on vanilla FG Palette 4.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-goomba
packages.title: Classic Goomba
packages.description:
A simple set of graphics that replaces SMW's spherical Goombas with hand-drawn ones that more closely resemble their normal counterparts.

Replaces SP2. No custom palette or credit needed.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-goombas
packages.title: Classic Goombas
packages.description: Here are some hand-drawn graphics to make your Goombas look more like actual Goombas.  The .zip includes graphics for the Goomba itself, its squished frame for those who wish to do the Tweaker/hex edit combo that turns SMW Goombas fully classic, and the frames for the Para-Goomba.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-grassland
packages.title: Classic Grassland 2021
packages.description: This grassland was inspired by one of the fill patterns in Paint.net.  I used said pattern as a base for the dirt pattern here.  Everything else was drawn from scratch.  Like every set I've made with "Classic" in its name, this doesn't require a custom palette and is based on vanilla FG Palette 0.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-graveyard
packages.title: Classic Graveyard
packages.description: I've been meaning to submit a graveyard set like this since 2011, but kept putting it off.  Oh well...Here it is now!  Like all my Classic foregrounds, this set is compatible with a vanilla palette.  In this case, said palette is FG Palette 0.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-ice
packages.title: Classic Ice 2021 Plus
packages.description:
This package not only contains an ice/snow tileset in the style of the rest of my "Classic 2021" sets, but also a bonus file with graphics for snow-covered pipes and various frozen items, the latter of which can be used with Ersanio's Ice Block pack. The base tileset requires no custom palette, but the snowy pipes and frozen items do. The pipes and blocks are in a separate .map16 file in case you just want to use them.

The frozen itmes included are:
* Frozen Coin
* Frozen Muncher
* Frozen Yoshi Coin
* Frozen Springboard
* Frozen Key
* Frozen Keyhole
* Frozen P-Switch

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-ice-athletic
packages.title: Classic Ice Athletic 2021 + Snowman Pokey
packages.description: Here's an icy athletic set that uses vanilla palettes and includes line guides for line-guided sprites.  I also included graphics to turn Pokey into a snowman.  The snowman Pokey graphics do require a custom palette.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-ice-cave
packages.title: Classic Ice Cave 2021
packages.description: Here's a cool icy cave set that uses FG Palette 5.  It includes some decorative crystals and flashing Christmas lights to hang on the ceiling.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-ice-crystal-cave
packages.title: Classic Ice Crystal Cave
packages.description: This icy crystalline cave set uses vanilla Palette 5 and contains plenty of ice and crystal-themed setpieces.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-jungle
packages.title: Classic Jungle 2021
packages.description: Here's a jungle tileset based on FG Palette 00.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-lava-cave
packages.title: Classic Lava Cave 2021
packages.description: Here's a fiery cave tileset with lots of bones and animated lava flows.  It looks best with FG Palette 7, but 3 could also work.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-moon
packages.title: Classic Moon 2021
packages.description: This lunar tileset is compatible with FG palettes 3, 4, 5, and 7.  It even includes evil stars a la Super Mario Land 2's Space Zone.  They turn into coins with a Silver P-Switch.  If using both the stars and standard spikes in the same level, it's best to use a custom hurt block with the latter.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-mountain
packages.title: Classic Mountain 2021
packages.description: This mountain tileset features pine trees, bridges, and even railroad tracks.  It looks best with FG Palettes 3, 4, and 7.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-ocean
packages.title: Classic Ocean 2021
packages.description:
This underwater set includes half-buried decorative Koopa Shells, animated seaweed, some shipwreck bits, and Jelectros that, by default, are set to turn into coins when a Silver P-Switch is pressed.

The treasure chests can even be used with a custom block like this.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-overgrown-ruins
packages.title: Classic Overgrown Ruins
packages.description: Here's a ruins/temple tileset that's teeming with greenery and flowers.  It's compatible with Palette 0.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-pyramid
packages.title: Classic Pyramid 2021
packages.description: Here's a desert pyramid set based on vanilla Palette 4. It features some of the same setpieces from my latest desert tileset, so you can use many of the same blocks. It also uses the same ExAnimation file.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-ruins
packages.title: Classic Ruins
packages.description: Here's #11 in the Classic Foregrounds series, a ruins/temple set with some Muncher flair.  This set works with vanilla palettes 3, 4, and 7.  Palette 5 MIGHT be good if you're doing an ice temple.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-sewer
packages.title: Classic Sewer 2021
packages.description: Here's a slimy, stinky sewer set based on FG Palette 1.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-ship
packages.title: Classic Ship 2021
packages.description: Here's a ship tileset based on FG Palette 4 that includes pieces for both Koopa Airships and pirate ships.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-sky
packages.title: Classic Sky 2021
packages.description: Here's a sky tileset that works with almost every vanilla.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-snake-temple
packages.title: Classic Snake Temple
packages.description: Here's a pyramid/temple with a slight snake motif in the statues and torch sconces.  This is compatible with Palette 4, but might also look good with Palette 7 for a night theme.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-swamp
packages.title: Classic Swamp 2021
packages.description: Here is a swamp tileset based on FG Palette 1.  It might be Shrek's, but it probably isn't.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-water
packages.title: Classic Water 2
packages.description: This soggy set contains everything you need to build a typical water level, including corals, seaweed, blocks, and decorative oysters.  It even includes a couple treasure chests, and the small ones could be used with sprite-spawning custom blocks to hide power-ups.  This tileset is compatible with vanilla palettes and looks best with Palettes 1, 3, 4, and 7.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-wham-bam-ruins
packages.title: Classic Wham Bam Ruins
packages.description:
Despite the name, this tileset draws most of its inspiration from Sonic 1's Labyrinth Zone. The Wham Bam part comes from the Wham Bam Rock graphic on one of the setpieces. This set requires no custom palette and will look best with vanilla palettes 3, 4, and 7.

UPDATE: I updated the Wham Bam Rock carvings to look more like his less-controversial Super Star Ultra design.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classic-wood-castle
packages.title: Classic Wood Castle
packages.description: This is an expanded version of the wooden castle foreground seen in Mega Rex's Castle in Super Mario Outbreak.  It uses vanilla palette 4 and is perfect for tree fort levels.

packages.name: smwgraphics-classy-airship
packages.title: Classy Airship
packages.description: An Airship with a Classy air in it, enjoy it.

packages.description:

The Mountain with Forest background from "Claymates" SNES game.

What do you think about this?

packages.name: smwgraphics-clear-pipes
packages.title: Clear Pipes
packages.description:
Pipes that are transparent, Super Mario 3D World style. Can be used for decoration, or as screen scrolling pipes (necessitates the SMB3 Screen Scrolling Pipes patch).

They use background palette 0 by default, as this is how they fit best in a vanilla SMW environment, but implementing a custom palette shouldn't be too hard.

See the readme file on how to use in conjunction with the SSP patch.

It's a BG, with clouds, and fluffyness! All info is included in the filenames, so have fun!

Circus clowns that serve as a replacement for Koopas.

packages.title: Conker Reloaded - Tediz
packages.description:
The Tediz from Conker, in their Live and Reloaded incarnation, I was about to make it a custom sprite, that shoots bullets, throws greneades and stuff, but since I can't code and program ASM, I just made it as Koopa replacement. Feel free to edit it as an ASM if you like.

packages.name: smwgraphics-construction-factory

packages.description:
This is my very first ExGFX I have ever made! I'm proud of my accomplishment :). But anyways,

packages.name: smwgraphics-construction-site
packages.title: Construction Site
packages.description: Here's a construction site set, just in case you want to pay homage to the original Donkey Kong arcade game or just have a level set in a construction site.

packages.name: smwgraphics-contra-hard-corps-base
packages.title: Contra: Hard Corps - Base
packages.description:

Updated By: S.R.H.

packages.name: smwgraphics-contra-hard-corps-highway

Do note that this submission doesn't include Rex, Mega Mole, Rainy Turtloid (Mega Man X6) and Goradus (Popful Mail (Super Famicom)). They are just used here to show how this simple info box graphic can be used.

packages.description:

If you set the define at the top of roto_disc.asm to !PaletteRotate = 1, then use PaletteRotate1.pal. This uses colors 3-5 on palettes 9-F, and it produces a slight shimmer on the border of the sprite.

If you set it palette rotate to 0, use PaletteRotate0.pal. The sprite will be a solid color, and by default it will use palette B.

Other names for this sprite: disco waffle, death waffle, atomic waffle

Also: they're square. Amazing.

Moderator's note: it's already mentioned in the readme, but to clarify it further: the included ExGFX change the 8x8 tiles used by the vanilla Layer 1 tiles. If you only insert and load the ExGFX and palette files, your Overworld will be filled with garbage tiles due to the new graphics affecting the default Layer 1 tile, which in vanilla was completely transparent. To address this, you have to, in Layer 2 8x8 Editor Mode, copy the new 8x8 Layer 1 tiles (found below the submaps) from the sample BPS's Overworld to the same location within your Overworld, so your Layer 1 tiles will use those instead.

packages.name: smwgraphics-earthworm-jim-snes-what-the-heck
packages.title: Earthworm Jim (SNES) - What the Heck?
packages.description:
Now it's the SNES version of Earthworm Jim - What the Heck, along with its layer 3. I had to fight 2 thingw here: one is frame 'fighting' of Evil the Cat and two is layer 3 management. After overcoming the challenges, I can say the backgrounds are done. In the original, the scrolling was slow, so you must find a way to set scrolling to slow or set it to none. If you check the in-game screenshot, you'll see that layer 3, while vanishing thanks to Remove Status Bar patch, is weirdly placed in front of layer 2. There's an explanation here. In the SNES EJ, the moon thing was placed behind the transparent layer 2, while the layer 3, being transparent at the bottom was in front of the BG and auto-scrolled. It's possible to simulate this in SMW, but you must be careful. Features:

-you can view the sample level to see how both the BG and layer 3 are set up.
-the palette is weirdly placed. It uses palettes 3, 5 and little bit of palette 1. Speaking of palette 1:
-it only uses 2 colors and placed those colors at layer 3 pslette 6 and 7. Those are the transparent colors, unaffecting SMW colors.
-layer 3 colors are easy to edit. Those don't affect SMW colors. It uses layer 3 palettes 3, 4 and 5.
-Bonus: Evil the Cat animates. Since I wasn't sure where the animations were, I decided to use the Genesis version and recolored tiles, so that it matches the SNES version and turned out good. Check the 1st picture.
-layer 2 can be 512x512 if so desired.
-layer 2 uses 402 9x9 tiles. It overwrites BG1, BG2, BG3 and a bit of FG1. You can't use bushes.
-BG uses 372 Map16 tiles. It almost overwrites 1 Map16 page and a half.
-layer 3 uses 384 tiles. You'd think it uses 3 ExGFX files, which is alraady a lot, but no, it uses 4 in total. I had to avoid tile FC here. It's 256x256 and you need DKCR Sprite Status Bar or Minimalist Status Bars patches.

You ca say it was version 1.0 above.

Version 1.12:
-fixed one of the blue eyes in one of Evil the Cat's animations. Now it's good.
-added transluscent fog to layer 3, which is better now.
-set both layer 2 and layer 3 X and Y scrolling to none for best results.
-extended the fog for layer 3. Anorakun said it cuts off.

BG2 sheet contains the basic English alphabets and sentence symbols, and BG3 contains the rest. If you're short on the space and want to only use English, you can omit BG3.

This font uses 3 monochrome colors, which are mapped to the same ones of "FG Palette 0" on Row 3. If you used the same palette set, they'll look fine.

packages.description:
The background seen in various sections of Aquann Castle and also seen in one of the final levels of the game.

MASSIVE UPDATE: Optimized GFX files, better map 16 organization, saner palette organization and now includes an extra variant.

Due to the purple variant using much more colors, they use different map 16 files and palette.

Aquann Castle: palette rows 0 and 3.
Aquann Tower: palette rows 3 and 5.

Bundled with this submission is two parallaxing codes, meant to be inserted with UberASM Tool 2.1. Pick the one you need the most.

Please check the readme included to know what's the difference between these two uberasm files.

A good fit for cave levels.

Another one of the backgrounds used in the Aquann Castle,from Ganbare Goemon 4. This one in particular is used in a shooting gallery, where Yae must used the enemy shooter to destroy some targets, so she can proceed even further in this bizarre place. The beautiful background that appears in the stages 1 and 4 of Planet Aquann, from Ganbare Goemon Kirakira Dōchū: Boku ga Dancer ni Natta Wake, lit. "Under The Road - Why I became a dancer". Use it for water levels or levels with a japanese vibe. The original game doesn't have aquatic sections in the levels that use it, so use your creativity how you'll use this background.

Includes two HDMA: one used in Saqqas Forest (Planet Aquann stage 1) and another one used in Bungee Ridge (Planet Aquann stage 4). I did my best to align the HDMA with the backgrounds.

This background uses two entire palette rows, and the last 3 colors from palette 6.

An underwater stage of Planet Impact, from Ganbare Goemon 4. It's an aquatic stage where Yae must cross a coral reef that has tons of dangers like spikes, scuba divers and nasty water currents. Credit would be great, but is optional.

Initially, I thought Touhou Koumakyou ~ The Embodiment of Scarlet Devil - Spellcard (Remilia Scarlet) was a very hard BG to rip, but I was wrong. The BG from Garfield and His Nine Lives (GBA) Arnbuckle Farm was worse. In this case, I wasn't able to erase many BG tiles for room. There was another thing I could do for tile reduction: flipping tiles. I flipped only the X-position of tiles for free space. You can see that in the background screenshot. Ripped the BG with the Lunar Magic Bitmap Pasting feature and I really had to play with few colors, in order for the blue color to be the back area color. I also salvaged a free color in palette 5.
Edit: Corrected the file name.

WARINING: NEARLY EVERY TILE FROM FG2 HAS BEEN REMOVED. ONLY FEW CAN BE USED.

packages.name: smwgraphics-gijinka-hammer-bro

A gijinka Hammer Bro. If you don't know what gijinka means, it's when a non-human character gets turned into one

This updated submission is meant to be used with Sonikku's Hammer Bro sprite. The files you'll find there are already included in this submission!!! I'm linking his work to give proper credit and so you know where to find extra info.


I needed to include the sprite's files here because I had to edit the sprite's tilemap and the "held" position of the hammer (in HammerBro.asm) as well as the palette to green (in HammerBro.cfg & .json). Aside from the .bin file, the rest of the files Sonikku provides are unmodified but they're still included here for convenience. Gloomy told me all this was justified and okay to do

Note: if you look at the GFX file, you'll notice there seems to be some regular bro tiles still. These belong to the Fire Bro, another sprite by Sonikku which uses these tiles only. These custom sprite graphics were included in the Hammer Bro's original .bin file. If you're new, know that you can just copy/paste my graphics into your own exGFX file, just make sure they're laid out the same! That is what we call "tileset mixing" my friend

packages.name: smwgraphics-gokujou-parodius-snes-cat-battleship-forever
packages.title: Gokujou Parodius (SNES) - Cat Battleship Forever
packages.description:
I decided to combine the 2 BGs into 1. I did make a few improvements. Made the clouds and the island use the back area color, along with the high clouds. If you do change it, then make sure you change the underwater colors, too. One of the palettes fits well palette 1, so I moved it there without affecting SMW colors. The Map16 tiles have been improved as well.

Update: I ripped the BG again.
I merged the BG seen above and underwater into one. It does use a lot of tiles but I classify this as complete. A tile is used from the FG1 slot. I also:
-Updated the palettes. Clouds use palette 0 without affecting SMW palette, palette 3 is used for the ground underwater and ship+defeated penguin boss, palette 4 is used for the sand below and palette 6 is used for the islands. Uses the 2nd half of those palettes;
-Map16 went through its overhaul. I drew 2 new tiles for the underwater transition and added a few extra tiles for the islands and the small cloud;
-The octopus cloud was added as well.
You should use the BG according to the horizontal level settings from the sample level.

No credit needed. This did took some time.

packages.name: smwgraphics-gokujou-parodius-snes-circo-porto-harborland
packages.title: Gokujou Parodius (SNES) - Circo Porto Harborland
packages.description:
The backgrounds seen in the first stage of Gokujou Parodius.

Includes two versions:
- First Half: it has the Circo Porto Harborland logo, the city at the background has an amusement park. It uses BG1, BG2 and BG3 slots and the palette rows 0, 3, 5 and 7. Heavy palette and graphic usage, even though there's a lot of space in BG3.

- Second Half: doesn't have the logo, the pillars have a beginning / end and the city is less varied. This version is the more recommended one to use. Uses only the BG1 slot and palette rows 3, 5, and 7.

Both versions can be used with the HDMA gradient file included in the zip file. Apply it with UberASM Tool.

Pick the version you're the most comfortable to use. Compared to the site version, my version (second half version) is much more optimized and accurate to the source material, along with better palette management.

"The name of this stage, "Circo Porto", originates from Konami's former chain of arcade and entertainment facilities in the early nineties."

A good fit for carnivals or cities.

Custom or Rip?: Custom;
Slot(s) Used?: BG1;
Palette(s): Palettes 00 and 03 (the status bar palette is NOT affected by palette 00);

I actually made this background for a side hack of mine, which is temporarely frozen, but it turned out so well that I decided to submit it to SMWC, so that everybody can use it. This BG would fit nicely in snowy/cold levels, however, they would fit in quite some other environments as well, if you tweak its palette a little bit. Sample level, palette, Map16Page file are included within the .zip file, and I highly recommend reading the readme included along with those files.

Credit is not necessary, but would be nice. Enjoy!

packages.name: smwgraphics-jikkyou-oshaberi-parodius-psx-boss-rush-first-and-second-bosses
packages.title: Jikkyou Oshaberi Parodius (PSX) - Boss Rush (First and Second Bosses)
packages.description:
You know how High Speed Patrol (Train Area) was the second worst and High Speed Patrol (Factory) was the first when it comes to adding it into LM with somewhat of an success? Now everything has changed as this BG of mine that comes from the Boss Rush section of JOP is now the absolute worst. First of all, I had to use 2 savestates for this BG, even though we know the BG is longer than it should be. It wasn't bad, but now comes palette management... oh boy. This BG did give me a great headache as not only I had to use many colors, but I had to use the Hue-Tolerance feature from the Lunar Magic Bitmap Pasting Tool. Even if I did manage to get a good BG results, some tiles had bad colors. I had to correct it until it looked decent and used a palette for the upper part of the observatory tower. The archive includes an HDMA effect made with EffecTool. You can also edit the back area color anyway you like. You can use the BG according to the screenshots.

Uses the second half of palette rows 4 and 6.

Credit not needed.

The background seen while you fight Goemon's Compact, in the PSX version of Jikkyou Oshaberi Parodius. Compared to the original version, i had to sacrifice a fair amount of details. packages.title: Mario Bros. - Phases 10+
packages.description:
The background from phases 10 and above from Mario Bros. on the GBA (Included in the Mario Advance series and Mario and Luigi: Superstar Saga), as well as being used in the bonus stages. It even has the animated snow graphics falling in the background!
Since there was no available rip of it, I decided to rip it myself. packages.name: smwgraphics-mars-bars
packages.title: Mars Bars
packages.description:
This is the second edition of the connected brown blocks I and others have adopted as a death block standard in recent years, a muncher-equivalent block free from both the limitations of munchers and the dullness of tiled anons.

This time, after years of avoiding it, I finally went through the trouble of adding extra tiles to round the funny looking inner corners. This is not the first time I’ve attempted this and I would describe it as an encyclopedic and pointless task but I’m pretty sure I’ve covered every possible configuration where there would otherwise be a little cutoff. It’s (slightly) more work to decorate this way, but for anyone who really cares about the details, these should look (slightly) nicer than the originals.

It’s recommended to use these with dacin’s muncher-size hurt/kill block to prevent breaks with powerups or silver p-switches.

They use 28 tiles in BG3 and the right side of the palette row. The test level provides anon-style example palettes with gray and red outline animations for hurt and kill respectively, but I encourage you to color them however you see fit.

packages.name: smwgraphics-meatland
packages.title: Meatland
packages.description:
A meaty tileset that can be useful for any sort of fleshy atmosphere. Whether it be some sort of cave or inside of an actual living organism, we got you covered! Contains a FG and a layer 3 BG.

It's probably best to use a sprite status bar or some sort of status bar patch to make sure the top of the BG does not get cutoff.

Whoever suggested I make this, I'll be watching you :^)

Edit: When using the layer 3 bg, it looks best setting h-scroll to none. It's meant to be sort of a corridor so looping it will look a little strange. But it's totally up to you.

packages.name: smwgraphics-meaty-powerups
packages.title: Meaty Powerups
packages.description:
Tired of SMW original powerups? So you can take a look at this stuff with meaty powerups replacing mushroom, 1-up, fire flower, cape and star.

This pack contains a meat for mushroom and 1-up, a chicken leg for fire flower, a fried egg for star and a fish for cape.

Also changes fireballs to chicken legs.

It uses original sprite palette.

NOTE: You may want to apply the patches in the .zip, which will fix some graphical and sense issues from SMW powerups system when using custom graphics for powerups like this.

packages.name: smwgraphics-metroid-brinstar
packages.title: Metroid - Brinstar
packages.description:
A complete rip of the first area from the original Metroid. Everything from the original game should be accounted for.

Some notes:
-The cracked blocks and Item Spheres require a custom block that can be broken with projectiles. Such a block can easily be made using Blockreactor
-There are two different backs for the Chozo Statues, one of which is solid while the other is not. Only use the solid backside when the Chozo Statue is facing against a wall.
-The Zeb pipes and the tops of Chozo Statues are passthrough unlike the original game due to the lack of any kind of slab blocks, both in the vanilla SMW and in the Blocks section.
-The only used vanilla colors that are overwritten are the berry colors. No other non-blank colors are affected.

Credit to Mica for ripping the original tiles on TSR that I used as reference.

packages.name: smwgraphics-my-little-pony-friendship-is-magic-spike-the-dragon
packages.title: My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic - Spike the Dragon
packages.description:
Hello, in July 2018, someone requested me to draw player graphics for Spike the Dragon from My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic. So I, DPBOX, worked with an artist, Mares-a-Mares, and, after almost a year of work, the graphics are complete, and here they are. I managed and Mares-a-Mares drew.

While most of these poses are original, like, 1 or 2 were ripped from My Little Pony: Rise of the Clockwork Stallions DX: Director's Cut https://www.dropbox.com/s/vcms2adkkqw3geu/My%20Little%20Pony%20Fan%20Games.zip?dl=0 and weren't changed, like, 4 more were ripped then modified slightly, but the rest are original, but either they started from the poses in that game then were heavily modified or were drawn completely from the ground up. All of the poses are based on that game's poses and use that game's style.

Please be aware that this is not a simple graphics swap. Some patches are needed. Everything you need to know to get these player graphics working is in the Read Me.

Credit goes to ExE Boss, Ladida, Neosz, and KilloZapit because the player requires some patches they made as well as yoshifanatic for helping me with some coding related things.

ATTENTION: Due to the fact that some of the patches required for these player graphics to work have been updated after I submitted this, I updated the Read Me. The Read Me is the only thing that was changed in this update, so if you downloaded this before, you don't need to download it again.

versions.title: My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic - Spike the Dragon

packages.description:
I ripped this from a demo called 'New Demo' made by a demo group called NESQuik(not to be confused with the milk brand).

This part was specifically ripped from the portion of the demo with a raster effect that repeats 1 scanline across the whole screen, and then changes the vertical position of the background within the scanline to make it look like parallax scrolling due to how the graphics look.

To apply the effect, add the included ASM through UberASM to a level using this background.

Here is video showing the code.

Alternatives to the default icegoom Redrawn Mario overworld sprite graphic as I found that to be generally unreadable. So I made my own in 2019, tho I did some touch-ups since then.

Extract this for your GFX10 file to use.

Note that this is designed for a single-player hack. As such, there is a file for having Mario as the player, and another for having Luigi as the player.

This is designed to be used with the overworld sprites from icegoom's Redrawn SMW graphics hack, which can be found here: https://www.smwcentral.net/?a=details&id=5914&p=section

packages.name: smwgraphics-paper-mario-the-thousand-year-door-vivian
packages.title: Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year-Door - Vivian
packages.description:
A complete set of player replacement graphics. Vivian from Paper Mario: The
Thousand-Year Door. Includes frames for cape, overworld, castle animations
and blushing. I drew these myself from scratch.

Should preserve the switch block and Yoshi palettes correctly.

Use Lunar Magic's "Insert Shared Palettes to ROM..." to insert the shared
palette. This will overwrite the entire shared palette in the ROM. If you
don't want to do that, you can instead use Player_Palette_Patch.asm with an
ASM patcher such as Asar. The patch will overwrite only the player portions
of the shared palette.

If you're using Lunar Magic's custom palettes on the overworld, the custom
palette will override the shared palette, causing Vivian to appear in the
wrong colours. You can use "Import to current overworld submap palette from
file" with Overworld_palette.pal to update the player colours in your
custom palette. Make sure Overworld_palette.palmask is in the same directory
when you do this.

When walking left on the overworld, part of the Yoshi will flash red instead
of green (or whatever colour the Yoshi is supposed to be). Normally this is
hard to see because the parts affected are mostly obscured by Mario, save for
a few pixels. This is because some of the tile data was incorrectly marked to
use Mario's palette. However, since Vivian doesn't have feet, you can see
more of Yoshi and it's quite distracting. You may want to apply the included
patch "Yoshi_Overworld_Fix.asm" using Asar to fix it.

With great thanks to @mm102_ for the template and player exporter.[1]

I would love to know what you use this in! Find me on Twitter. Credit is
greatly appreciated.

Twitter: https://www.twitter.com/weeble
Twitch: https://www.twitch.tv/clockworknettie

Version history

1.0.0 - First release

[1]: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t7qfZgj8nnc&t=0s

Note: This tileset comes with a background which is meant to go with this foreground tileset to create a neat parallax scrolling effect when layer 2 horizontal scrolling is set to anything besides constant. Layer 2 vertical scrolling should be set to constant so that the background will always appear at the correct height.

Note: Graphics file 9B only contains the graphics for the giant "Welcome!" sign, making it optional if you want to use it or not. Which is good, because you can't use the original SMW's goal point in any area that uses that sign since most of the tiles found in FG2 get overwritten by the sign graphics, including the goal graphics. packages.name: smwgraphics-readable-gothic-font
packages.title: Readable Gothic Font
packages.description:
Unlike the other generally stylized Blackletter gothic fonts I either create myself or on the rare occasion that I rip fonts from other video games such as Bloodstained - Curse of the Moon, this one goes into the former category of it being a font I made myself for a now-scrapped CLDC 2020 level entry that I couldn't finish in time that prioritizes readability over stylization, similar to how Pix3M did his Alagard font that I took heavy inspiration from to make this font.

There were minor touchups from the 2020 version as seen in the video linked on a few characters, mainly for readability purposes.

You are free to use this in whatever game or hack project(s) you have in mind, as long as you do credit me in your projects. To use this font in SMW, replace GFX2A in the Graphics folder with the downloaded font.

2022 UPDATE - Updated various letters upon seeing various Let's Plays and Twitch Streams of hacks that used this font, as there were certain letters that needed to be addressed further for readability's sake. depreciated.bin shows you the various alternative versions as well as the letters from the initial release that have been replaced.

This is a selective collection of the English alphabet fonts used in SNK fighting game Real Bout Fatal Fury. It is sized 8x16 and works best against non-black, non-white background. This also comes with Spanish and Portuguese orthography.

BG2 sheet contains the basic English alphabets and sentence symbols and BG3 contains the rest. If you're short of space and only need to use English, you can omit BG3.

This font uses 3 monochrome colors, which are mapped to the global SMW palette on Row 4.

packages.name: smwgraphics-redrawn-styled-bowser-castle-set

packages.description:
A Redrawn-styled Bowser Castle set meant for interior and exterior areas, complete with foreground, background, and ExAnimation (both normal and Layer 3), which is inspired by various Mario games such as SMB3, NSMB (1+2), Mario RPG, Mario & Luigi 1 DX, and others.

Test levels (containing the ExAnimation data), palettes, and map16 files are included alongside the ExGFX files.

Note: While the Backgrounds are compatible with the Status Bar, the Layer 3 BGs are meant to be used with a non-layer 3 Status Bar or a HUD which doesn't cover the upper half of the screen with Layer 3 tiles. In any case, the backgrounds can be edited manually without issues to remove the top tiles should the user want to keep SMW's original Status Bar.

packages.name: smwgraphics-redrawn-styled-cloud-tileset
packages.title: Redrawn Styled Cloud Tileset
packages.description:
For those redrawn style enthusiasts, this pack that promises to expand the original cloud stuff from Super Mario World Redrawn may be useful.

It adds new faces and sizes for the original redrawn cloud stuff from SMWR, useful if you want to create a cloud section or just make your hack more varied.

It uses palette 7 from SMWR (so if you're using this hack graphics the palette included isn't necessary), and a great map16 slot.

Also includes upside down versions for each cloud, which act as 1C8 (but being a bit glitched).

NOTE 1: Tile 3F7 just mimics the original cloud (happy and upside up), so you can ignore it and use global tiles cloud if you want.

NOTE 2: The pack also includes GFX14 from SMWR that contains the redrawn cloud graphic if you're not using SMWR.

packages.name: smwgraphics-redrawn-styled-fire-chomp

packages.description:
For use with edit1754's Fire Chomp sprite.

A Redrawn-styled SMB3 Fire Chomp for use in SMW Redrawn-styled SMW hacks. Comes in two main versions based on mouth shading, further divided by head animations, and fire palette.

packages.name: smwgraphics-redrawn-styled-fryguy

packages.description:
Redrawn-style graphics for Sonikku's SMB2 Fryguy custom sprite, meant to be an amalgam between his official artwork and Super Mario All-Stars/Super Mario Advance in-game design.

packages.name: smwgraphics-redrawn-styled-ghost-guy-snufit
packages.title: Redrawn Styled Ghost Guy & Snufit
packages.description:
Redrawn-styled graphics for the custom sprite recreations of the Ghost Guy (bu smkdan) and Snufit enemies (by RussianMan) respectively.

Multiple variations are included depending on what palettes the Snufits look best with (+ one that invokes the enemy's design from Super Mario 64). Similarly, the Ghost Guy has 2 variations based on whether its mask is closer to Icegoom's Shy Guy, or if it uses a custom mask of my own design.

Finally, the custom palette included also comes with a palette for the Ghoul Guy variation of Ghost Guy seen in Mario & Luigi: Partners in Time. As this one's set in Palette E, using it requires changing Ghost Guy's color through PIXI's CFG editor to apply it.

Credit's not required but heavily appreciated.

packages.description: A redrawn version of this sprite, it comes with some variants so you can choose the one you like the most, the red one uses the original red palette from redrawn, the one with black spots is meant to ressemble the in game sprite Hoopster had in other games, the one with pink spots is based on artworks, and the yellow one is how the enemy looked like in Super Mario Advance 1.

A redrawn styled death block useful for signaling a hurting block. It acts as 12F (the piranha plant act as that hurts the player) but you can set it as 130, 25 or whatever you want.

It uses only 3 tiles from BG3 so probably won't take up much slot, and uses the blank part of palette row 7 (along with black and white used colors).

packages.name: smwgraphics-redrawn-styled-jelectro

packages.name: smwgraphics-redrawn-styled-joe-the-shark

packages.name: smwgraphics-redrawn-styled-koophd-pack
packages.title: Redrawn Styled KooPhD Pack
packages.description:
A custom pack based on Iceguy KooPhD's custom sprite. It comes with graphics meant to go along with Icegoom's redrawn style that can be used for both the custom sprite in question, and also the normal SMW Koopa and all of its variants (shell-less, super, net, etc.).

The normal KooPhD graphics use SP1 to SP4, while the custom sprite - including its vial projectile- uses only SP3. Also included are 4 versions of the graphics meant for SP3: 2 where KooPhD's vials use either normal or smear frames when thrown; and another 2 where the custom sprite is in full lab coat and lacks a shell (for those who want the custom sprite to be visually distinct from the normal KooPhDs).

Custom palettes for all 4 possible KooPhDs are included as well.

Give credit if used, as it's always appreciated.

packages.name: smwgraphics-redrawn-styled-lava-lotus

packages.name: smwgraphics-sanae-kochiya
packages.title: Sanae Kochiya
packages.description:
Player graphics of Sanae Kochiya from Touhou Project.

The Player 2 palette is Reimu Hakurei.
The fire palettes for each player are white haired "Mokou" Sanae and PC-98 Reimu respectively.

Includes the following files:
- GFX00.bin (Big player extra sprites)
- GFX10.bin (Map player)
- GFX22.bin (Small kiss blush)
- GFX24.bin (Big kiss blush)
- GFX28.bin (Hud text: "SANAE" & "REIMU")
- GFX32.bin (Player graphics)
- sanae_shared.pal (Shared player palette)

- yoshi_ow_fix.pal (Fix for Yoshi's overworld palette. To apply, import to every overworld submap using the Green Star + Red Arrow button in Lunar Magic)

Please note that the art style is not "smw styled", so it may not be entirely accurate to vanilla.


If you just want to play vanilla smw as Sanae, consider using this "Super Sanae World" bps patch instead. It has been patched to fix all text and adds other Sanae-related gfx changes (custom title screen & "The End" picture)

A simple and very nice tileset from Sexy Parodius. This game has two stage 3: one being Castle Dracula, and the other one being an underwater palace. This specific stage is based in Yie Air Kung-Fu, one of the first fighting games in history, made by Konami. The ramen bowls in the original game is where chinese dragons spawns to attack the player. A good fit for chinese / eastern based levels.

Credit would be great, but is optional.
