packages.name: smwgraphics-sexy-parodius-psx-bath-house-boss
packages.title: Sexy Parodius (PSX) - Bath House (Boss)
packages.description:
Originally, I wanted to rip the stage 1 BG from Sexy Parodius as debut, but since PSX-View had no ability to save a screenshot using a button as far as I know, (I may come back to it when I can.) I decided to go for the stage 2 boss BG where the player ship fights Finally Penguin. I removed the candles as not only those weren't able to have their own palette as I ripped the BG with Lunar Magic Bitmap Pasting Feature, but I also edited the BG in Aseprite to remove the blocks at the very top and bottom and replaced those with the tiles seen in PSX-View. Use it in either a level end section or a boss fight. You can technically have horizontal scrolling if set to a really slow value such as Slow or Slow 2.
Enjoy as it took a lot from me.

packages.name: smwgraphics-sexy-parodius-psx-bath-house-far

packages.description:

packages.name: smwgraphics-sexy-parodius-psx-castle-dracula
packages.title: Sexy Parodius (PSX) - Castle Dracula
packages.description:
Originally, this BG was only meant to be used for horizontal scrolling. However, I decided to complete it with tiles that meant to be used with vertical scrolling. Result is good. I used Lunar Magic Bitmap Pasting feature a 2nd time, because the first time when I added the BG into LM, I did notice some reds I didn't spot into Aseprite. How can you blame me. Those did look the same. Corrected this glitched behaviour of the BG with the color green and added the proper red color for the BG.
Uses 2 palettes. I thought it'd use more.

No credit needed.

packages.name: smwgraphics-sexy-parodius-psx-coal-mine-outside
packages.title: Sexy Parodius (PSX) - Coal Mine (Outside)
packages.description:
Here's another BG encountered after you fail Castle Dracula in Sexy Parodius. When I tried ripping this BG, I failed because of the number of colors.

I tried again later, this time with good results.

Still, because this BG uses way more tiles than needed, since it comes from a Playstation game, I had to apply the Touhou formula.

I kept on flipping many tiles and removed few tiles for a repeatable tile. I also removed the stars for an easier time.

Used Lunar Magic Bitmap Pasting feature and did corrections.

Used the second half of palette 6 to correct the tree and its stump since the result gave me a blue one and decided to bring the stars from the game back. This BG uses the unused tile B.

The stars use palette 0.

The BG overwrites bushes, diagonal pipes, triangle and transluscent blocks and net tiles. The rest of the tiles can be used.

Also uses the second half of palette row 4.

Enjoy!

Edit: Replaced map16 E000 with E600.

versions.title: Sexy Parodius (PSX) - Coal Mine (Outside)
versions.filename: Sexy Parodius (PSX) - Coal Mine - outside - good.zip

packages.name: smwgraphics-sexy-parodius-psx-farm-day

packages.name: smwgraphics-sexy-parodius-psx-sweet-sky
packages.title: Sexy Parodius (PSX) - Sweet Sky
packages.description:

In the original, the rainbow was transparent and I don't have the asm knowledge to add it for the rainbow for this game, but perhaps someone with this knowledge might be able to leave a code that's compatible with the HDMA included in the archive.
The clouds were a great challenge for me to paste into Aseprite while looking good. Drew some new tiles for the clouds for proper loop. Use the Lunar Magic Bitmap Pasting feature twice to rip this BG and removed most of the useless pixels near the vines for detail.

No credit needed.

packages.name: smwgraphics-skyland
packages.title: Skyland
packages.description:
A custom sky themed tileset. These graphics are set up to allow users to still use all the extra tiles in the FG1 slot, minus the bushes and slanted pipe of course. This set also contains upside down slopes if you would like to use them. Also contains pillars, blocks, and ledges which can be used for temples/ruins.

NOTES:
- Make sure to set the GFX Header (the purple poison shroom) to Underground in order to get the upside down slope interaction to work correctly.
- Also contains tiles that allow pipes to be placed on top of clouds correctly.

Compatible tiles from FG1:
- Doors
- Vines
- Arrow sign
- Moon
- Translucent block
- Nets (and all edges)
- Triangle block
- Goal posts
- Midway point
- Star block
- On/Off switch

packages.name: smwgraphics-snes-controller-buttons
packages.title: SNES Controller Buttons
packages.description:
Originally made and submitted (and rejected) on the Summer C3 of 2023. This submission was a suggestion / request by
Heitor Porfirio.
It has since been refined and greatly improved thanks to the feedback received.

This is a pack of graphic tiles for each and every button on a SNES / Super Famicom controller.
They're intended to be used in tutorial levels, or as general indicators of what input is expected from the player at any point in a level.

There are a few alternate designs for most buttons to suit different needs and preferences, including different colors and button formats.
There are also animated versions of all tiles to show the button being pressed.

The graphics use a handful of palette rows to accomodate for all different colors of buttons, but only uses the right side of them, so the only palettes overwritten are Pink Berry and Red Berry.
Depending on your needs, you may not use all palettes.

The included ReadMe file contains information on the usage of palettes, as well as the use of slots for ExAnimation, so it's worth checking out if you need to change these things for any reason (such as palette space, AN2 file space, ExAnimation slots...).

packages.name: smwgraphics-somari-rings
packages.title: Somari - Rings
packages.description:
That's an update for the Somari Rings submission (firstly submitted by KaidenThelens and updated by Hammerer (me)).

This update includes some notable changes, like:

1. The gfx for the rings was modified, now it looks more like the Somari rings ripped.
2. Added the ring graphics in GFX01 (for the coin animation when hit blocks), something missed in the first submission, along with the ring palette in palette row A for the coin sprites (it replaces the last 3 color slots (AD, AE and AF))
NOTE: The tile EA is slighter than the GFX33 version, since it was necessary to reduce the tile size to fit in the 8x8 space.
3. The blue palette in row 7 is different now, with shades that match best with the original palette (in row 6).
4. There's now the option to modify also the coin tile used in status bar, replacing it with the ring miniature in Sumari's status bar. I've included two ways to do that:

Way 1 (still): Using the tile 2E included in the submission's GFX28;

Way 2 (animated): Using ExAnimation to replace the original tile 2E in GFX28 with an animation similar to the coin animation in Sumari's status bar.

For this, the submission includes a mwl file with the exanimation (it's in the level exanimation option - you can change it to the global exanimation option if you want without problems) and a ExGFX file to be inserted in AN2 slot (you can set the exanimation to use alternate ExGFX file instead of using AN2, name the file with 60-63 for it).
NOTE: It will also change the collected Dragon/Yoshi Coin graphics in the status bar, as SMW uses the same tile for both!
5. You may want to use Tweaker tool to change the palette row used by sprites 45 (directional coin) and 7E (flying coin) from 8 and C to A.
Description from the first version of the submission:

Rings from Somari. That's about it.

packages.name: smwgraphics-sonic-mania-press-garden-zone-act
packages.title: Sonic Mania - Press Garden Zone (Act 2 - Trees)
packages.description:
This is both ripped and original. By original, I mean I drew some extra tiles, as I wasn't able to include every tile here. Besides, I might end up with more tiles. Also, I aimed for accuracy. I think I did well, but it's your decision. I did this according to Teyla's suggestion. This goes really well with Anorakun's Sonic Mania - Press Garden Zone rip.
Here's what you can do:

-full 512x512 BG - check;
-configurable BG for other users - check, but watch out.
-uses all palettes - check. I wanted to add more, but because of palette limitations, I went with my configuration and turned out well.
-SMW status bar compatibility - no. You must use either DKCR Sprite Status Bar or Remove Status Bar patches.
-tile consumption: 124 8x8 tiles. A very good BG choice.
-.mwl sample file - check;
-screenshot and in-game pic - irrelevant, but check.

Give credit, if used.

packages.name: smwgraphics-steampunk-storm
packages.title: Steampunk Storm
packages.description:
My foreground entry for the ExGFX contest in 2016.

Stormy clouds and steampunk-styled flying submarines. Many animations are used.
Custom blocks for the thunderbolts are not included.

Credit is not necessary but I appreciate it.

packages.name: smwgraphics-steel-empire-stage
packages.title: Steel Empire - Stage 1
packages.description:
Here's the BG of the 1st stage of Steel Empire for the Sega Genesis or Mega Drive. NSX2015 ripped it and I made it available for SMW.
It doesn't use many map16 tiles.
Recommended scrolling: use variable horizontal and vertical scrolling or variable horizontal scrolling and slow vertical scrolling.

No credit required.

packages.name: smwgraphics-stitch
packages.title: Stitch
packages.description:
Stitch! My favourite Disney's character!

- Ripped Big Stitch (After given a Mushroom) from Lilo & Stitch: Space Baby/The Firmament Baby (Bootleg) by changing colors and by removing antennas.

- Small Stitch made by myself.

- Palmask only for Stitch in the overworld.

- Vanilla palette for Stitch Player (Not need to change his color) and Stitch can got the Leroy color after given a Fire Flower.

- You'll need the 32x32 Player Tilemap Patch.

- Don't use it for scenes (Like castle destruction)

Update: There was small things that I forgotten to modify.

packages.name: smwgraphics-stone-pathways
packages.title: Stone Pathways
packages.description:
Yay, more graphics...
This is some town graphics - it has houses, with enterable doors and stand on roofs, bridges, slopes on roofs for pointy roofs.

It doesn't do much else really apart from look pretty and be useable for graphics :D

packages.name: smwgraphics-stone-wall-ruin
packages.title: Stone Wall Ruin
packages.description:
From time to time you just need something interesting to add a bit of depth to a Level, using Layer 3. I pixelated these ruins for one of my hacks and they could be great for ghosthouses or catacombs.
Have fun with them, please give credits if you use them.

Please use it with Kevin's Ram Toggled Status Bar or any other patch / uberasm that removes the status bar.

Best Rudi

packages.name: smwgraphics-stranded-spaceship
packages.title: Stranded Spaceship
packages.description:
An abandoned spaceship tileset, as requested by Anorakun. Hopelessly and aimlessly drift through the galaxy, in style!

Credit is not required.

Falconpunch Edit: I made some edits to this tileset to make it much more versatile.

packages.name: smwgraphics-strata-ridge
packages.title: Strata Ridge
packages.description:
A lightweight cliff/ridge/mountain tileset that uses only one palette line and one bin file; includes three palette variants.

This is a port of a small tileset I designed awhile ago for a development project that was cancelled. It was designed with SNES limitations in mind, so it uses minimal palette and file size.

Enjoy!

packages.name: smwgraphics-street-fighter
packages.title: Street Fighter (1987) - Ryu and Ken
packages.description:
Here's The Finished Graphics Of SF1 Ryu. He's Originally From The First Game.

The Zip Includes:

Palettes
GFX00
GFX10
GFX22
GFX24
GFX28
GFX32
shared.pal


Moderator's note: I've included alternate GFX and a palette file to fix Yoshi's colors on the Overworld, by sacrificing a single color in the palette and moving things around a bit.

To use it, use the gfx in the alternate folder, and import the palette with the Green Star + Red Arrow button on every submap.

packages.name: smwgraphics-streets-of-rage-title-screen
packages.title: Streets of Rage - Title Screen
packages.description: Ripped from the Title Screen of the first Streets of Rage on Megadrive (Genesis in North America).

packages.name: smwgraphics-stripeless-switch-palace
packages.title: Stripeless Switch Palace
packages.description:
Oh wow, words cannot express how much I despise the vanilla SMW switch palace tileset. The stripes everywhere make my eyeballs want to puke. So, I made this simplified tileset that uses the existing pallet that is a bit easier on the eyes. Could be helpful for people with photosensitivity? Can be easily recoloured to match any colour theme.

As seen in my hack Wake Up Call

pls credit me

packages.name: smwgraphics-stronghold
packages.title: Stronghold
packages.description: Old GFX set I drew, inspired by Demon's Crest. Includes 1 exanimation.

packages.name: smwgraphics-stuart-little
packages.title: Stuart Little 2 (GBA) - City
packages.description: A background depicting a distant city and some bushes, found in Stuart Little 2 for the Game Boy Advance.

packages.name: smwgraphics-subcon-overworld
packages.title: Subcon Overworld
packages.description:
This OW GFX set was for my hack Super Mario Dream World. It's meant for SMB2 based hacks.

Moderator edit: the top of the vase was out of perspective. Edited it to make it look more consistent.

packages.name: smwgraphics-submarine-sam
packages.title: Submarine Sam
packages.description: A submarine variant of Torpedo Ted that can be used in deep, dark waters.

packages.name: smwgraphics-submarine-ship
packages.title: Submarine/Ship
packages.description:
My C3 2014 summer submission.

The graphics are made by shikatermia (from Mario Fan Games Galaxy), not me, it was stated that the credit isn't required for this.

I hope that you enjoy.

packages.name: smwgraphics-subor-v8
packages.title: Subor V8.0 - Title Screen
packages.description:
The background used in the title screen of version 8.0 of Subor's educational machine for the NES.

Notes: The cutoff with the hill is present in the original, and horizontal scroll must be set to None.

packages.name: smwgraphics-sugar-sweet-tileset
packages.title: Sugar Sweet Tileset
packages.description:
HAPPY BIRTHDAY Donut !!

A sugary sweet tileset with mushrooms, slopes and bridges (as well as a =P cloud).
Barely fits into one ExGFX file.

Can be used in a food related level.

packages.name: smwgraphics-summer-hammer-time-beach-and-cave
packages.title: Summer Hammer Time - Beach and Cave
packages.description:
Handdrawn beach and cave tileset I originally made for my CLDC 2016 entry, named Summer Hammer Time. Contains FG, BG, Layer 3 graphics, tilemap and an ExAnimation GFX file to be used with the beach BG.

Recommended to use Lui37's "Move Layer 3 to subscreen fix" patch as well, unless you want your status bar to go behind layers 1 and 2. Or use a sprite status bar.

Nope Edit: Very minor fixes to sample levels; unused palette rows were wiped out, added them back in to save users a step in inserting these. The animated tiles in the beach background were set to slots so they would change animation on the same frame.

versions.title: Summer Hammer Time - Beach and Cave

packages.name: smwgraphics-sumo-wrestler
packages.title: Sumo Wrestler
packages.description: These graphics replace the Mega Mole and the Sumo Bro. Great for japanese levels, but can work with any type of level. Uses vanilla palette. All the credits should go to No Body The Dragon.

packages.name: smwgraphics-sunny-island
packages.title: Sunny Island
packages.description:
This is the fixed version of my first graphic. It's a simple BG of an island in the sea (which can be animated or not) with the Sun behind it. You can use it in sea-side levels or in a cutscene.
Uses BG1, ExAnimation and 2 rows of palettes ( the first half of the palette 0 and the palette 2).

This file contains:
-bg1.bin (the graphic itself);
-an2.bin (the ExAnimation);
-.mwl file (the sample level);
-Map16 file;
-.pal file (palette).

Credits? I would appreciate, but it doesn't need it.

packages.name: smwgraphics-sunny-plains
packages.title: Sunny Plains
packages.description: This is some graphics from my Chocolate Level Design Contest Entry, which I'm now releasing. Please give credit if used.

Ripped from the Ending Screen of Sunset Riders on Super Nintendo.

Have fun!

The fleshy background seen in SAI's Round 2-3. Yes, believe it

packages.description:
The foreground tiles of the jungle level of Super Adventure Island. Ripped by me. Uses palettes 0x2 and 0x4.

Background will be inserted later if I can. Use only in Underground levels (1).
Enjoy.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-adventure-island-mist
packages.title: Super Adventure Island - Mist
packages.description:
The mist seen in SAI's Round 3-2, which is actually Layer 2 in the original game due to game's limitations, but it uses 3 colors per tile so for smw hacking purposes it fits better as Layer 3, so I did it so.

This is a fullscreen layer 3 so it's best to use it with Sprite Status Bar (or a similar asm workaround) to display it properly without cut. However, the tilemap is easily editable so you can adjust it to keep vanilla status bar without issues.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-adventure-island-snow
packages.title: Super Adventure Island - Snow
packages.description: The snow set that appears in level 3-3 from Super Adventure Island.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-adventure-island-stage-1
packages.title: Super Adventure Island - Stage 1-2 (Forest)
packages.description:
Here are the foreground graphics from the forest level on Super Adventure Island for the SNES. (The second level of the game.) It includes all the tiles in the level for the most part except all the waterfall graphics.


Comes with three ExGFX files which includes the waterfall animation and uses palette rows 2-5 and uses a little bit of row 7.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-adventure-island-stage-5
packages.title: Super Adventure Island - Stage 5-2 (Castle)
packages.description:
Here are the graphics from the first castle level on Super Adventure Island for the SNES. (The level before the final level.) It's a pretty small tile set but with decorations it can go well with castle type levels.

Uses palette row 2 and half of 3.

packages.description: The underwater background seen in SAI's Round 4-3.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-alfred-chicken-cheese
packages.title: Super Alfred Chicken - Cheese
packages.description:
This is a resubmission of my previous Alfred Chicken Cheese foreground. Download this, NOT the other. This has more foreground objects and all of the Map16 problems are fixed.

This is the foreground of the first level in the strange yet memorable game Alfred Chicken. Features cheese, wires, and other things that I can't name.

Ripped by Piky36 from screenshots. No edit's tool here. No credit needed, but if you feel the need to do it you can.

packages.description: The toy-filled foreground from the second level of Alfred Chicken, ripped by me. Credit wouldn't hurt.

packages.title: Super Back to the Future Part II - Stage 4-1 and 4-2
packages.description:
Ripped from Super Back to the Future Part II

I already advance that this one is not the complete tilemap of the game because it is a run and jump so the tilemap is linear but this one does not lose details compared to the original

both palettes are included the day palette is part of stage 4-2 and the night palette is from stage 4-1

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-bat-puncher-general-tileset
packages.title: Super Bat Puncher - General Tileset
packages.description:
This is a rip of the general graphics in 'Super Bat Puncher'.
A rather unknown game, developed by Morphcat Games.

I think these Graphics would fit really well in a mega-man style like cave level. ;)

I hope you have fun with the Graphics! :D

Edit: Map16 is in the folder now (forgot to include it). I also reworked the Map16 and the Demo-Level a bit! :D

-badummzi

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-bomberman
packages.title: Super Bomberman 2 - Battle Mode Menu & Password Screen
packages.description:
The background seen in the Battle Mode Menu and Password Screen from Super Bomberman 2.

Recommended usage is using it with a large line of tiles 152 (invisible solid), and other kind of global objects.

The cracks and holes in the wall can be easily organized in any kind of pattern.

A good fit for urban levels.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-bonk-juicy-jungle
packages.title: Super Bonk - Juicy Jungle
packages.description:
It's the BG seen where Bonk is in a giant house that belongs to a dinosaur. There are enemies slightly bigger than Bonk.
You can edit the back area color, it consumes nearly a GFX file and palette can be edited.
Recommended scrolling: both horizontal and vertical scrolling set to variable.
Credit isn't needed.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-bonk-moon-towers
packages.title: Super Bonk - Moon Towers
packages.description: These are the Moon Towers BG and FG from Super Bonk, I really like the FG colors here, but that's not why I had to fit it into 1 palette (row 2), because there were in 2 or 3 separate palettes in the original game, plus, I felt too sick and a little nauseous (and also kinda lazy) to add the Earth as seen from the moon in the BG, I couldn't fit the whole FG tileset in 1 ExGFX file so I had to split it into one for the FG3 slot and the BG3 slot

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-bonk-sky-bonus-area
packages.title: Super Bonk - Sky Bonus Area
packages.description:
Ripped this background from 'Super Bonk'.
This background could be used for sky/bonus themed levels.
The palette file (.tpl file) overwrites palettes 3,4,5 and the first half colors of palette 0.

Credit is not required.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-bunny-world-grassland
packages.title: Super Bunny World - Grassland
packages.description: The grassland tileset from Super Bunny World, a cute little mobile game about a cute little bunny. The block that looks like a square from a waffle is breakable in the original game, so it could be used as a brick block, I guess.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-buster-bros-silk-road
packages.title: Super Buster Bros - Silk Road
packages.description:
This is the beta version of the game. It's the same as the original. This background is seen in the area where the boys or, in my case, boy since I was playing the game myself, busts colored balls in a desert area with mountains afar and a building that clearly looks like a prison. This BG had game assisted tiles that stood in my way. I ripped the background using Lunar Magic bitmap pasting feature, since the BG uses more colors. Fortunately, the tiles were already drawn, so used those. Besides using palette 3, uses the 2nd half of palette 4 and palette 1 without affecting SMW colors.
Have fun using it!

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-castlevania-iv-stage
packages.title: Super Castlevania IV - Stage 7 (Art Gallery)
packages.description:
A simple and spooky background used in the second half of stage 7, from Super Castlevania IV.

This skull-themed background can fit ghost houses, castle or haunted levels, in general.

UPDATE: Optimized GFX files, saving around 4 tiles of space, making it more user friendly. Moved it to the BG1 slot, as well. Adjusted background looping a tiny bit too.

packages.title: Super Castlevania IV - Stage A (Clock Tower - Entrance)

A very dark and simple background used in the entrance of the Clock Tower, from Super Castlevania IV. A great fit for dungeons or prison escape sequences or even castles.

One of the backgrounds of the iconic Clock Tower, from Super Castlevania IV. Perfect fit for tower levels. It's mostly seen in the vertical sections of the stage.

I recommend using it for vertical levels or very tall horizontal levels. Although it uses two palette rows, only the final three colors of palette 5 are used.

The original background is not that large, but I expanded it to fit Super Mario World.

Credit would be great, but is optional.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-fantasy-zone-stage

The BG and the FG were on the same layer in the original game but this isn't much of a problem here since this stage is shrouded in darkness and you've gotta buy some super lights to light up the stage, still in the original game. Adding some parallax scrolling (like in the original game) is highly recommended for this BG.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-mario-all-stars-custom-forest
packages.title: Super Mario All-Stars - Custom Forest
packages.description:
This tileset was based in some stuff from Super Mario Maker 2 in Super Mario Bros. from NES mode, from some other tilesets.
Now, it was completely created in the Super Mario All-Stars style!

The Background and Layer 3 contains three other palette variants plus the default one, that means you have four options.

And the Foreground has only one palette variant plus the default one, resulting in two options.

NOTE: If you use the Layer 3, you still can use the vanilla status bar normally if your level doesn't have vertical scrolling, and along with the background obviously.
But it's most recommended that you use some alternate patch that modifies the status bar mechanics.

Here are some examples:
DKCR Styled Sprite Status Bar
New Super Mario Bros. Wii Styled Status Bar
Remove Status Bar
RAM Toggled Status Bar (& IRQ)

Ripped from these sheets:
SMAS Custom Forest Background
SMAS Custom Forest Tileset

Both made by SuperSledgeBro, and some extra stuff/modifications by me.

Enjoy!

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-mario-bros-deluxe-styled-overworld
packages.title: Super Mario Bros. Deluxe Styled Overworld
packages.description:
These are overworld graphics loosely based on the overworld graphics from Super Mario Bros. Deluxe for the GBC.

Caveats:
- These graphics are not compatible with the original SMW overworld graphics. If you want to use these, you'll have to (re)build your overworld from scratch.
- The waterfall animation is 15 FPS. SMW doesn't initialize overworld animations like it does with level animations, meaning overworld animations faster than 7.5 FPS mess up in-game. This is fixed in Lunar Magic 2.53, but if you're using an earlier version of Lunar Magic for whatever reason, there's a fix included that uses UberASM. Alternately, there's a version included that slows the waterfall down to half speed to sidestep this issue.
- The level tiles use multiple color palette animation. If you want to edit the animation, edit ExGFX 84 in a hex editor starting at offset FC4 at your peril. If you want to remove the animation, clear global exanimation slot 03.

versions.title: Super Mario Bros. Deluxe Styled Overworld

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-mario-maker-super-mario-world-airship
packages.title: Super Mario Maker: Super Mario World - Airship
packages.description:
Ripped from Super Mario Maker; official SMW(ish)-styled airship graphics.

Mario Maker has multiple variations of some of these tiles, but including these small tile variations would use up an excessive amount of space. I opted to only include tiles with significant differences, though some tiles may still be slightly similar to others.

Small modifications to the graphics were made in the event that the changes were nearly unnoticeable to conserve palette space. They use palettes 2 and 3, along with the unused half of palette 4. Additionally, there is a small amount of space leftover which can be filled by ExAnimation or other graphics.

Palette and PalMask files are both included.

Here is a tutorial how to get the squashed Goomba GFX.
http://www.smwcentral.net/?p=viewthread&t=35765&page=1

You can also add your custom Goombas for the sprites too.

Parachute Goombas NOT INCLUDED!

I wonder if the ice wiggler is here?


Well, now it is! A wiggler frozen in an ice block. Contains both 7-colour (half a palette row) and 15-colour (full palette row) versions. They both use the same map16. Acts like a cement block, and to make it slippery either toggle that setting for the level or use a custom slippery block.

packages.description:

Magikoopa had the biggest changes due to the original Super Mario Maker sprites being too small so I combined the bodies between the original and Mario Makers! To change the color of the new Para-Bomb and Bubble Bob-ombs use Tweaker and choose Palette B.

I didn't include.

-Turning Yoshi Body due to size being too wide.
-New Dry Bones due to size.
-No new Line guides.
-No new Lakitu Cloud.
-No new Door.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-mario-world-beta-cage-mockup
packages.title: Super Mario World - Beta Cage (Mockup)
packages.description:
At long last, the famous beta cage mockup from TCRF is finally here to the public, right where it belongs! Credit to BMF (a.k.a. Rachel Mae) for the original mockup! Unfortunately, the actual .bin file for the graphics wasn't shared, so I had to manually draw every tile accurately from the screenshot. Included is a patch that allows you to remap the sprite tiles used by the wings. It also features the basic ability to manually remap the tiles used by the cage in case you don't want to use the provided LT4 file for some reason. The provided LG4 file can either be used per-level or globally replace 'GFX2B.bin', but be aware that the 'Nintendo' and 'SUPER MARIO BROS. 4' text are overwritten. Lastly, the provided SP2 file contains a slightly modified version of the prototype wings that overwrites the Yoshi berry. Enjoy!

No More Sprite Tiles Limit v1.2.1. is needed for all the wings to display properly.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-mario-world-beta-styled-bros-and-giant-enemies
packages.title: Super Mario World (Beta) Styled Bros. and Giant Enemies
packages.description:
Custom graphics for the generic Bro. enemies that come with Romi's Sprite Tool 1.41 and Nameless Protagonist's Fire/Ice Bro pack. It comes with:

-SMW pre-release styled graphics for the Hammer / Boomerang / Fire / Ice Bros. Due to the graphics for these being unfinished, I took some liberties regarding how they would have looked had they stayed in the final game.

-SMW styled graphics for the Hammer / Boomerang / Fire / Ice Bros. Mostly based on the Super Mario Maker Hammer Bro. graphics.

Contents of the zip:
-GFX00.bin*4
-GFX32.bin*4 (four versions for each of the options mentioned above)
-GFX22.bin (sorted only with the options it's needed for)
-A shared palette for the overworld
-And a readme with in-depth installation instructions as well as example.png which the readme refers to.

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-mario-world-redrawn
packages.title: Super Mario World Redrawn
packages.description:
Icegoom's original description: "I've played a lot of SMW hacks. Many of them have really cool graphical changes. But one thing that always bugged me was that no matter how extensive the changes were elsewhere, there were always a certain amount of old SMW sprites left over. You can't rip climbing Koopas, Urchins, Fishin' Boo, or Bowser's Clown Car from other games. So I set out to redraw every single sprite in the game in a Gameboy Advance/Nintendo DS style. Along the way, I also started doing foreground objects.

Basically, this hack is here for anyone starting work on a Super Mario World hack who wants a complete and stylistically consistent spriteset. The sprites themselves are basically done, although I'll tweak them quite a bit for the next release. The foregrounds are in an incomplete state, and I haven't even started replacing the backgrounds yet. The overworld's had extensive work done on it, but there are a lot of screwed up palettes I haven't bothered to fix yet.

Anyhoo, these sprites are here for whoever wants them. Completely open source, no credit necessary. Just focus on making some fun Super Mario World hacks, guys."

It's had some modifications from the version hosted in hacks section, some things might be different as the overworld, palettes of some sprites, so you'll have to fix some things yourself with Overworld Editor and with external tools as Tweaker as for some sprites.

It also includes a folder with alternate redrawn graphics in case you feel like trying different versions of graphics icegoom has made before. With this said, hope you enjoy it!

packages.name: smwgraphics-super-mario-world-styled-glass-pipes
packages.title: Super Mario World Styled Glass Pipes
packages.description:
Glass version of the vanilla SMW pipes. The first type uses a lighter blue color and is completely solid. All tiles are available so you can use decorative pipes and exit enabled pipes. The second type uses a darker blue color and is priority enabled and non-solid. You will need to place solid blocks around these to prevent the player from falling through. The best application is to use them in the ground with solid tiles around them that use the same graphic as the rest of the ground around them. The passthrough pipes have been modified to create a better visual effect preventing the 1 pixel line of transparency on the sides.

For an even better visual effect, use a background that has a sky in the top and underground theme on the bottom (such as the underground bg from SMAS SMB3), and set the Layer 2 scrolling to H:Variable, V:Constant. Adjust the height of the background so the sky starts where the ground of the level is going to be, to prevent sky from showing through the transparent underground pipes.

versions.title: Super Mario World Styled Glass Pipes

packages.description:
That's an alternative for Zuccha's Orbinaut sprite here, featuring SMW styled graphics as the original sprite features non-SMW styled graphics, so being useful if you want to use the sprite but on a SMW styled hack.

Important Notes:

1. You must need to change the sprite (orbinaut.json and orbinaut_spike_ball.json) for another palette row using CFG Editor, a program included in PIXI files.

The sprite is intended to feature a blue color, so you would need to change it for palette row B, but you can as well change it for another sprite palette row that would fit good with the sprite, as row A (yellow), row C (red) and row D (green).

Don't forget you need to change the palette row for both sprites included, orbinaut.json and orbinaut_spike_ball.json, but if you want you can set different color for head and spike balls sprites (for example, making the orbinaut head gets green and the spike balls get red).

2. Credits aren't necessary, but would get me happy.

packages.title: Super Mario World Styled Super Mario Bros. 3 Overworld
packages.description: This is an smw-styled approach at the more diorama-y overworld maps of Super Mario Bros 3. It comes with full compatibility with SMW paths as well as SMB3-style straight paths with the dots inbetween. Personally I prefer the latter. You can keep the landscape geometry more faithful to SMB3 with its sharp corners, or you can lean more into the SMW style with some diagonal ledges. Collapse Text

packages.name: smwgraphics-taiketsu-ultra-hero-gba-clouds

Hi. I'm here with another BG from a game I never heard of in my life. It's called 'Taiketsu! Ultra Hero ' for the GBA. The word 'Taiketsu' means 'Showdown'. The BG was used in The City stage. Originally, this BG was ripped by Omega, the one from Spriters Resource. I converted it to SMW usage by using the Lunar Magic Bitmap Pasting Feature. The best thing is that the palette is very easy to edit and the back area color is used, too. I had to fix the BG a bit with no trouble at all. Because this BG comes from a fighting game, it's recommended to set both Vertical and Horizontal scrolling of the BG to None.
Omega85 deserves the credit. I only did my job. Enjoy!

BE is used for the Ice Mountains stage. This had the Touhou-like formula. I actually had to edit the BG, as the original version surpassed the 4 GFX limit. You can use the Goal Tape, Midway Bar, Doors, Star Blocks and 3-up Moons and that's it. Because of the BG structure, either the top, bottom or both parts must be covered. In the screenshot, you see the BG being covered by the bottom part. Because this BG comes from a fighting game, it's recommended to set both Vertical and Horizontal scrolling of the BG to None.
Omega85 deserves the credit.
Hope it's useful.

packages.name: smwgraphics-the-legend-of-the-mystical-ninja-horo-temple
packages.title: The Legend of the Mystical Ninja - Horo Temple
packages.description:
A complete (almost) rip of the first stage from Ganbare Goemon : Yuuki Hime Kyuushitsu Esaki, lit. "The Rescue of Princess Yuki", or The Legend of the Mystical Ninja.

Unlike the old rip in this site, who had a messy map 16 and a worse sample level, almost everything here was ripped manually, with the exception of the tree and the ruined walls, because in those I used the bitmap pasting feature, and then I rearranged the tiles manually in Lunar Magic. This rip took me two days to get it right. Perfect fit for haunted levels, since in the original game, it's used in a level with flaming ghosts, flying umbrellas, skeleton warriors and zombies.

WHAT IS INCLUDED IN THIS RIP:

- Main ground;
- Ruined walls;
- Bamboo;
- Bamboo Spikes;
- Tombstones;
- Trees;
- Grass;
- Logs;
- A "Shrine" of sorts. I also included the bell from the original game;
- Lanterns;

WHAT IS NOT INCLUDED:

-ExAnimation. I couldn't figure out a way of making it look good in Super Mario World;
- Some gravestones, logs and grass tiles;

Credit would be great, but is optional.

packages.name: smwgraphics-the-legend-of-zelda-oracle-of-ages-seasons-overworld
packages.title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages & Seasons - Overworld
packages.description:
I've always thought the graphics of the overworld from the Legend of Zelda games on the Game Boy would make for a great replacement set of graphics for the overworld in Super Mario World, so here it is.

This is a pretty comprehensive tile set as I took a great deal of effort to get as wide and varied a selection of tiles from the source games into this resource as I felt feasible, to enable many possibilities for terrain style. Additionally, some improvements were made over the originals regarding palettes and tile overlap details since there are fewer technical limitations.

The sample overworld I've included is relatively basic (there's no events, for example) and just throws down some ideas for map areas, but I feel there is a great deal of potential in this set and I look forward to seeing the overworlds people create with this.

NOTE 1: Player 2's colors are slightly brighter than Player 1's.
NOTE 2: The OW palette isn't a shared palette, you must import it on all submaps and the main map or Jerry will look like a silhouette!

You must use this patch to fix the victory pose when you're small while riding Yoshi if you're using him in your hack, the included "Hex Edits.asm" if you want the START messages (which requires the use of the included GFX0F.bin to fix the Y), to change Mario's name to Jerry when selecting or erasing a save file in the title screen, and to change the lives exchanger text when playing with 2 players.

Edit: Antennas were missing from the overworld frames.
Edit 2: Fixed leg in one of the walking while big frames.

packages.description:
I'm back, and this time with a BG from Touhou of all games. This background was originally 512x512, but I had to reduce it to 256x256 due to many many tiles the BG uses. I followed Thomas' idea of reducing the picture as best I could, until nearly 4 ExGFX are used. The result was really good and you do have room for a FG. This was used in the real final battle with Kaguya Houraisan. Use it in boss battles with no scrolling for both background and foreground or levels with background scrolling set to none.

WARNING! THIS SUBMISSION SACRIFICES ALMOST ALL OF THE FG2 TILES.

packages.description:
Here's the BG from Touhou 6. Sure, it's also seen in Stage 6, but this BG is used as spellcard effect by Remilia Scarlet. This was just as hard as Touhou Eiyashou ~ Imperishable Night - Stage 6B (Outside), if not harder. This BG was not only harder to reduce tiles, but I had to remove the 'black' pixels, in order to conserve tile space. This does use the bushes, diagonal pipes and part of the fence tiles. No credit required.

Credit would be appreciated.

- Bullet Bill (horizontal, vertical, and diagonal), Banzai Bill, Torpedo Ted
- Cheep Cheep (from SMB1)
- Piranha Plant, Muncher
- Big Boo, Boo (from YI), Boo Buddies, Boo Block

packages.name: smwmusic-a-ha-take-on-me-invincibility-remix
packages.title: A-ha - Take On Me (Invincibility Remix)
packages.description:
This is to go even further beyond!!!

It's one of A-Ha's best known songs, Take On Me, aka the song that bops every time it's played at a party. It's been remade in a style that's supposed to be used as the music for an invincibility star.

There are two versions of the song:
- Global: This one uses @8 for the bass and @10 for the bass drum. It's optimized to work with the global songs, so you're probably gonna want to use this one if you want it to be your invincibility theme (or p-switch as well). But you can use it as your local song as well.
- Local: This one uses @14 for the bass and @21 for the bass drum. This one won't work with the global songs, but it does use a different set of instruments that some may find to be better than the global version.

This can be used as your invincibility theme, p-switch theme, bonus stage, or even as your victory jingle.

Made a special re-imagined remix of ActRaiser's Fillmore for Halloween. By far one of the most memorable main themes on the system (more than what you can say for Super Castlevania's Theme of Simon) to the point where people can get fooled into thinking this is a Castlevania theme.

packages.name: smwmusic-alcahest-a-world-without-soul-the-demon-underworld-remix
packages.title: Alcahest - A World without Soul ~ The Demon Underworld (Remix)
packages.description:
Did an arrangement of The Demon Underworld from Alcahest. Seriously, for an obscure (but really awesome) Super-Famicom-Only Action RPG by HAL, Jun Ishikawa went hard on this OST. This soundtrack feels like a blend of Ishikawa's style in Kirby Super Star with Nobuo Uematsu's style in the SNES Final Fantasy games. It's easily my favorite Kirby soundtrack given its style and the compositions here.

Originally was planning on doing Panakeian Castle, but I thought I'd give a spotlight to the heavily underrated endgame stage theme 'cuz it's amazing. What's with Squaresoft games having amazing endgame themes anyways?

Important:
♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. C Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. C# Minor (Japanese Goblin Pitch)
3. D Minor (Custom Pitch)

packages.description:
𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐢𝐬 𝐬𝐮𝐬.

Among Us has taken over my brain and forced me to make this lazy remix of of the Dead Body Reported Drip Theme theme. Jokes aside, I decided to do this for fun 'cuz I thought it'd be neat to come up with a short SNES arrangement of that song in my style.

The theme of the third extra stage bosses, Mei and Mai, in the third Seihou game, Banshiryuu. I don't think any of the three people who know about this game expected a port from it to ever exist, eh?

This song is overall a mess, both compositionally and mixing-wise, and while I did try to clean up the mixing at least, it's still a bit all over the place.

Sindy's theme from Barrage Musical, a Touhou clone with a focus on synchronizing everything to the music. The music is also Touhou-styled, with this song probably being one of the most Touhou-sounding in the game.

packages.name: smwmusic-boards-of-canada-dawn-chorus-bass-remix
packages.title: Boards of Canada - Dawn Chorus (bass remix)
packages.description:
This remix was done using a custom bassline I've found to be fitting with the song and a rhythm found in a bootleg song by the band.

It also brings little variations in the flute and choir lines as well as some octave changes.

Very satisfying, serene vibes, useful for chill levels where flying or clouds are involved.

And that's one more song I was able to cover by ear! Now I find it pretty addictive to listen to.

packages.name: smwmusic-boards-of-canada-diving-station
packages.title: Boards of Canada - Diving Station
packages.description:
Another ear-transcribed port of mine. The overall ambience is loyal to original, although performed with a different set of instruments/SFX, I found the noises from Chrono Trigger to be very fitting here.

The duration is shortened a bit as to not insist on the non-melody aspects of the song.

It is probably best fit for overworlds and cutscenes, but can also work in levels that have a timer shorter than the song... Which isn't really a problem either since I gave a loop after a short silence.

It has been showcase at C3 Winter 2022.

packages.title: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow - Underground Reservoir
packages.description:
As the name suggests, this plays in the Underground Reservoir area in the game. It's the obligatory cave/water section of Dracula's castle!

This is my first attempt at a non-SNES port, but I guess it doesn't really count because the GBA is somewhat similar to the SNES hardware-wise :P

Anyway, huge thanks to musicalman for his Samples of Insanity pack! That's where I got most of the samples I used here. And thanks to Pinci too, for helping me find a water SFX sample!

Warning: Incompatible with Blarggs and the Thunder SFX! Also, please don't use this for level 0/100, because the Bonus End jingle won't play correctly. I figured these two samples were fine to exclude since the song doesn't quite fit a lava (Blargg), dramatic/final (Thunder) or bonus level.

packages.name: smwmusic-castlevania-aria-of-sorrow-whip-cross-justice-don-t-wait-until-night-x-heart-of-fire-remix-ii
packages.title: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow - Whip, Cross, & Justice!! ✝️ ~ Don't Wait Until Night x Heart of Fire (Remix II)
packages.description:
❝ 𝔑𝔬𝔱𝔥𝔦𝔫𝔤 𝔶𝔬𝔲 𝔰𝔞𝔶 𝔴𝔦𝔩𝔩 𝔰𝔱𝔬𝔭 𝔪𝔢! 𝔓𝔯𝔢𝔭𝔞𝔯𝔢 𝔱𝔬 𝔡𝔦𝔢! ❞
ㅤ- Julius Belmont, Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (2003)



Did a second arrangement of Don't Wait Until Night from Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow (originally from Haunted Castle). Celebrating 6 years of SNES-mix uploads (5 years on YouTube specifically) with arranging the song that would be my first ever mix uploaded onto YouTube. I thought it'd be fun to go back and do another "re-remix" of an old mix of mine, though this time, I'd base it off both the Haunted Castle & Aria of Sorrow versions rather than basing it off just Haunted Castle's version.

I have plans to do more "re-remixes" of some very old tracks in the future, and this is one of my first ones I'll be doing.

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, Yoshi SFX, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. D Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. E Minor (Remix I Pitch)
ㅤ3. C Minor (NES Pitch)
ㅤ4. D# Minor (Whip Rush!! Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Original Echo Delay, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (OG Echo)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Decreased Echo Delay, but disables outro (DISABLES Outro)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ3. Drastically Decreased Echo Delay (LOWER Echo)

versions.title: Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow - Whip, Cross, & Justice!! ✝️ ~ Don't Wait Until Night x Heart of Fire (Remix II)

packages.name: smwmusic-castlevania-bloodlines-bane-of-tepes-theme-of-simon-remix
packages.title: Castlevania: Bloodlines - Bane of Tepes ~ Theme of Simon (Remix)
packages.description:
Been a while since I last did a Castlevania theme, so I decided to remix Theme of Simon from Castlevania: Bloodlines. Not a fan of Super Castlevania IV, but am a big fan of Bloodlines and its version of Simon Belmondo'st's theme. This ended up being one of my more fun remixes to work on, but it also took quite a while to do.

This baby can fit in castle / tower stages, industrial stages, final areas, intense cutscenes, and even second phase final boss fights.

Important:
- "Bonus End," Yoshi, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also 2 customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. G Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. F# Minor (Custom Pitch)

versions.title: Castlevania: Bloodlines - Bane of Tepes ~ Theme of Simon (Remix)

This is a arrangement of Iron Blue Intention from Castlevania Bloodlines, which is also Eric Lecarde's theme according to a lot of fans and even Konami themselves.

Use this if you need a epic final level or castle; the tubular bells at the beginning really fit well with the finality of this theme IMHO (tho it's Jorge D. Fuentes you should thank for that, not me lmao), so I think it would definitely be used well in this setting.

packages.name: smwmusic-castlevania-bloodlines-machine-turn-back-now-iron-blue-intention-remix
packages.title: Castlevania: Bloodlines - Machine, Turn Back Now! ~ Iron Blue Intention (Remix)
packages.description:
Did an arrangement of Iron Blue Intention from Castlevania: Bloodlines. It's been a couple years since I last did a song from this game (and it wasn't even from Bloodlines in particular), so I'm doing the dedicated "clock tower" stage theme from this game.

A really sick track. Not my favorite song from the game, but one that I really do like, especially the stage it's used in (and especially the cool-ass boss at the end of the stage)
ㅤ
Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. B Minor (Remix Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. D Minor (Original Pitch)
ㅤ3. C# Minor (Custom Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Default Echo Delay, but sacrifices Yoshi SFX (Default Echo Delay)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. Decreases Echo Delay (Lower Echo Delay)

versions.title: Castlevania: Bloodlines - Machine, Turn Back Now! ~ Iron Blue Intention (Remix)

packages.description:
Did a remix of New Messiah from Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge. Promised myself that I'd do more Castlevania remixes (the jingles I did don't count) since the last song I did was Don't Wait Until the Night, and that was right before my music actually started to get better. I haven't played the Gameboy Castlevania games that much, but I have listened to New Messiah quite a bit, and it's actually a pretty good track, so I thought I'd remix that for this time. Only took me a couple hours to do surprisingly.

This song is perfect for castle, factory, castle grounds, and tower stages.

Important:
There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."
- @7, Thunder, and Yoshi SFX are disabled.

packages.description:
𝕾𝖙𝖎𝖑𝖑 𝖚𝖙𝖙𝖊𝖗𝖎𝖓𝖌 𝖙𝖍𝖊 𝖘𝖆𝖒𝖊 𝖓𝖔𝖓𝖘𝖊𝖓𝖘𝖊. 𝕹𝖔 𝖒𝖆𝖙𝖙𝖊𝖗. 𝕹𝖔𝖜 𝖎𝖘 𝖙𝖍𝖊 𝖙𝖎𝖒𝖊 𝖙𝖔 𝖕𝖚𝖙 𝖆𝖘𝖎𝖉𝖊 𝖞𝖔𝖚𝖗 𝖜𝖊𝖆𝖐 𝖍𝖚𝖒𝖆𝖓 𝖘𝖎𝖉𝖊, 𝖆𝖓𝖉 𝖏𝖔𝖎𝖓 𝖒𝖊 𝖎𝖓 𝖗𝖊𝖒𝖆𝖐𝖎𝖓𝖌 𝖙𝖍𝖎𝖘 𝖜𝖔𝖗𝖑𝖉!


Bloody Tears from Worst Metroidvania ever Castlevania II: Simon's Quest. Since everyone seems to like porting the Super Castlevania IV version more than the original, I had to do my part and give you guys my rendition of the original song. Nothing way too extreme, but nothing simple either.

This song could fit intense castle levels, fast-paced levels, dark levels, and maybe even some bosses

Note: There's a !!! READ ME !!!.txt file which has the sample bank for the song. You need to copy that over to Addmusic_sample groups.txt or else the song will not work. Also you go into the song file, you can adjust the pitch to five different options that are on there: a# minor (Default), b minor (Hyper-Realistic by Lui37), a minor (Custom one but I call it "Mega Man"), g minor (I think it's custom, but I call it anyways "Touhou" because it's always about Touhou!), and f minor (Super Castlevania IV).

Also shoutouts to @springhakurei "Jeto" on twitter. Jeto makes some awesome / kawaii art on Small Richter, Touhou girls, and a lotta Simon... and I mean a lot.

packages.description:
This is the theme that plays when you're fighting Richter Belmont, the game's fake final boss, in Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. This is a very final-like song, but it's also a very weird and "janky" one, thanks to the 5/8 time signature this song is mostly in, which, along with the overall strong presence of dissonance, gives off a very great sense of unsettlement and tragedy to the battle itself, to differentiate from other final boss themes.

We all know how iconic it is! It's the first thing you hear once you enter Dracula's doors into his newest and most biggest castle (at the time). It's such an amazing theme song for the amazing game that changed the world forever!!!

Hooded's Obsessive Shilling Over Dead Cells & Why You Should Play It
Dead Cells is a must-play for any Castlevania, Metroidvania, and Rogue-lite fans. It's an underrated masterpiece that continues to be a better live-service than every live-service game out there (w/o even being a real live-service game in the first-place) w/ constant updates adding new content to the already-finished game. Its combat is fluent, its level design is perfect, its atmosphere is tense and Castlevania-like, IT'S ALL PERFECT, AND YOU SHOULD PLAY IT!!!

SERIOUSLY! WHAT ARE YOU DOING WITH YOUR LIFE RIGHT NOW?!?! GO BUY IT!!! PLZ!!! IT'S SO FREAKING AMAZING!!!

❝ 𝐖𝐞𝐚𝐩𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐀𝐫𝐞 𝐍𝐨𝐭 𝐌𝐞𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐓𝐚𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐎𝐟 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐬. 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲’𝐫𝐞 𝐌𝐞𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐅𝐨𝐫 𝐒𝐚𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦. ❞
ㅤ- Melchior, 1995

Did an arrangement of Battle 1 from Chrono Trigger in memory of Akira Toriyama. Not often I do something like this, but as fan of Chrono Trigger and huge fan of Akira Toriyama's work & art, I thought it'd be great to dedicate this one to him.

Chrono Trigger's Battle theme is one of my favorite battle themes in any RPG

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi SFX, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. D Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. C Minor (Custom Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Default Echo Delay, but sacrifices the P-Switch Jingle & @9 is replaced with @0 (Default Echo Delay)
ㅤ2. Decreases Echo Delay (Lower Echo Delay)ㅤ[turned on by default]

packages.name: smwmusic-civilization-snes-title-theme
packages.title: Civilization (SNES) - Title Theme
packages.description:
A practically identical re-creation of the title music from the SNES port of the classic game we all know and love, Sid Meier's Civilization. It's worth noting that the SNES version of the game had an entirely original soundtrack composed in-house at Koei, so this tune is not present in other versions of the game. The original composer is unknown.

This song could work well in an epic/dramatic cutscene, as well as (obviously) the title screen of your hack. Due to the climactic and triumphant nature of the track, it may also work near the game's ending. A few people on Discord said that it would be fit for use in a kaizo hack, as well.

0 - Default in-game version
1 - In-game version but with the addition of the drum intro from CTR Nitro-Fueled (0x0AD5)

packages.name: smwmusic-crash-nitro-kart-main-theme

0 - Normal version, plays on the main menu
1 - XBox version of the menu theme, which is slightly longer by featuring an extended bassline (0:39, 0x03DE)
2 - Opening version, has an intro and an extension, this port is slightly different than the original version as that version features an abridged version of the main motif that gets mixed with the intro voices, and this version keeps it on the same length as the menu versions (1:04, 0x04EC)

Note: the normal OST version is incompatible with thunder, blargg and Yoshi sound effects and the vanilla bonus end jingle. This is not the case for the alternate variation which replaces the pizzicato with the guitar.

packages.name: smwmusic-crystalized-fractal-realm
packages.title: Crystalized Fractal Realm
packages.description:
Some of you wondered whether or not the Crystal Castle was the ghost house theme... well, no. This is actually the one I intended as the ghost house theme. And this is when you get lost in this hall of mirrors... lots of reflections, but which is the real one?

NOTE: Given how long the song is in the first place (longer than 999 seconds to SMW's standard), a ghost house with no timer would probably work best for this particular song... or use a 16-bit timer patch.

NOTE: The Hurry Up! effect may not appear to speed up all sections of the song, mostly due to lag-related effects from me using a high tempo to minimize staccato (in addition to using light staccato in the first place) as well as usually using volume fades across all of the channels in at least one case. The nature of the song tends to mitigate the usual lag-related gotchas, though, as usually the lag is occurring in the sections where the volume fades are occurring on all of the channels in one go, subsequently meaning that the lag ends when the fades stop occurring on all of the channels at once, which is neatly timed to the end of a section as well.

packages.name: smwmusic-deltarune-faint-courage
packages.title: Deltarune - Faint Courage
packages.description:
This is not
your fate...!

Please,
don't give up!

Come on,
that all you got!?

Kris,
get up...!

----------

This is the Game Over theme for Deltarune chapters 2 and onward!

For once, I have actually completed one of my 7 bazillion WIPs.

I don't really see this working practically as anything more than a game-over theme, and I wouldn't advise against using it as anything else either as channels #6 and #7 do have noticeable audio in them. I might fix it at a later time but for now I'm more or less satisfied with this.

I tried to go for a chiptune-ish sounding beginning like Deltarune has then transitioning it to use more instruments and panning in the second half.

I hope to do more Deltarune and Undertale music in the future! Though theres a lot of unique sounds and instruments that I'm having trouble replicating with default samples.

----------

THEN THE WORLD
WAS COVERED
IN DARKNESS.

packages.description:
❝ 𝐍𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐈 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫, 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐢𝐬 𝐦𝐲 𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐫

Did an arrangement of Crocodile Cacophony from the GREATEST GAME EVER MADE!! Did his first theme song last year, so I HAVE TO do his true theme song!!! Took heavy inspiration from both the original and Smash renditions.

Important:
ㅤ♠ What's disabled:
ㅤㅤ - "Bonus End" (@7)
ㅤㅤ - Thunder SFX

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. G Major (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ2. A Major (Croc Isle Pitch)
ㅤ3. G# Major (Finest Hour Pitch)
ㅤ4. F Major (Custom Pitch 1)
ㅤ5. F# Major (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Original Volume Level (OG Volume)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Decreased Volume Level (LOWER Volume)ㅤ[turned on by default]

packages.name: smwmusic-donkey-kong-country-x-touhou-koumakyou-the-embodiment-of-the-scarlet-devil-roses-n-kruelty-gang-plank-galleon-x-u-n-owen-was-her-remix
packages.title: Donkey Kong Country x Touhou Koumakyou ~ the Embodiment of the Scarlet Devil - Roses 'N Kruelty 🌹 ~ Gang-Plank Galleon x U.N. Owen was Her? (Remix)
packages.description:
❝ Right, I've had enough of this. It's time for me to get going. So you Kongs better get off of my ship or else! ❞
ㅤ- King K. Rool, Donkey Kong Country [GBA] (2003)


Did a mashup arrangement of King KAROOL's theme song Gang-Plank Galleon x Flandre Skarlet's theme song U.N. Owen Was Her? from Donkey Kong Country & Touhou 6 Koumakyou ~ the Embodiment of the Skarlet Devil, respektively. Two krazies, two bangers, one psykhotic mix!! This was a mix I planned for at the beginning of the year and, of kourse, expekted it to be one of my more ambitious ones.

Given this mashup's entire premise, I primarily wanted to primarily base this remix off the Smash Ultimate version of K. Rool's theme (given the pace of that version matches up with Flan's theme) while also retaining elements of the original.

Important:

Did an arrangement of Challengers from Dragon Ball Z: Budokai. Just got into Dragon Ball recently and binged through the entirety of OG Dragon Ball, DBZ Kai, and DB Super, and I thought it'd be fun to make a mix of one of the series best themes, and there's no better song to choose than the one I've been listening to way WAY before I got into this series!!

Hooded Edge rambling on about this theme
I LOVE THIS THEME!! Challengers is easily one of my favorite fighting game themes of all-time, and, other than Makafushigi Adventure, this is one other song I primarily think of when it comes to Dragon Ball music. I thought it'd work incredibly well with Sanae's theme from Touhou 10: Mountain of Faith, Faith is for the Transient (I swear, her theme song goes well with nothing but absolute bangers like MM2 Wily's Castle & this song).

I actually remember first hearing this song in a Sonic 1 romhack, Mobius Evolution, and that was years ago, and it was even used as a Super theme in that game too.

packages.description:
*A S C E N D S*


Did an arrangement of The Moon stage theme from DuckTales. What can I even say about this track that hasn't been said before. It's easily Disney's most iconic theme they had in any video game of theirs renditions of musicial numbers from the movies don't count. It's been arranged so much to the point where goddamn Jake Kaufman had to cough up a banger arrangement for the remake. It's one of my favorite songs on the NES, especially from a game I generally enjoyed when I was younger.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. F# Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. F Minor (Custom Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. Enables Voice Clip, but at the cost of the P-Switch & Thunder SFX
2. Disables Voice Clip (turned on default)

packages.name: smwmusic-endless-determination

packages.description:
My first remix of my own composition (or I guess technically you can call this it's own composition, in which case, this is the fifth finished one).

After re-listening to Endless Nights I wondered if I can make it more boss battle themed and the result was this!

Some parts were from compositions that didn't go anywhere, like the intro, so I reused them, since they fit well here.

Was made to be used in boss battles, but I could also see its use in chase levels or intense castles with lasers.

packages.name: smwmusic-f-zero-life-in-the-azure-lane-big-blue-remix
packages.title: F-Zero - Life in the Azure Lane ~ Big Blue (Remix)
packages.description:
Show me ya moves!

Did an arrangement of Big Blue from F-ZERO. One of the best racing themes in the history of racers and my favorite F-ZERO & Mario Kart theme (Rainbow Road Themes don't got anything against Big Blue). As someone who grew up playing a ton of the original F-ZERO, I fell in love with this track immediately after I played through Big Blue for the first time.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi, P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. A# Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. B Minor (F-ZERO X Pitch)
3. A Minor (Mario Kart 8 Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. Enables Voice Clip, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility
2. Disables Voice Clip & lowers echo (turned on default)

packages.name: smwmusic-f-zero-silence
packages.title: F-Zero - Silence
packages.description:
My goal for 2019 is to upload more music and generally be more active... and possibly have a shot at mosts!

This is Silence, a moody piece from the original F-Zero that debuted on the SNES in 1990, 1991, and 1992 in Japan, America, and Europe respectively. It's probably one of my favorite games... Great soundtrack, and you get to slam into walls at over 3 times the interstate speed limit and uh, die... While listening to some really catchy music! Even the music that plays after you die is great

Unlike the song's name implies, there is no actual silence. It starts out rather calm, but then the second part of it drops into something less calm that would definitely fit an exciting level.

Accuracy was not in mind when I made this song!

packages.description:
❝ Die like your father, you pin-headed son of an ice cream maker! ❞
ㅤ- Geese Howard, Fatal Fury Special (1993)



Did an arrangement of the one and only, Soy Sauce for Geese from the Fatal Fury franchise. I've been getting into Fatal Fury / King of Fighters recently (they're really great games), and I thought I'd dedicate an arrangement to the one and only Howard Geese's theme 'cuz it is exactly what people say it is: A BANGER!!!

This song has always been fascinating to me because of its fusion of hard rock and honkyoku music that's made the song iconic and also fitting for Geese's character (as gaming's first American Weeb).

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, Yoshi SFX, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. C Minor w/ Slight Detune (Remix Pitch)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. C Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ3. A Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
ㅤ4. C# Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Enables the voice clip, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (Voice Enabled)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Disables the voice clip & Decreases the Echo (Voice Disabled)ㅤ[turned on by default]

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Original Echo Delay, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (OG Echo)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Decreased Echo Delay, but removes the intro (DISABLES Intro)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ3. DRASTICALLY Decreased Echo Delay (LOWER Echo)

packages.description:
𝓢𝓽𝓪𝓻𝓴𝓵𝓮, 𝓼𝓽𝓪𝓻𝓴𝓵𝓮 𝓵𝓲𝓽𝓽𝓵𝓮 𝓽𝔀𝓲𝓷𝓴... 𝓝𝓸𝔀 𝓲𝓽'𝓼 𝓽𝓲𝓶𝓮 𝓽𝓱𝓪𝓽 𝔂𝓸𝓾 𝓰𝓾𝔂𝓼 𝓢𝓘𝓝𝓚!!
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ- Gilgamesh, 1992

Did a special arrangement of Battle on the Big Bridge from for my 6K SUBSCRIBER MILESTONE!!!

It's not only my favorite song in Final Fantasy 5, but also my favorite song in the entire franchise. Shoutout to FINAL FANTASY Record Keeper] for having the best version of the song period (and also being a great reference to use for this port).

Super Castlevania IV fake-ass Trumpet jumpscare. lmao

packages.name: smwmusic-final-fantasy-vi-born-from-chaos-dancing-mad-part
packages.title: Final Fantasy VI - Born From Chaos ~ Dancing Mad (Part 5) (Remix)
packages.description:
❝ 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐞... 𝐃𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐬... 𝐇𝐨𝐩𝐞... 𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦? 𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐝𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐠𝐨...? 𝐒𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐦𝐞𝐚𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬... 𝐈'𝐥𝐥 𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐦 𝐚𝐥𝐥! ❞
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ- Kefka Palazzo, 1994

Did a special arrangement of Dancing Mad (Part 5) from Final Fantasy VI. A special request from Daizo Dee Von for his hack ~OMH~. Easily one of my favorite final battle themes in the series and also one of the hardest tracks I had to work on. Either way, it was a ton of fun to do!!

credit to Tamaki and their port for the Kefka laughing sound.

Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. C# Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. C Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. B Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Voice Clip [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. Disables Voice Clip

versions.title: Final Fantasy VI - Born From Chaos ~ Dancing Mad (Part 5) (Remix)

packages.description:
Did an arrangement of The Decisive Battle from Final Fantasy VI, aka one of the most popular songs in the entirety of RPGs. Easily my favorite track from this fantastic OST / Game and my favorite decisive battle theme in the series bars none. This was definitely in my to-dos for Final Fantasy arrangements, and I went all out on this one like every other song I do. I love this soundtrack so much, and I hope more people get to listen to it (and play the game too)!!

packages.name: smwmusic-final-fantasy-vii-mako-reactor
packages.title: Final Fantasy VII - Mako Reactor
packages.description:
The deeply menacing theme representing the Mako Factory from Final Fantasy VII, or as I like to call it "Magitek Research Facility's Younger Brother". Not accurate to the original due to not having the proper samples, so I used some of my own ones. Since I really like the Remake version, I included a small nod to it that plays every second loop if you enable it using the define "LOOP2" (see txt for details). If it's disabled, the size will decrease to 0x042D and the real length will be 1:35.

Includes the option to enable/disable staccato with the staccato define. With it enabled, the size will decrease to 0x05C6 (which really isn't much). If this is enabled along with LOOP2 disabled, it will become 0x0467.

This submission accounts for the max size and length using the various defines.

Song not compatible with P-switch, Bonus End, Thunder, Yoshi, or Blarggs.

Edit: Wrong notes been corrected (to the best of my abilities), tho I kept in the "wrong intro notes" as an option in the "ACCURATE" define because I unironically liked it better. Nameless is the one to thank for pointing where I made mistakes. With ACCURATE disabled (setting it to 1), it'll add 3 extra bytes.

packages.description:
Ported by request.

6 custom samples (8.89KiB) based on the original ones. The flute is original due to not being able to find a decent version of the original sample, and a square wave was layered over the e-piano sample to reduce polyphony.

Tweaked the envelopes and echo a fair bit from the original, because IMHO, the original was a bit choppy, making it a bit annoying to listen to for extended periods of time.

Re-uploaded for improvements: Saved 181 bytes(!), swapped pizzicato (now in Ch6) with a string channel (now in Ch7), and starting to place all my samples into a single folder.

"We're getting to 6:00 AM with this one."

The iconic theme heard when your grandfather clock dials it's chimes. It's also used in the hit indie game "Chipper & Sons Lumber Co." by Scott Cawthon, amongst a few others-less popular-titles.

There are two versions: one specifically used in ~omh~, and one that's compatible with global (lacks any echo, and uses more channels to recreate it). You CAN use the ~omh~ one with echo as a victory theme if you just use it as a local song and set the death theme to the song number in asm/SNES/tweaks.asm.

The ~omh~ version is 0x0097, while the global version is 0x00E0.

If the goal define is 0, the size decreases to 0x005A for ~omh~, while it'll decrease to 0x009D for global.

packages.name: smwmusic-fortress-of-artificial-fabrication
packages.title: Fortress of Artificial Fabrication
packages.description:
Time to infiltrate this place. What are they making here?

This song, which I originally revealed in Super Famicompo 2, actually has a pretty long history. It was originally created on 7/11/12 for something that I never submitted. The biggest thing about it is that it wasn't actual SNES music, but generally speaking it used soundfonts from various games. I revived it after doing some volume balancing, intending on submitting it for the first Super Famicompo, but picked the wrong song by mistake (which was something I prototyped for the same thing). Thus, this instead came out for the second Super Famicompo, which in turn caused me to get contacted about this song being ported shortly after the compo concluded.

I have redone the port myself, mostly to take advantage of more modern techniques that were previously not possible on earlier AddmusicK versions. Plus, the overall filesize is smaller as a result of doing this... well, at least the song data is smaller.

WARNING: This song has multiple stock sample substitutions due to memory constraints, and has a set of sample groups that should be added to the Addmusic_sample groups.txt file to facilitate this. These affect the following:
  • Miss song (uses a non-stock sample)
  • P-Switch song
  • All Thunder-based SFX (including Blargg and affecting $1DF9 SFX IDs $21, $25, $27, $29 and $1DFC SFX IDs $1A, $2C) ($1DFC SFX ID $1A (the Castle Destruction Bomb SFX) is not recommended, mostly because it's quite a bit more reliant on the original sample than the others, being a single note)
  • Yoshi SFX ($1DFC SFX ID $1F) and Bonus End song (uses a non-stock sample)

packages.name: smwmusic-ghouls-n-ghosts-amiga-title-screen
packages.title: Ghouls 'n Ghosts (Amiga) - Title Screen
packages.description:
Acoustic guitar-heavy title screen music from the Amiga version of Ghouls 'n Ghosts.

The custom loop version is made in order for the song to loop smoothly, being intended for levels, and it's slightly smaller than the full version (0x0739 bytes). The full version is more for cutscenes and whatnot.

In the full version's text files, there is a #define LOOPABLE. It's set to 1 by default, and when it's set to 0, it will not loop back to the beginning at all, it'll just be still when the song comes to an end.

Incompatible with @7 (bonus end fanfare) and thunder sound effect.
The full version will omit one of the samples under the following defines:
-#define P_SWITCH 1 will enable P-Switch sample and omit Yoshi sample.
-#define P_SWITCH 0 (or other number) will be vice versa.

UPDATE: Corrected a few notes, as well as updating the overdriven guitar sample.

packages.name: smwmusic-goanimate-dance
packages.title: GoAnimate - Dance
packages.description:
Jokes aside, GoAnimate (now known as Vyond) is you guessed it! A website that allows you to animate using drag and drop, even having themes that allow you to create custom characters (e.g. Comedy Worlds, Lil' Peepz, Chibi Peepz, etc.).

It was intended to be an easier and quicker alternative to tools such as Flash, and although initially obscure, it suddenly became popular in the mid-2010s, and nope, it's not because of its easy to use nature, it's not because of one theme (Comedy World) being themed after Family Guy, no no no, it's because of, as mentioned in the picture above, those infamous "you are grounded grounded grounded" videos, often featuring characters from preschool shows such as Caillou, Barney the Dinosaur, Dora the Explorer, Elmo, being you know... grounded, often for literal eternity, sometimes for minor things or even nothing. And don't forget those infamous rant videos featuring terms such as "[subject]? What, more like [mock name]! Oh my god, this [thing] sucks", "they like to go on failure adventures together", "Do you know who likes/hates this [thing]", "[subject] sucks, and so does [another subject]! [yet another subject] is [long number] times better than [subject]!", etc.

Basically, what used to be an easy-to-use animation tool ended up becoming Gen Z brainrot. In order to appeal to businesses (which contrary to popular belief, is NOT because of the grounded videos), the site became subscription-based and eventually changed its name in 2018 to the aforementioned Vyond, but by that point, the damage has already been done, and the site ended up creating one of the largest internet rabbit holes in history, full of kids who try hating preschool shows just to look "cool and mature" (or at least try to, since they're mostly the exact opposite), and videos that are so bad, they're good.



Basically, for those who are wondering, yes, the site did offer MIDI music in its early days, alongside some non-MIDI music.

Good for industrial levels, overworlds and cutscenes.

packages.name: smwmusic-hall-of-mirrors
packages.title: Hall Of Mirrors
packages.description:
Welcome to the null and void, where you and everything within will leave behind their own afterimages... oh wait, the SNES normally doesn't do this. Nevertheless, you may have noticed that some time ago I started using a game name of "Hall Of Mirrors Effect" for a few of my songs as part of an indirect series of songs. This is the titular song, and it also compliments the Strange Hub song via the same utilization of the Legend of Zelda: A Link To The Past's Mirror song sample (though the quality was increased somewhat), as well as some instrument samples straight out of the song for extra flavor.

Contains four user defines: one is a master echo enable switch, and a second one enables it for the music. Echo for SFX (though I tuned it so that the effect doesn't go too far into the seemingly endless), within the context of AddmusicK 1.0.10, the latest moderated version at the time of this release, (which still requires the master echo enable switch to be on) is handled through 1DFA commands $05 and $06: use 1DFA command $06 right after the song starts to enable echo for SFX. A third one enables all of the panning commands (without them, the song is in mono), and the last one enables a surround effect. The latter also requires panning to be enabled in order to be used.
