packages.description:
𝕯𝖗𝖆𝖈𝖚𝖑𝖆. 𝕯𝖎𝖊 𝖓𝖔𝖜, 𝖆𝖓𝖉 𝖑𝖊𝖆𝖛𝖊 𝖙𝖍𝖎𝖘 𝖜𝖔𝖗𝖑𝖉! 𝖄𝖔𝖚'𝖑𝖑 𝖓𝖊𝖛𝖊𝖗 𝖇𝖊𝖑𝖔𝖓𝖌 𝖍𝖊𝖗𝖊!

A remix of the last stage theme in the Haunted Castle arcade game, Don't Wait Until The Night (which is also heard in the battle against Julius Belmont in Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow.

This song works best in castles, factories, towers, final areas, & other levels with intense vibes.

Note:
There is a ADD ME TO ADDMUSICK.txt file that has the sample bank that you need to move to Addmusic_sample_groups.txt. Thunder and Yoshi sound effects are disabled.
There are two customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song file:
- e minor (the default pitch specifically for this remix)
- d minor (The original pitch from the games)

versions.title: Haunted Castle - Last Belmont Standing ~ Don't Wait Until The Night (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-haunted-castle-order-of-the-holy-spirit-cross-your-heart-remix
packages.title: Haunted Castle - Order of the Holy Spirit ~ Cross Your Heart (Remix)
packages.description:
𝖂𝖍𝖆𝖙 𝖆 𝖍𝖔𝖗𝖗𝖎𝖇𝖑𝖊 𝖓𝖎𝖌𝖍𝖙 𝖙𝖔 𝖍𝖆𝖛𝖊 𝖆 𝖈𝖚𝖗𝖘𝖊!

This is an arrangement Cross Your Heart, the first stage theme from Konami's Castlevania arcade game Haunted Castle. I had this song stuck in my head for about a week and decided to let it out of my head and into a port.

This song can fit castle, factories, towers, and intense levels / scenarios.

Note:
There is a !! Read Me!!.txt file that has the sample bank that you need to move to Addmusic_sample_groups.txt. Thunder and Yoshi sound effects are disabled.
There are three customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song file:
- f# minor (The default pitch from the original game)
- g minor (Based on Crucifix Held Close from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin)
- e minor (A custom pitch that I thought sounded pretty cool for this song)

If you haven't already, check out Ultima's arrangement of Crucifix Held Close, a similar song from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin. It's a well-crafted arrangement that some may prefer over this one if you liked that version better than what Haunted Castle had to offer.

mod note: the $EE command used in versions 1 and 2 detunes certain sound effects very slightly.

versions.title: Haunted Castle - Order of the Holy Spirit ~ Cross Your Heart (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-hebereke-no-oishii-puzzle-wa-irimasen-ka-crossword
packages.title: Hebereke no Oishii Puzzle wa Irimasen ka - Crossword
packages.description:
Hebereke no Oishii Puzzle wa Irimasen ka, for those curious, is just the SNES version of the Sunsoft arcade game Oishii Puzzle wa Irimasen ka, but this time featuring characters from Sunsoft's Hebereke video game series. It's basically a party game consisting of you guessed it, puzzle mini games.

This song plays during the Crossword mini game, which NGL, is a HUGE language barrier, as obviously, that game was never released outside of Japan, and there isn't even a fan translation yet.

Note that this game uses Opus's "SQ & DBOOT" sound driver (undoubtedly the second most used sound driver on Super Famicom games, only behind Nintendo's Kankichi-kun/N-SPC sound driver; it was even used in the first-party game Mario's Super Picross), which is infamous for constantly shuffling channels during song playback, and because of that, porting songs from games using that sound driver would be a complete nightmare.

Therefore, I had to recreate the entire song from scratch, using the original instruments, samples, volumes, panning and echo, but without shuffling the channels this time, although fortunately, there aren't any notable inaccuracies in this port that I could find.

Good for puzzle levels, overworlds and cutscenes.

versions.title: Hebereke no Oishii Puzzle wa Irimasen ka - Crossword
versions.filename: Hebereke no Oishii Puzzle wa Irimasen ka - Crossword.zip

packages.name: smwmusic-icrawfish-walls-that-are-still-called-home
packages.title: icrawfish - Walls That Are Still Called Home
packages.description:
My submission for 120hoSPC #12, a remix of icrawfish's Walls That Were Once Called Home, which won 3rd place.

The song tells of a familiar place, where many a memory continues to be made; though it'll one day be but a memory, it's still here and whole today, time not having made its mark yet. Tangible as these might be, these cozy walls are often taken for granted. I think we all have these kinds of places, and they might slip away as time goes on, so this remix serves as a celebration of those places, and a reminder to cherish those feelings and memories, right here right now!

packages.name: smwmusic-ikachan-battle-inside-water
packages.title: Ikachan - Battle Inside Water
packages.description:
A really energectic, and upbeat remix of a calm, and happy song from Ikachan.
Man, this one was really challenging to remix, considering how this original theme's so peaceful, to make something really tense and upbeat. However, it was really worth the result it become in the end, am happy with what I've done.

Anyway, this remix's based on both the original Mizuno, AND this early version as well, found on the early OrgView files, named as "mizu[水の中で].mid", which was where I based off the string parts, this mix's pitch, and other small things, that I worked on.

packages.name: smwmusic-ikachan-magirete
packages.title: Ikachan - Magirete
packages.description:
A cute song, used on the controls screen of Ikachan. It was apparently also a theme song for Pixel's dev room.

It does uses the KDL3 soundfont.

There's a plenty of define options for this song, where two of them fast forward, or slow downs the song (and pitch), and an option for make the percussions audible again (as the original puts them all the way down to volume 1, for some reason). If you want either of those options, open the text file, and change one of those define values, by anything other than 0.

Original description by Pixel
Original:
○雨に紛れて：開発室Pixelのテーマ曲だった。
Rough translation:
• Behind the rain: It was the theme song of the development room Pixel.

packages.description:
Inside the Machine, a composition composed for Super Famicompo 4. It ranked 7th place in the 'Originals' category.

Did a special arrangement of IOSYS's Cirno's Perfect Math Class (which is a famous arrangement of Cirno's theme in Touhou 6, Beloved Tomboyish Girl) for a special event that's happening in September. It's . Another banger song to have arranged, and it's another remix based off another remix.

As someone who's not a fan of a majority of IOSYS's "meme" (I don't know how else to describe them) songs, I genuinely really like this one, especially given how much more upbeat this one is. Always been a fan of 2000s internet culture, and this is one of the reasons why.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi, P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. D Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. C Minor (Chill Penguin Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. Enables Voice Clip, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility
2. Disables Voice Clip & Lowers Echo Buffer (turned on default)

I would've liked to have captured more of the counter-melody that the original has going on, what with this being a song about two people and all, but I'm still content with how it came out.

packages.name: smwmusic-jojo-s-bizarre-adventure-battle-tendency-divine-hamon-bloody-stream-remix
packages.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Battle Tendency - Divine Hamon ~ Bloody Stream (Remix)
packages.description:
𝐍𝐢𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐲𝐨!!!

Did an arrangement of Bloody Stream from Jojo's Bizarre Adventure (Part 2): Battle Tendency. Had this on my mind for months ever since I did that Chase remix but never had the guts to do it until now. Sick opening theme and was my first favorite before hearing everything else and this... dropping from first to fifth (Chase, Crazy Noisy Bizarre Town, Sono Chi No Sadame, and Stand Proud beat it for me). Funny enough, it also reminds me way too much of Divine Bloodlines and Septette for the Dead Princess (should be no surprise to anyone who knows how much I love both songs).

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There's also an option to enable or disable the loop in the song file with an ending like in the OP:
1. Loop (turned on by default)
2. No Loop (like in the original)

versions.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Battle Tendency - Divine Hamon ~ Bloody Stream (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-jojo-s-bizarre-adventure-diamond-is-unbreakable-chase-opening
packages.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Diamond is Unbreakable - Chase ~ Opening 2 (Remix)
packages.description:
𝐕𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐢𝐬 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐛𝐲 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲. 𝐓𝐡𝐚𝐭'𝐬 𝐰𝐡𝐲 𝐈'𝐥𝐥 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐲𝐨𝐮.

Yes, I did a remix of Chase from Jojo's Bizarre Adventure (Part 4): Diamond is Unbreakable. You're not seeing things. It's my favorite of the Jojo OP themes and is by far one of the most underrated ones in the series. The hard rock combined with the deep emotion set piece really sets the mood for the entire song. Note, this isn't the actual full song and is just based on the OP version, since doing the full song would take up so much ARAM.

This baby can fit title screens, credits, [final] boss fights, intense stages, final areas, and castle / towers stages.

Important:
There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."
- "Bonus End" is disabled.

There's also an option to enable or disable the loop in the song file with an ending like in the OP:
1. Loops the song (turned on by default).
2. No Loop

versions.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Diamond is Unbreakable - Chase ~ Opening 2 (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-jungle-village
packages.title: Jungle Village
packages.description:
Here's a potential jungle-esque level theme from my archives.

Welcome to the archival series! This was created for a conceptual SNES homebrew project (yes, a homebrew project, not a Super Mario World romhack) that I was going to create all the way back in 2007-2008 or so... well... until I lost most of the music in a hard drive crash, and subsequently the iteration is mostly lost except for a few songs that were created on the G3, of which this is one of them. These songs were never authentic SNES music in the first place, mostly because they pre-date SNESMod's entire existence and also pre-date my ability to compile the tools (XMSNES did exist, though, which was by the same author). And on your side, to my knowledge you really only had Addmusic Java to work with, to put in perspective how long ago this was. Therefore, until recently, these songs were never properly checked for sample filesize in particular and thus were never ported over. This one was initially done on 10/7/07.

WARNING: This song is not compatible with the speed-up effect of the Hurry Up! SFX. This is mostly because the main sample backing used here is tempo sensitive.

packages.description:
Port of a beaultiful and mystical composition written by Kil, played in the famous Talkhaus collab hack A Super Mario Thing, in 2010.
It's played on the "Trial of Iron" level, in one of the first teleports.


Define option
How this song was written during an old era of Addmusic, it does uses an older version of @2, where it does sound quite different from the modern / default versions. Knowing that, there's an option to use this older @2 sample, or use the SMW default @2 sample. If you want to use this older @2 sample (for whatever reason), open the text file, and change the "Use_Older_@2" define value to anything, other than 0.

packages.description:
❝ 𝐇𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐬𝐞𝐥𝐟 𝐚 𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐲 𝐇𝐨𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐡𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐦𝐚𝐬! ❞

You all have been nice this Christmas, so you're getting a special arrangement of Frozen Hillside from Kirby Air Ride (ft. way too many songs). Been addicted to Kirby Air Riders for the past few weeks, and I thought it'd be sick to make my X-MAS SPECIAL SNES-MIX another Kirby Mashup. Thought it'd be neat to turn Frozen Hillside into a rock-inspired track heavily inspired by Ruined Castle Corridor & Silver Wolf (from Castlevania: Harmony of Despair & Mega Man Zero 2 respectively).

I never really liked this song growing up, but I've grown to appreciate it way more after playing Kirby Air Riders recently to where it's one of my favorite race track themes from the game.

packages.name: smwmusic-kirby-s-return-to-dreamland-border-of-life-fly-kirby-remix
packages.title: Kirby's Return To Dreamland - Border Of Life ~ Fly, Kirby! (Remix)
packages.description:
Bravo, Kirby. You've truly earned your reputation as a hero.

Did an arrangement of Fly, Kirby! (Another Dimension) from Kirby's Return To Dreamland, one of my favorite games on the Wii (alongside Epic Yarn) and in the series. Wanted to do this for a while to celebrate Kirby's Return To Dreamland Deluxe, but I had a better idea to do it for an April Fools joke special instead. It's one of my favorite songs in the game and is easily the best shoot-em-up stage theme in the series (this is a hill I will die on).

Joke
Ninjitsu Art of Duplication!

Did an arrangement of Border Of Life from Touhou 7: Perfect Cherry Blossom. Ngl, not a big fan of the original song, so I thought I'd base this arrangement off the one in Kirby's Return to Dreamland. It's so cool ZUN gave Jun Ishikawa the rights to arrange the song 'cuz he made it even better than before!!!


Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi, P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. G Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. F# Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. F Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Voice Clip, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. Disables Voice Clip [turned on default]

versions.title: Kirby's Return To Dreamland - Border Of Life ~ Fly, Kirby! (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-kirby-super-star-ultra-vengeance-the-mask-s-awakening-masked-dedede-remix
packages.title: Kirby Super Star Ultra - Vengeance, The Mask's Awakening ~ Masked Dedede (Remix)
packages.description:
𝒪𝓊𝓇 𝑔𝓇𝓊𝒹𝑔𝑒 𝓌𝒾𝓁𝓁 𝒷𝑒 𝓈𝑒𝓉𝓉𝓁𝑒𝒹 𝒶𝓉 𝓁𝒶𝓈𝓉...
𝑀𝑒𝑒𝓉 𝓂𝓎 𝓅𝑜𝓌𝑒𝓇𝒻𝓊𝓁 𝓈𝑒𝒸𝓇𝑒𝓉 𝓌𝑒𝒶𝓅𝑜𝓃...
𝒯𝒽𝑒 𝒷𝓇𝒶𝓃𝒹-𝓃𝑒𝓌 𝒟𝑒𝒹𝑒𝒹𝑒 𝐻𝒶𝓂𝓂𝑒𝓇!

Did an arrangement of the one and only, Masked Dedede's Theme, from Kirby Super Star Ultra for my 5K subscriber milestone. A massive goal reached deserves some treatment from the King himself. I already did his theme once... now it's time to do it again!!!

It shouldn't be a surprise when I say this is my favorite Kirby theme and one of my favorite final boss themes in any video game period. Seriously, to top the original song (which is already one of the best songs in the series) with this is an achievement very few can achieve.

Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ Death sound is gonna sound weird (@1 replaces @9 to save on space).

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. C# Minor w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch - Listening Only)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. C# Minor (Remix Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. C Minor (Original Pitch)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ4. B Minor (GaMetal Pitch)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ5. D Minor (Candid Friend Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Voice Clips, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. Disables Voice Clips [turned on default]

versions.title: Kirby Super Star Ultra - Vengeance, The Mask's Awakening ~ Masked Dedede (Remix)

packages.description:
A nice water-y or ruins song with some big stakes involved.

I don't exactly know what its role was in-game since I discovered it browsing Zophar domain. So far it is the nicest track I could find in the whole OST, I hope you'll enjoy it as much as I do.

-------------
Important update:

On the former version, it was brought to my attention by Stivi, that calling Pause was not interrupting the song, but rather letting it freeze in place on the last played note.

It occurs on AddMusicK1.0.8 when channel #6, which plays the pause SFX, has noise inside, as explained by KungFuFurby and Kevin.

While I could have chosen to take #6's contents to channel #7, I found this choice inesthetical since #7 always gets cut with Jump or coin sounds. So I just replaced the noise sample of #6 by an external closed hat sample.

packages.description:

packages.name: smwmusic-krack-the-hack-sokobansolvermanianicazen-sins
packages.title: Krack The Hack - Sokobansolvermanianicazen Sins
packages.description:
The long repetitious bonus final level theme from Krack The Hack with a very long name to boot, originally made for Mario Must Die 3 until Sokobansolver decided to use a different theme instead. Made to be exciting training music made to fit multiple environments. There are a few differences between this version and the version in Krack The Hack itself as a result of optimizing the port for a public release.

A "no staccato" define option is present for those who wants to save space. With staccato set to 1, it'll decrease the size to 0x03A8 but will sound slightly worse (but accurate to how it was heard in Krack The Hack).

Taking a page off of Hooded Edge, there are two versions: an E Minor version (Krack pitch), and a D minor version (Daizo pitch). Pick either or to match your level as you wish!

This song isn't compatible with every SMW sample, but you're free to enable/disable what you need using the provided defines. By default I enabled LevelClear, Star, Death, and GameOver; which leaves out Thunder, Blargg, P-switch, Star, Bonus End, and Yoshi.

OPTION:
This song has an echo toggle option that controls how compatible with SMW the song is.
ECHO 1: uses #optimized, but minimal echo.
ECHO 5: More echo, but not compatible with Yoshi, Bonus End, P-switch, and Thunder (Miss uses @1).
ECHO 7: Listen-only, most faithful to source.

packages.name: smwmusic-last-bible-iii-central-of-the-world-underworld-forest-remix
packages.title: Last Bible III - Central of the World ~ Underworld Forest (Remix)
packages.description:
Decided to make my 200th port upload on this site something special similar to my Air Man Remix in February, so I did a special remix of SMWC's National Anthem Underworld Forest from Last Bible III.

History Of The SMWC National Anthem
Six years ago, legendary porter Nanako made a port of this song, and little did anyone know that it'd change the entire Super Mario World industry. Nearly every SMW hack had this theme in it in some way or form. You could not escape it, even if you tried. And to make things worse, a year ago, other legendary porter Samantha made an unsampled port to add to the chaos. SMWCentral has never been the same since. What was once an innocent web site for gamers who wanted to express their love for the amazing Super Mario World has now turned into an Underworld Forest cult. SMWCentral deprived themselves of their Super Mario World content in order to please the Underworld Forest god with using this song in their hacks. This site is stuck in an endless cycle of torture of making sure this song was engraved into our brains, note for note, and us porters are forced to port / arrange this song or else our end will come. This is not just an end of an era. but it's the true end of... The Time-when-Underworld-Forest-wasn't-a-thing Days...


Jokes aside though, this song's absolutely fantastic (and so are those ports). There's a reason why so many people love using it, and I hope I was able to spice things up with my take on this awesome theme for my special! :D

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. B Minor w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch, Listening-Only)
2. B Minor (Remix Pitch, turned on default)
2. C Minor (Original Pitch)
2. A# Minor (Custom Pitch)

versions.title: Last Bible III - Central of the World ~ Underworld Forest (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-link-the-faces-of-evil-do-the-duck-walk-firestone-lake-remix
packages.title: Link: The Faces Of Evil - DO THE DUCK WALK!! ~ Firestone Lake (Remix)
packages.description:
❝ 𝑀𝒶𝒽 𝒷𝑜𝒾, 𝓉𝒽𝒾𝓈 𝓅𝑒𝒶𝒸𝑒 𝒾𝓈 𝓌𝒽𝒶𝓉 𝒶𝓁𝓁 𝓉𝓇𝓊𝑒 𝓌𝒶𝓇𝓇𝒾𝑜𝓇𝓈 𝓈𝓉𝓇𝒾𝓋𝑒 𝐹𝒪𝑅! ❞
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ- King Harkinian, 1993

Yes, you're not seeing things. I just did an actual SNES arrangement of Firestone Lake from Link: The Faces of Evil. I dunno if y'all know about this... but I'm UNIRONICALLY in love with the first two Zelda CD-I OSTs. I'm not kidding when I say this is some of my favorite Zelda music ever. Look, other old-school Zelda OSTs are good too, but William Havlicek just said "fuggit!" and gave us high-energy music. This doesn't sound like Zelda in the slightest, but who cares! I like it, and you will too!!!

Also, this is my first Zelda arrangement / port, and it had to be from this game, lmao.

Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. C / F Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. C# / F# Minor (Ricky Martin Pitch)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. A / D Minor (Shrek 2 Pitch)

versions.title: Link: The Faces Of Evil - DO THE DUCK WALK!! ~ Firestone Lake (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-long-range-motivation
packages.title: Long Range Motivation
packages.description:
An original song I made in a competition of ORG Maker. I felt so happy with what I had composed, that I wanted to port it.
I think it doesn't seem to fit very well in a SMW level, unless someone use it wisely.

03/19/2021 Update
* Did rework the entire port from zero, so now every section is properly optimized, and the text file is MUCH MORE readable;
* Added more channels to fill the strings part, so it sounds much more fuller;
* Replaced the cymbal sample to the KSS one;
* Reworked on most of non Kirby samples, downgrading some, and making the organ-like wave more higher quality;
* Crammed all of the percussion parts in one single channel;
* Added a second text file which does contain the final section of the song (which is where the actual song ends, instead of looping forever). Keep in mind that the full one loops once, then it'll stay silent, like the original piece;
* Lowered the global volume to w166.


03/22/2021 Update: Just a small fix on the organ-like wave sample on the full version, where the highest note channel overflows at the final section.

packages.name: smwmusic-lost-desert
packages.title: Lost Desert
packages.description:
I originally made this song for a 100% free (with no in-game-real-money payments) sidescroller MMORPG game called Aeon Rivals back in 2017 when it was in development.

It was originally for the Lost Desert level, as the author was requesting for .XM music to be put into the game.

I gave the author this song and while he liked it, he couldn't put it in the game because I was 14 at the time, so I was too young to be able to receive payment without complications.

Of course, I'm still too young now, and it seems the game is already done, so I'll just upload the song here. Well, converted to AddMusicK MML.

This might not sound like most other desert themes. I tried to go not for the classic Saharan feel, but for a more southern US atmosphere that is also mysterious.

And yes, I lifted the drum samples from Evanescence's Bring Me To Life stems.

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ- Luis Fonzi, 2017

No, you didn't just accidentally skip back to a 2017 meme compilation, this is a 2023 SNES remix of Despacito by Luis Fonsi (ft. Daddy Yankee). Let it be known that I don't understand 90% of the lyrics (despite knowing like 5% Spanish), but Despacito's got an amazing beat, and that's all that really matters.

Important:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End" Yoshi, & Thunder SFX are disabled.
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ Death sound is gonna sound weird (@0 replaces @9 to save on space).

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. B Minor w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch - Listening-Only)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. B Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. A Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ4. C Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Nylon Intro & Voice Clip, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. Enables Nylon Intro Only, but at the cost of @12 [turned on by default]

packages.name: smwmusic-machinations-m-t-opolitaines
packages.title: Machinations Météopolitaines
packages.description:
"You're walking through the big city, lost in thought. But, looking around, things aren't quite so bad when you're here."

A joint composition between icrawfish and bebn legg that won 4th place at Super Famicompo 4. We took turns composing and porting each part, which was lots of fun, and this fusion of a piece was the result.

We came up with the title by combining some themes the song reminded us, like cities and machines, but also seasonal/weathery vibes, and brought that over to French to come up with "Machinations Météopolitaines" (the second word being a combination of "météo" meaning weather, and "métropolitain", or metropolitan).

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Goal Tape SFX [turned on by default]
‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ0. Disables Goal Tape SFX

Studies have shown that if this song is used in your romhack, it will increase its coolness by 50%. :)

packages.title: Mario is Missing! (NES) Expanded - Berlin Germany
packages.description:
Ever wondered what the music would sound like if Mario is Missing! for the NES was ever expanded upon?
Well, I certainly was and the result was this!

It's a pretty neato composition I'd say, it captures some stuff from the original and turns it into something new.
The percussion is a bit of unhinged compered to how it is in the actual game, but I think it has a certain charm to it that compliments the song well.

Will I end up doing more?
Certainly, but not actively, maybe once a couple months.

Anyway, this song can be used in retro levels and cities.
It can be a bit repetitive after a while, so keep that in mind!

𝗗𝗼𝗻'𝘁 𝗳𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆--𝗳𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗳. 𝗩𝗶𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲.

packages.name: smwmusic-mega-man-2-110-million-miracles-dr-wily-s-castle-1
packages.title: Mega Man 2 - 110 million miracles ~ Dr. Wily's Castle 1 & 2 (Faith is for the Transient Remix)
packages.description:
𝐘𝐨𝐮 𝐜𝐚𝐧'𝐭 𝐥𝐞𝐭 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐬𝐞𝐥𝐟 𝐛𝐞 𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐝 𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐛𝐲 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐨𝐧 𝐬𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐆𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐨𝐤𝐲𝐨, 𝐫𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭!?

A remix of the famous Dr. Wily's Castle 1 from Mega Man 2 (mostly based off the Wily Wars version) ft. Sanae Kochiya's theme, Faith is for the Transient, from Touhou 10: Mountain of Faith. I love Wily's Castle 1 to death. It's one of my favorite VGMs of all-time, and I've been wanting to do a remix of this song for ages. I had such a fun time working on this, and I decided to incorporate Sanae's theme in there because her theme song always reminded me of this song.

This song is perfect for castle stages, tower stages, castle grounds stages, airship stages, intense stages, space, and final areas.

Note:
There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."
- @7 & Thunder SFX is disabled.

There are also five customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
- C# Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
- D Minor (S.S.H Pitch)
- C Minor (Smash 4 Pitch)
- D# Minor (Power Fighters Pitch)
- E Minor (Sonic Mega Mix v4 Pitch)

versions.title: Mega Man 2 - 110 million miracles ~ Dr. Wily's Castle 1 & 2 (Faith is for the Transient Remix)

Best for castle or final levels.

If you want to insert the Wily Wars variant, find
Code
#define WilyWarsDrums 0
in TXT and follow instructions.

Did an arrangement of Dr. Wily's Castle 1 & 2 from Mega Man 2 stylized after an old SMW port from 2008 when the @7 steel drum used to be the best sample ever. Seriously, I have a ton of nostalgia for this version, and I remember listening to this exactly after I first heard the song in Mega Man 2 and fell in love with it. I did heavily base this off my previous port / remix of this theme.

𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗯𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗱 𝗺𝗲, 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘁𝗼 𝗠𝗮𝗻! 𝗜'𝗺 𝗴𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗮 𝗯𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗸 𝘆𝗼𝘂, 𝗠𝗲𝗴𝗮 𝗠𝗮𝗻!!

Did a remix of Dr. Cossack's Citadel 3 & 4 from Mega Man 4. Had loads of fun doing this one, and it is one of the most memorable themes in the series. It's also incredibly catchy as well!! Got the idea of doing this song after hearing (again) an old port of this song used as the final stage theme in Super Mario World: The After Years (Ultra).

packages.title: Mega Man 4 - Stairway to Corruption ~ Dr. Wily's Castle 3 & 4 (Remix)
packages.description:
Did a remix of Wily's Castle 3 & 4 from Mega Man 4, given how incredibly underrated this track is and how much I love it. I took some inspiration from the Complete Works version when working on this, and I also decided to go all out with a supporting piano chord on this one, baby!! This song captures the darkness of Wily's Castle incredibly well (before Mega Man 5's Wily's Castle would overtake that title) and makes those last few stages that more intense.

This song is perfect for factory, tower, and castle stages.

- @7 & Thunder SFX is disabled.

packages.name: smwmusic-mega-man-7-wily-stage
packages.title: Mega Man 7 - Wily Stage 1 (X2 Style)
packages.description:
This is a Megaman X2 styled arrangement of the Wily Stage 1 theme from Megaman 7, also known as Wily Stage 1 ~ Entrance. While MegaNerd14 requested this song to be ported, unlike the unsampled version, this one was my own choice since I also wanted to try and do a X2 styled port of this song. :V

it sounds a bit too much like Luiz Fernando de Jesus Ribeiro's arrangement of the song tho (here's a link to it in case you're wondering: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y4DSmGiLHVo), and while I wanted to use the sax sample from X2 to differentiate this arrangement from his, it just wasn't full enough, so sadly I had to use the brass sample the same way he did; oh well, it sounds good, so ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

This should probably fit in a lot of final scenarios specifically (like an entrance right before the final level of a hack), but not much else.

EDIT: Fixed a slight issue with the marimba where it desynced slightly before the loop due to the note length being slightly off; not too noticeable, but with how fast the marimba plays in that part, it gets annoying fast :V

packages.name: smwmusic-mega-man-battle-network-operation
packages.title: Mega Man Battle Network - Operation!
packages.description:
This is the battle theme from the first Battle Network, just like what you seen in Idol 9's first round. I wasn't planning on releasing any Idol ports of mine, but since this was already optimized, I said "hey, why not", and decided to release this lol. IMO, this theme is a pretty good theme for friendly battles and races, and this theme would be best suited for those, but it could also fit athletic levels quite well. Maybe.

Fun fact btw: some people were talking about why I used SMW samples for the drums, and that's actually because I misinterpreted the challenge and I didn't know you could use more than 3 samples (else I would've used some sweet TR-909 drums >.>); at least I didn't get DQed because of it tho, so that's good

packages.name: smwmusic-mega-man-x2-turn-up-the-heat-volcano-s-fury-remix
packages.title: Mega Man X2 - Turn Up The Heat!! ~ Volcano's Fury (Remix)
packages.description:
Did an arrangement of Flame Stag's Stage from Mega Man X2. Needed to clear my mind off some things, so I decided to do this song as a means of distracting myself from that.

It's one of my favorites from X2, despite its short length (and lackluster instrumentation). To be honest, I feel like Mega Man X2 has amazing compositions, but the instrumentation just feels very empty, especially when compared to X1 and many other really great SNES OSTs. Maybe it's because the channel usage in this one is limited or the samples used don't complement the songs really well, but most of these songs feel like they deserved better.

Important:
There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. B Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. A Minor (Custom Pitch)

This was a rather difficult one to get right, I managed to pull through, though.

This is the Blizzard Buffalo's Theme from Mega Man X3, my favorite song from the game.

packages.name: smwmusic-mega-man-x4-for-the-livin-dead-split-mushroom-s-stage-halloween-special-voile-mix
packages.title: Mega Man X4 - 𝔽𝕦𝕝𝕝 𝕄𝕠𝕠𝕟, for the Livin' Dead 🌕 ~ Split Mushroom's Stage (Halloween Special Voile-mix)
packages.description:
❝ 𝕳𝖆𝖕𝖕𝖞 𝕳𝖆𝖑𝖑𝖔𝖜𝖊𝖊𝖓! ❞🎃

Did a special Halloween mashup-mix of "Split Mushroom's Stage 🍄 x Voile, the Magical Library 📕 (Patchouli Knowledge's Stage)" (from both Mega Man X4 & Touhou 6 Koumakyou ~ The Embodiment of the Scarlet Devil) for the funny spooky scary skeletons and shivers down your spine season.

I had the idea to finally cook a mashup that I've had in my head ever since I heard Patchy's theme for the first time in EoSD (so like 6 years ago... damn it's been that long) because it always reminded me of Split Mushroom's Theme from X4. It's one of my oldest ideas, and I thought it'd fit for the season given how grim and dark Split Mushroom's Stage is (there's a full freaking moon in the background, like that's some Castlevania shit right there).

I love both themes and are some of my favorite stage themes from both games (at least top two for both). Really wanted to cook something incredibly intense, as if you were traversing through are more difficult version of the SDM library or abandoned laboratory,

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, Yoshi SFX, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. A Minor w/ detune (Remix Pitch)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. A Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ3. A# Minor (MIDI Pitch)
ㅤ3. G Minor (Azure Reflections Pitch)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Enables the voice clip, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (Voice Enabled)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Disables the voice clip & Decreases the Echo (Voice Disabled)ㅤ[turned on by default]

packages.name: smwmusic-mega-man-zx-pallida-mors
packages.title: Mega Man ZX - Pallida Mors
packages.description:
And here's something I don't think anyone here would expect: a remix (no, it's not an arrangement this time, I mean an actual remix) of the final boss theme from Megaman ZX, Pallida Mors. This one was made for a certain competition for the Chiptune Cafe Discord server, and since it's been a while that the competition ended, I think it's a good enough opportunity to release this now haha

Anyway, this one is very different to the original in many different ways, but the biggest change specifically is the extra section I've added at 2:47. Since this was made mainly thinking about the competition itself and not specifically for SMW, it doesn't loop like the original does. Despite that tho, I have made a looped version for it, and honestly, the song is long enough by it's own that it fits it's purpose well enough to work even without the loop.

There's also optimized versions for each version as well; these don't have the echo and removes a few SFX samples, like Yoshi bongos and the thunder SFX, but I feel like it could be done better than this, I just couldn't be bothered really lmao

But anyway... this one I feel like it could only really work in a final boss setting, but the looped version is there if you want to use it for a level pretty much. Not much else to say here, just have fun :P

The jungle theme from the NES port of Metal Gear. Original by Kazuki Muraoka.

packages.name: smwmusic-metal-gear-rising-revengeance-change-your-own-destiny-it-has-to-be-this-way-remix
packages.title: Metal Gear Rising: REVENGEANCE - Change Your Own Destiny ~ It Has to Be This Way (Remix)
packages.description:
One day every person in this nation will control their OWN destiny. A land of the truly free, dammit. A nation of action, not words. Ruled by strength, not committee.

Did an arrangement of the Senator Armstrong's last phase theme, It Has To Be this Way (aka "Standing Here") from Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, despite it not being as long as the original (due to ARAM constrictions). Just got into the Metal Gear series recently (beating this game and MGS1), & MGR lives up to the hype of being one of the best action games ever made. Not only that, but it has one of the most kick-ass final boss themes in any action game period. I felt the need to do this theme given this game has no representation on this site (and really needs it), and it's become one of my favorite final boss themes now.

PS: This song is not actually used in the scene where Raiden punches Armstrong, despite memes telling you otherwise.



Important:
♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. B / D Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. C / D# Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
3. A# / C# Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. Enables Voice Clip, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility
2. Disables Voice Clip (turned on default)

versions.title: Metal Gear Rising: REVENGEANCE - Change Your Own Destiny ~ It Has to Be This Way (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-mustard-motordrive
packages.title: Mustard Motordrive
packages.description:
An original song I made for Superfamicompo 2. This song originally started out as a discount version of Stardust Speedway (Present) from Sonic CD (JP/EU), but it sort of drifted off into its own chaotic thing. I admittedly felt very uninspired throughout the month that I was working on this, which you can probably tell by the various shifts in mood throughout the song, but I'm generally still satisfied with how the song turned out, and I think each section has its charm. I love sawtooth waves, so it was fun to make a song with one as the lead.

Overall, this song probably fits night levels, perhaps ones centered around speed, and maybe highways? That's the visual I had when composing.

packages.description:
The song that inspired Chrono Trigger's Corridors of time, ported in the style of Corridors of time. Very mystic, atmospheric, contemplative. I invite you to listen to the original versions by Joe Hisaishi. Useful for ruins, deserts and cave overworlds.

Trivia:

After humming corridors of time all the time, I did have my epiphany, found the similarity between the two, and decided to go for it.
This took a good bunch of hours trying to re-create melody from ear.
In the mix I added some elements from Corridors of Time, and also some elements from "Ohmu", the track from the image album. Below are the sources:
- Original soundtrack's "A princess who loves insects", starts at 1:00
- Image album's track "Ohmu", used as inspiration for the pitch bends.
- Re-mastered version

packages.description:
Part of The New Super Mario Bros. Soundtrack. Please give credit if used.

Original Description
The New Super Mario Bros. Soundtrack. As more songs are ported, more will be added. Currently contains:

-Bowser Jr.'s Castle
-Castle (original and alternative version)
-Flowing Lava
-Mushroom Waltz
-Underground
-Walking The Plains


Currently doesn't contain:

-The rest of the songs
-Support for use of global songs and global samples

Please give credit if used.

Change Log:

7-6-19
Renamed the songs accordingly. Added Flowing Lava as well as a port of Castle using the game's samples.

8-1-18
Redid every song minus Course Clear and Star Power (these need to be redone, if you're interested in them download them in version history). Added Fortress onto list. Credit to musicalman for making the samples (big thanks).

packages.name: smwmusic-nostalgia-airship-boss
packages.title: Nostalgia - Airship Boss
packages.description:
Hey guys, I'm still alive! Lol. This time, it's epic battle music from this RPG for the Nintendo DS. This was a very difficult port for me to make. I would like to extend many thanks to LadiesMan217 for helping me reduce the song down to 8 channels; I certainly wouldn't have been brave enough to tackle this without his help!

As much as I tried to save space wherever I could, this port flirts with aram limits with default amk configs due to the amount of samples needed... I really wish I had an extra channel or two to mitigate the need for those haha

About the hq spc: When I started this port I made the samples much too big, but rather than scrap them, I thought it'd be interesting to see what they'd sound like. Of course the samples/txt included are for the somewhat stripped down version intended for use in smw.

packages.description:
❝ Don't really want to make it tough
I just want to tell you that I've had enough
It might sound crazy but it ain't no lie
Baby bye bye bye ❞
ㅤ- N'SYNC, 2000

Did an arrangement of Bye Bye Bye by N'SYNC. Watched Deadpool & Wolverine (god-tier movie coming from a very biased Deadpool fan) a couple months back and was sent back by two decades the second I heard that song pop up at the beginning (I was singing throughout the entire sequence) and also once more grinding the Ch. 5 Season 4 Fortnite Battle Pass recently and obtaining the Deadpool & Wolverine Bundle + the Bye Bye Bye taunt. Really wanted to arrange this song after all of that 'cuz I haven't done a non-VGM track in a hot minute, and N'SYNC was a huge part of my childhood (quite literally some of the first ever music I heard).

Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's text file:
ㅤ1. G# Minor w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. G# Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ3. A Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
ㅤ4. F# Minor (Custom Pitch 2)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Original Echo Delay, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (OG Echo)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Drastically Decreased Echo Delay (LOWER Echo)ㅤ[turned on by default]

packages.name: smwmusic-omh-springtrap-is-mocking-you-i-always-come-back
packages.title: ~omh~ - Springtrap is Mocking You ~ I Always Come Back
packages.description:
You enter a hallway that appears to be an office.
You walk across, and find a midpoint.
When you reach the other side.
An old rotting suit comes out of the shadows.
All he says is...

"Well I have...the perfect idea. Engage the motherf***er."
"I always come back."

You then proceed to fight the a rotting corpse in a strange rabbit suit.

--

A boss battle remix sampling Scraptrap's line "I always come back." from FNAF Ultimate Custom Night (and a version from Dead by Daylight). Could fit for...bosses? Mainly bosses themed around rotting animatronics with an old man singing "I always come back" over and over. Used in ~omh~.

Credit to Jonah and Hooded Edge for the "Battle Against A Vending Machine" and "Gadobadorror" melodies they ported that I used for this remix. Give credit to me for the overall song.

--

2025 EDIT: Now includes a version of the same iconic voiceline/sample, but it's from the version heard in Dead By Daylight (by the same actor PJ Haywood)! Just toggle the VoiceLineVersion define. With it enabled, it adds 3 extra bytes to amplify the volume of the vocal (0x060A).

Also, this is better optimized than the original.

packages.name: smwmusic-othello-world-end-of-game
packages.title: Othello World - End of Game
packages.description:
Othello World is one of those Othello games you probably saw in some Japanese pawn shop or something like that. Developed by Dice and published by Tsukuda Original, it's very obscure, though easier to find at your nearest online shop for pretty cheap. Surprisingly, according to GDRI, it uses HAL's N-SPC variant, which is also used in games such as Kirby Super Star. In fact, every HAL game uses this sound driver, with the exception of EarthBound, which instead uses another N-SPC variant.

This jingle plays upon finishing a stage. After that, we get the counter and another jingle plays (varies if you either lost or win).

Good for goals, if it wasn't that obvious. There's even a flag in the TXT file that allows you to add the goal whistle at the start of the song.

This is the unsampled version.

packages.name: smwmusic-outrun-splash-wave
packages.title: OutRun - Splash Wave
packages.description:
This is Splash Wave from OutRun, A.K.A that one game everyone knows about by name but knows jack shit about it otherwise... well, some people may know about the soundtrack at least, it's considered a classic by many after all LOL

For this one, I, of course, decided to put my own spin on this theme by adding a lot of my own embellishments based around my own musical style (A.K.A tons of drum syncopation and focus on drums in general), so it's not *too* accurate to the original, but I hope people still enjoy this :D

Anyway, this is a absolute LONG boi, so if you want to use this in a level it's got to match up with the length of the song; outside of that, this could be used for beach, final, or just long ass levels in general, but of course, it could also be used as a credits/staff roll theme as well because of the length, so it's pretty multipurpose, which could make the long size a bit more worth it :P

EDIT: Along with the alternate loop version, there's now a no legato version in case the melody gets cut after the song gets paused; those are separate mainly so that people can use those versions in case your hack has the entire song silenced wherever you pause the game (A.K.A what SMW normally does by default), and the normal versions are for hacks that doesn't silence the entire song when you pause the game.

packages.title: Pilotwings - Light Plane
packages.description:
The very chill and jazzy Light Plane theme from a game called Pilotwings, which, thanks to Soyo Oka, has a pretty amazing soundtrack. It's honestly really surprisingly high-quality for a SNES launch title too, and it's definitely a much better example of a good SNES Nintendo soundtrack compared to most of their other works. Still, the samples could be better, which is why I gave this the resampled treatment, like I do with a lot of my other ports.

Alright, so, in this you will see two versions; one is a standard rearrangement with added flourishes of my own, and the second is a vocal version with samples I have recorded myself (I don't have any proper voice recording equipment tho, but they still get the job done :V), made specifically to mimick the vocal version in Smash 4's version.

Oh, and uh, if you need to use this, you could try using it in a sky, grassland, or early-game athletic stages, I suppose. Alright, hope y'all enjoy :D

packages.name: smwmusic-pilotwings-rocketbelt
packages.title: Pilotwings - Rocketbelt
packages.description:
This is the theme that plays in the Rocketbelt stages in Pilotwings. Like my Light Plane port, this isn't actually supposed to be a 1:1 cover of the original, but instead it's more of a remaster than anything, done on the same soundchip it's on, except with more higher quality samples. Also, I added some pitch bends in this one because why not lol

Anyway, this would be best used for sky or grassland levels, probably a few athletic stages too.

packages.name: smwmusic-pink-floyd-comfortably-numb
packages.title: Pink Floyd - Comfortably Numb
packages.description:
Comfortably Numb is a mellow, atmospheric song by English progressive rock band Pink Floyd, from their 1979 Magnum Opus, The Wall. This remix of comfortably numb features synthesized vocals, strings and horns playing accompaniment, laid back bass and drums, and a note-for-note recreation of one of the most iconic guitar solos in rock 'n' roll. Perfect for water levels or any slower paced course.

There is no pain, you are receding...

packages.name: smwmusic-planet-x2-oh-no-more-square-waves
packages.title: Planet X2 - Oh No! More Square Waves!
packages.description:
Yes, I know it mainly uses sawtooth waves, but that's what the original song was called.

The song was originally made by David Murray. It was made for video on his '8-Bit Keys' channel where he reviewed a pulse wave keyboard called the Yamaha PSS-125. David Murray then had Anders Enger Jensen compose the soundtrack to his C64 game 'Planet X2', hence the simplicity here. One of those songs happened to be a remix of 'Oh No! More Square Waves!'.

Did a special arrangement of The Haunted Shrine from Touhou Pocky & Rocky after reaching 750 subscribers. Originally thought about doing a Touhou theme for this, but I thought it'd be more neat if I did a theme from the bullet that was most likely the biggest influence for Touhou.

Surprisingly, this was a fairly difficult song to do given my current style is vastly different than Iwatsuki's "eastern" style, but despite that, I still had fun doing this.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. B Minor (Remix Pitch, turned on default)
2. A Minor (Original Pitch)

You can also adjust whether Yoshi will be compatible in your level(s) in the song's txt file:
1. Yoshi-Incompatible
2. Yoshi-Compatible (Turned on default)

packages.description:
The lovely theme from everyone's favourite blue and pink towns in the Kanto region, so comfortingly remixed in Generation IV.

This song is so dear and special to me, and has been ever since I was a little child. It's a shame it got shafted so hard in the original Generation II games. So here's me doing my part to give this song the love it deserves.

packages.name: smwmusic-pok-mon-mystery-dungeon-red-blue-rescue-team-sky-tower
packages.title: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red/Blue Rescue Team - Sky Tower
packages.description:
A beautiful and heavenly sounding song that plays in Sky Tower, the final dungeon of the main story. Makes extensive usage of ARAM, so some SMW samples have been disabled for it. Comes in four versions of txt:

- SMW Compatible: has the best quality of the bunch, but isn't compatible with Blargg roar SFX, Thunder SFX, Valley of Bowser appears SFX and Castle destruction bomb SFX. Additionally, it uses noise instruments that affect noise-based SFX, like Fire Spit SFX, Podoboo SFX and Koopaling land in lava SFX.

- Noise SFX Compatible: uses a noise sample instead of the regular SPC700-generated noise, meaning it won't affect noise-based SFX. The other alternative to circumvent the issue would be to send all the noise instruments to channel 8, but then the song would suffer noticeable cuts every time the jump SFX played.

- Blargg & Thunder Compatible: at the cost of some echo delay, it is compatible with Blargg roar SFX, Thunder SFX, Valley of Bowser appears SFX and Castle destruction bomb SFX.

- Most Compatible: a combination of the previous two versions.

All versions are incompatible with the Bonus End music.
Samples omitted: 09 SMW @7.brr, 0D SMW @14.brr, 0F SMW @21.brr, 11 SMW @17.brr, (13 SMW Thunder.brr)*.
*Only for the SMW Compatible and Noise SFX Compatible versions.

I've also included the SPC of the original port for listening purposes. Enjoy!

packages.name: smwmusic-pok-mon-ultra-sun-ultra-moon-battle-team-rainbow-rocket-snes-arrange
packages.title: Pokémon Ultra Sun/Ultra Moon - Battle! Team Rainbow Rocket (SNES Arrange)
packages.description:
This is a SNES arrangement of Team Rainbow Rocket's battle theme from Pokemon USUM, where the original was basically a remix of the original Team Rocket battle theme from Pokemon G/S/C (was also present in Pokemon HGSS).

This was VERY hard to do honestly; 3-4 days were spent just to make the samples and fit everything in the MIDI I used to fit the SNES's 8-channel limit, and then another 3-4 days to optimize and sequence this MML. I'm surprised this has worked so well tho, considering the sheer amount of samples and MML size that this port has, and the MIDI also had 13 channels, so it was kind of a wonder how it was possible to fit in everything (as you can see by how busy this port is); guess this is the true power of making chord samples lol

This could be used for a long boss fight, or a long chase sequence, but other than that, I dunno if this has many uses; and again, this port is really large, so use this with caution.

oh yeah, MIDI is by ShinkoNetCavy btw

Update: Fixed the tuning of the distorted guitar, and (hopefully) improved the mixing a bit.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐬𝐲𝐜𝐡𝐨 𝐛𝐚𝐥𝐥'𝐬 𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐛𝐮𝐫𝐬𝐭𝐬, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐀𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐧𝐚'𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦 𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬.

A remix of the banger that is the Psycho Soldier theme song in the Mega Man 7 style. I'm surprised there isn't any ports of this song on here.

This song is perfect for intense, athletic, and fire stages. Could also work for Mini-bosses.

Note:
- There is a "READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."
- The Thunder SFX and @7 are disabled.

packages.title: Puyo Puyo - Brave of Puyo Puyo
packages.description:
The second cutscene theme from Puyo Puyo, also present in Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine as a remix for Stage 13 (A.K.A Robotnik's stage)'s intro, and a version more faithful to the original which has gone unused (Sad!). It was also used in the Mega Drive version of Madou Monogatari as its second opening theme, tho I'm not sure about the other versions of that game.

Anyway, this song would definitely fit well with a dramatic and final cutscene, so if y'all want to use this for a hack, definitely consider that as a option. If not, the final levels of your hack would also benefit from that. Or you can just ignore this and use it on your own way, I dont care LOL

Oh, and btw, thank JonKaruzu for helping out with the last parts of the conversion of the original SPC to MML. While my skills with MML have definitely been getting better, I'm still not very comfortable with it, so help like this is always very appreciated >:]

packages.name: smwmusic-rakugaki-mario-fake-final-real-final-classic-remix
packages.title: Rakugaki Mario - FAKE FINAL (real final classic remix)
packages.description:
The theme used in the level "Life has it's Ups and Downs" from Rakugaki Mario. This is a downported version of "real final" from R-ACK, which that song can be downloaded here. Not to be confused with the unsampled version. This can work for airships, castles, water levels, title screens, cutscenes, or even space levels.

This is specifically designed to emulate the same style as those older japanese ports from back then, which itself has a nostalgic feel for a lot of the older SMW hacking folk, me included. Of course, this "style" is not exclusive to japanese ports (a lot of older FPI and S.N.N. ports have that same feel), which is why it's more accurate to call it a "classic remix".

packages.name: smwmusic-rapina-bros-reach-to-the-top
packages.title: Rapina Bros. - Reach to the Top
packages.description:
Probably best known as the invincibility theme from Sonic The Next Level, which is a hack of Sonic 1 with a lot of polish, including CD-quality music. This port is just a 30-second section of the song, just like the Sonic The Next Level version.

This song is probably best suited for happy and hopeful areas, like bonus rooms or overworlds, or maybe a sky.

You can probably use this as an invincibility theme as well, but you'll most likely have to lower the echo delay to avoid a pause, as well as add @21 as a global sample. It also lasts much longer than the vanilla star duration.
(Edit: added an additional version that uses a @0 kick.)

packages.name: smwmusic-rat-attack-title-screen

The title theme from the PS1, N64 and PC hidden gem, Rat Attack! (the PS1 version is thankfully re-released on GOG). Starring the Scratch Cats (not to be confused with you know, the programming language you definitely used at school if you're a Gen Z), the goal of the game is to eliminate you know... rats that appear on screen, using a rectangular lasso (functioning almost similar to the arcade games Libble Rabble and Qix).

Not compatible with Blargg/Thunder and Bonus End!

Good for not only title screens, but also overworlds and mid-level bonus levels.

2026-01-08: Updated with more noticeable echo, and the speed now matches the original more closely (the internal song tempo was also doubled, for less staccato).

Last Bible’s Dungeon theme, remastered using Last Bible III’s samples. This remix actually won the 11th 120hoSPC contest too, so that’s neat!

packages.name: smwmusic-rhythm-heaven-megamix-songbird-remix
packages.title: Rhythm Heaven Megamix - Songbird Remix
packages.description:
The mysterious yet singing theme from Rhythm Heaven Megamix's Songbird Remix, which is probably my favourite remix in the series. This song is quite a mish-mash, and even features some brief dubstep-y sections.

I ported this ages ago and showed it off during C3, but I was too lazy to loop it, as the original doesn't loop. Naturally, 3:00 a.m. on a school night is the best time to tackle MML surgery. I wasn't sure how best to loop it, as the song doesn't give many opportunities to do so, but hopefully you enjoy the point I picked.

Special thanks to Hazel for helping me play around with that noise pitchmod buildup thing.

Here's an image:

packages.name: smwmusic-rhythm-heaven-remix
packages.title: Rhythm Heaven - Remix 9
packages.description:
The funky and all-over-the-place (as with most Rhythm Heaven music) music of the 9th Remix from Rhythm Heaven on the DS, prominently featuring the evil moais that nobody likes, but now with sunglasses!

Also my entry to 72hoSPC #6.

It's a song that's a bit chaotic. I suppose it could fit puzzles, bosses, or maybe even a rhythmic level.

On a more technical note, fitting the business of this song into 8 channels was Very messy and there's several instances of multiple of the original's channels/melodies being crammed into one SNES channel.

ft. Cut Man's Stage from Mega Man Numero Uno

I remember first hearing it in Mushroom Kingdom Meltdown years ago, and played Blaster Master Boy for the first time a couple months back. packages.title: Rockfish (Unreleased) - Boss
packages.description:
Accurate port of a game of Studio Pixel (the guy who made Cave Story and Ikachan) that was in development for the IOS on his Devlogs, and eventually got unreleased. This game has later reworked to become Gero Blaster, and finally Kero Blaster.
Also manually programed the samples, using only the filter 0, for better accuracy.

packages.name: smwmusic-rockfish-unreleased-boss-encounter
packages.title: Rockfish (Unreleased) - Boss Encounter
packages.description:
An upbeat and more tense remix of Rockfish's first dev log song.
This game was being developed by Pixel for the IOS, back in 2010, until it got cancelled in order to work on Gero Blaster. Later on, it finally got rebooted into Kero Blaster, in 2014.

It does uses the KDL3 soundfont.

Original description by Pixel
Original:
ボスBGM
BGMはピストンコラージュから出力した制限付き形式を使う。
今のところ、三角波 ＋ 矩形波 ＋ ノコギリ波 ＋ バスドラム ＋ ハイハット(クローズ)の計５音。
60フレームで割り切れるビート・テンポを使用。
小さいスピーカーでは低音が聴き取りにくい。
でもそれにあわせてボリューム調整をすると、今度はイヤホンがつらい。
矩形波やノコギリ波は低音でも目立つけど耳が痛い..
Rough translation:
Boss BGM
BGM uses the restricted format output from PxTone.
So far, there are a total of 5 sounds: triangle wave + square wave + sawtooth wave + bass drum + hi-hat (closed).
Uses a beat tempo that is divisible by 60 frames.
Bass is hard to hear with small speakers.
But when I adjust the volume accordingly, the earphones are hard this time.
Square waves and sawtooth waves stand out even in the bass, but my ears hurt ..

packages.name: smwmusic-rockfish-unreleased-life-on-the-ship
packages.title: Rockfish (Unreleased) - Life on the Ship
packages.description:
A calm, but upbeat theme from a later version of Rockfish, where you control a human, instead of a fish.
This game was being developed by Pixel, the same person who made Cave Story and Kero Blaster, and then was cancelled in 2012, in order to work on other projects at the time.
Until then, he never talked about it, when after recently, he started posting about this game again on twitter, and then, posted this cute little song, in which I felt like porting it.

It does uses the KSS's soundfont.

packages.name: smwmusic-rudra-no-hihou-light-under-the-sea-underwater-city-remix

packages.description:
Did an arrangement of Underwater City from Rudra no Hihou (Treasure of the Rudras in English). Thought it'd be fun to do my own take on another Squ'enix theme, though I have not gotten the chance to play this game yet. Mostly heard this OST from other hacks and from listening to the soundtrack on my own time in the past.

Regardless, absolutely amazing theme!! Has a very ancient yet magical vibe that Square was definitely known for doing with a lot of their traditional RPG OSTs at the time.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. B Minor w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch - Listening-Only)
2. B Minor (Remix Pitch, turned on default)
3. A Minor (Original Pitch)
4. C Minor (Custom Pitch)

packages.name: smwmusic-secret-of-mana-distant-thunder
packages.title: Secret of Mana - Distant Thunder
packages.description:
A lengthy and complex prog-rock-influenced track from Secret of Mana, composed by Hiroki Kikuta. This song uses a method of composition called "beat displacement", in which the percussion is designed so that the snares/hi-hat hits have inconsistent patterns and never land on the same beat. This made the first two channels of this song an absolute nightmare to transcribe. If I've made any errors on that front, I apologize and will fix them if they're pointed out to me. Otherwise, this is a more-or-less identical recreation of the original song.

This could work in a relaxed level, perhaps fitting especially well in a jungle/forest or beach stage. I could also see it being at home in an overworld or town setting.

Due to issues with ARAM limitations, the original SMW samples @7 and Thunder are overwritten. If you need to use those samples with this song, however, then enough room can be made simply by removing/reducing the echo effect.

Requested by Brutapode89.

packages.name: smwmusic-secret-of-mana-distant-thunder-trials-of-mana-style
packages.title: Secret of Mana - Distant Thunder (Trials of Mana style)
packages.description:
A friendly tune to be played in desert or jungle settings, sounds like adventure.

I cannot believe how tedious and grindy it was to try myself on this and honest I was feeling like I reached my limits. It features a lot of instrument changes among each channel, and deciphering the clues I got on the original spc about pan or vibrato, was a chore too. Re-working it with Trials of Mana samples was definitely an interesting task, and I found out Trials of Mana neither has proper claps, nor a bassoon. So the aesthetic I went for here is more similar to desert tracks like Harvest November, that rely very much on flute.

It is released for the Winter C3. (re-work)

@7 (Bonus End Fanfare) has been omitted.

versions.title: Secret of Mana - Distant Thunder (Trials of Mana style)

packages.name: smwmusic-secret-of-mana-meridian-dance-resampled
packages.title: Secret of Mana - Meridian Dance (Resampled)
packages.description:
An epic and fast-paced, but at the same time, majestic final boss song. Makes extensive usage of ARAM, so some SMW samples have been disabled for it. I've included a more SMW compatible version for convenience.

Samples omitted: 09 SMW @7.brr, 0D SMW @14.brr, 0F SMW @21.brr, 11 SMW @17.brr, (13 SMW Thunder.brr)*.
INCOMPATIBLE WITH: Bonus End music, (Blargg roar SFX, Thunder SFX, Valley of Bowser appears SFX, Castle destruction bomb SFX)*.
*Items in parenthesis are not a concern in the more SMW compatible version.

If you need even more samples enabled, you have the option to lower the echo delay (at the cost of sound quality). Find "$F1 $02 $A2 $01" in Meridian Dance [Resampled] (More SMW Compatible).txt, lower the $02, and then try re-enabling the sample you need. Note, however, that $02 is already a low echo delay and decreasing it further might make the echo sound really shallow. Consider working around the custom samples instead, provided you have the knowledge or someone willing to do it.

packages.name: smwmusic-shin-megami-tensei-blasphemous-souls-castle-of-the-four-gods-remix
packages.title: Shin Megami Tensei - Blasphemous Souls ~ Castle of the Four Gods (Remix)
packages.description:
Did an arrangement of Castle of the Four Gods from Shin Megami Tensei. Started this months back and had it sitting on my PC collecting dust. I thought it'd be neat to finish this port, since I've always wanted to arrange a Shin Megami Tensei theme. Also, I swear to God, it's clear SMT1's SNES OST had some budget cuts with its version of the OST (makes sense given how kinda simple yet effective these songs are in spite of the very obvious lower quality samples), but the Sega CD version just pushes the soundtrack to its limit.

Castle of the Four Gods is my favorite track from every version of SMT1, and I wanted to have both the energy of the Sega CD version while also sticking to the roots of the SNES version with this mix.

Also, this is easily one of my smallest song files I've uploaded in a long time (not counting any jingles I've made at all in that time).

HUGE CONFESSION
Huge fan of the OST (listen to it way too often, ESPECIALLY THE SEGA CD VERSION 'CUZ MY GOD IS IT AMAZING!!!), but I get goose bumps every time I try playing any of the 16-Bit Megami Tensei games. That in-game art style (along with the first person camera), man... the very clay-like look it has got me sleeping with one eye open at night. Also doesn't help whenever it's complimented with a really freaky demon design that usually wouldn't get to me in any other art style.

Maybe watching gameplay of the game when I was like 10 did it, 'cuz that really got me shit scared when I saw some of the demon designs back then (btw, this was before I got into Castlevania), and then I watched Marsh's videos on SMT1 and IF, and that still gave me goose bumps. I could never get traumatized with FNAF or a regular horror-ass jumpscare, but looking at some of the Megami Tensei SNES trilogy sprites for more than 10 seconds will get to me. Maybe one day I'll be able to play them if they get like remakes that don't have the OG sprites (great opportunity for Atlus to finally release those games overseas on devices worth a damn instead of that mobile port that's lost media now because it never got updated for modern devices).


Important:
ㅤ♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. C Minor w/ Slight Detune (Remix Pitch)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. C Minor (Original Pitch)ㅤ[turned on by default]
ㅤ3. C# Minor (Custom Pitch 1)
ㅤ4. D Minor (Custom Pitch 2)
ㅤ5. A# Minor (Custom Pitch 3)

There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
ㅤ1. Enables the voice clip, but sacrifices SMW-Compatibility (Voice Enabled)ㅤ[Listening-Only]
ㅤ2. Disables the voice clip & Decreases the Echo (LOWER Echo)ㅤ[turned on by default]

versions.title: Shin Megami Tensei - Blasphemous Souls ~ Castle of the Four Gods (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-shinobi-iii-return-of-the-ninja-master-alone-in-the-flames-solitary-remix
packages.title: Shinobi III: Return Of The Ninja Master - Alone in the Flames ~ Solitary (Remix)
packages.description:
Did an arrangement of Solitary from Shinobi III: Return of the Ninja Master. Once again, was feeling the old-school genesis mood and decided to do another Shinobi III banger. First heard this in a Sonic romhack many years back, and it holds up as one of my favorite themes from Shinobi III.

It has this great balance between being a very badass theme while also having a bit of a somber tone as if you're just entering a dark area. It's freaking perfect!!!

Important:
♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:
1. C Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)
2. C# Minor (Custom Pitch)

packages.description:
Did an arrangement of Whirlwind from Shinobi III: Return of the Ninja Master. I knew this day would come, and it did. Hooded Edge Whirlwind remix is finally real. I've achieved my goal, and I can finally rest in spaghetti, never forgetti. A S C E N D S

What do I even need to say about this song that hasn't already been said by any hardcore SEGA fan. It's one of the best songs to come out of a Genesis cartridge and is just so freaking intense!!!

Great song for any auto-scroller / auto-runner stages given the original context of this song in the game.

packages.description:
The uncertainly strong stage 1 theme from Shuusou Gyoku, which has a heavy sense of an adventure beginning. Would probably best fit early-game levels with somewhat of a more serious tone. The key of the song is also based on the ZUN's later arrangement, although slightly flat because I felt it gave it a certain charm. The mixing is mostly based on SC-88 recordings of the song, though there's some sprinkles of the GM mixing as well.

On the technical side, this was an intersting song to port because, 8 channels barely being enough aside, there are lots of sections where there's tons of channels of @1 playing together, which thankfully don't overlap (somehow).

I took some slight liberties with the panning, especially with the square waves, since the original uses a lot of same-note/different-instrument channels panned away from each other (which I didn't have space for here), and had a lot of the unique channels exclusively panned to the left, which would end up a bit obnoxious.

packages.name: smwmusic-some-kind-of-mechanical-abomination
packages.title: Some Kind of Mechanical Abomination
packages.description:
...what is that thing?!

Welcome to the archival series! These were created long ago for a homebrew project (of which this song I don't ever recall sending in, specifically because it is a segment of something extremely large and never finished that had musical branches planned) that never really got off the ground. These songs were never authentic SNES music in the first place, mostly because they pre-date SNESMod's entire existence and also pre-date my ability to compile the tools (XMSNES did exist, though, which was by the same author). And on your side, to my knowledge you really only had Addmusic Java to work with, to put in perspective how long ago this was. Therefore, until recently, these songs were never properly checked for sample filesize in particular and thus were never ported over. This one was initially done on 8/29/07.

WARNING: This song has multiple stock sample substitutions due to memory constraints, and has a set of sample groups that should be added to the Addmusic_sample groups.txt file to facilitate this. These affect the following:
  • Miss song (uses a non-stock sample)
  • Stage Clear song (uses a new truncated version of a stock sample)
  • P-Switch song
  • Contact ($1DF9 SFX ID $02) and Clap + Pop ($1DF9 SFX ID $19) SFX
  • All Thunder-based SFX (including Blargg and affecting $1DF9 SFX IDs $21, $25, $27, $29 and $1DFC SFX IDs $1A, $2C) ($1DFC SFX ID $1A (the Castle Destruction Bomb SFX) is not recommended, mostly because it's quite a bit more reliant on the original sample than the others, being a single note)
  • Yoshi SFX ($1DFC SFX ID $1F) and Bonus End song (uses a non-stock sample) (Bonus End is not recommended, while Yoshi... will sound quite a bit different, but at least is more usable SFX-wise... note that Bonus End has other substitutions, but those came out better than the sample shared with Yoshi noted here)

You have 0xE7 bytes of leeway from AddmusicK 1.0.11's stock state for whatever extra sound data you want to add on, but you otherwise have no extra luxury space-wise, as the sample memory combined with this is otherwise nearly maxed out... so yes, this is a pretty expensive song memory-wise, mainly with the sample data. You have been warned.

NOTE: A higher quality version is provided that has a couple of higher quality samples. However, it is incompatible with Super Mario World because it requires !noSFX to be enabled in the user defines.

packages.name: smwmusic-sonic-colors-somber-blue-sea-aquarium-park-act
packages.title: Sonic Colors - Somber Blue Sea ~ Aquarium Park Act 1 (Remix)
packages.description:
𝗡𝗼 𝗰𝗼𝗽𝘆𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗹𝗮𝘄 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗴𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗽 𝗺𝗲!

Did an arrangement of Aquarium Park Act 1 from Sonic Colors. With all the hype surrounding Sonic Colors Ultimate / the series 30th anniversary and the remix to this theme being showcased recently, I had to arrange this song, and Jesus! This might have been my most difficult one yet, which was amazing!!

This song is beautiful. It has a calm yet sad tone with some super freaking catchy melodies to accompany it. It perfectly fits the water-type zone and is a song that'll stay in your head even after you turn off that Wii console. It also brings brings back memories of me buying this game (along with Kirby's Epic Yarn) as a kid and spending hours on both games. I still love this game a ton and was my first introduction to the boost formula games.

Important:
♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi, P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

versions.title: Sonic Colors - Somber Blue Sea ~ Aquarium Park Act 1 (Remix)

packages.name: smwmusic-sonic-forces-sunset-heights-arrangement
packages.title: Sonic Forces - Sunset Heights (Arrangement)
packages.description:
This is an arrangement of Sunset Heights from Sonic Forces. Mostly used samples from different SNES games for this one, along with a few custom samples here and there so I could get a good enough feel for this. I'm still not too satisfied with the overdriven guitar choice (mostly since I couldn't find a better suited one for this song, and I didn't want to do another port with the MMX1 overdriven guitar, so), but other than that, I think it's fine.

Anyway, use this if you need some kind of a "tables have turned on your favor" situation, like when a final boss is kicking your ass, and then you somehow get enough power to defeat it, and you KNOW you can't fail everyone or else the world will be destroyed kinda situation; I know, hella specific, but still

packages.description:
The song that plays for one of the Titan fights in Sonic Frontiers, A.K.A widely considered by many to be the hypest fuckin' thing in that game, and for damn good reason.

Anyway, for me at least, this seems to be best suited to boss and final boss fights almost exclusively, so I dunno whether or not it can fit in a level, but regardless I've added a looped and non-looped version to fit whatever needs you desire... well, technically you'll have to manually edit the .txt file for that to work (change the ? in the text file to / and vice-versa basically), but I just didn't want to clutter up the .zip file with too much shit this time around so uh, yeah.

packages.name: smwmusic-sonic-heroes-casino-park-re-arranged
packages.title: Sonic Heroes - Casino Park (re-arranged)
packages.description:
This sounds more like a sky song than a casino song. For me it has a strong Tails characterization.

Re-instrumentation is done to fit SNES sound limits; I've done my best to keep the most relevant pieces of drums; and also I've got rid of the different effects and drums patterns changing over iterations of the song, to keep it less busy. But in my book it fits well.

I could not have done that without my heavy use of musicalman's samples, so big thanks on that.

Requested by user OrangeBronzeDaisy.

packages.name: smwmusic-sonic-heroes-this-machine-team-dark-s-theme
packages.title: Sonic Heroes - This Machine (Team Dark's Theme)
packages.description:
This is Team Dark's theme song from Sonic Heroes, which was requested by StrikeForcer. When he first asked me to do this song, I wasn't too into the idea back then, and back then I also found it to be too complicated to be done. However, I slowly got more and more interested in this song, and honestly it actually wasn't as hard as I thought, mostly due to all the recent techniques I've learned that helped a lot here, especially chord sampling. Well, I hope you like this I guess (even if you wanted a unsampled version instead) :P

Anyway, due to the way the song is structured, I think the best way to use this is for a long and badass intro sequence, or if you want it for something more plausible, a badass ending sequence. However, since it's looped, you could use this for a level as well; I mean, why not, it's your hack after all lol

Oh, and another thing: this song is preeeeeeetty big, mostly due to the fact this song is literally 3 minutes long, so if you need more space for something else, think about it before you use this. That's all lmao

packages.title: Sonic the Hedgehog - Labyrinth Zone
packages.description:
The disproportionately chill sounding fourth level from Sonic the Hedgehog. This level is infamous for being a slow water level with many tricks and dangers and an annoying boss to contend with, but it's honestly not as bad as people claim it to be. As such, this song is perfect for levels where Mario has to speed from air pocket to air pocket to avoid drowning.

Uses noise, so be careful of noise SFX.

packages.name: smwmusic-sonic-the-hedgehog-marble-zone
packages.title: Sonic the Hedgehog - Marble Zone
packages.description:
The somewhat slow and sad second stage theme of Sonic the Hedgehog. Fitting, for a stage whose gameplay is in fact very slow compared to what you'd expect from Sonic.

There's two customizable parameters here: vibrato and octave. You can choose between a slow, subtle vibrato, or a fast and pronounced one. packages.name: smwmusic-sonic-the-hedgehog-star-light-zone
packages.title: Sonic the Hedgehog - Star Light Zone
packages.description: The very pleasant, very starry, very night, very green fifth level from Sonic the Hedgehog. Given this level is the predecessor to Scrap Brain Zone, the most mechanized level by a country mile, it really makes you wonder whether or not this place is a Robotnik creation. It's essentially a glorified construction zone, but it's also speedy and honestly pretty non-threatening like Green Hill Zone. The worst part about it is probably that there's no checkpoints, which I guess is supposed to make it harder? Maybe it's South Island's symbolic allegory to Florida, a place where you go to live the end of your days. There are no checkpoints in life, and there will be no restarting from the middle in death. Unless you're about to fight Robotnik; it's Mobian law to put a checkpoint there. And Miami's in the background.
