This tool converts music files used in console video games into standard MIDI and DLS/SF2 files. It also plays these files in-program.

Notes:
- Requires Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 or later runtimes to be installed to run.
- This version is 64-bit only. Versions for macOS and other platforms can be found in the GitHub page.

packages.name: tools-vsnes-2
packages.title: vSNES 2.91
packages.description: In SMW hacking, this has mainly the same purpose as BGMapper, but this has a GUI (it's not DOS). It also has a lot more features, try it out for yourself. It also opens SNES9x savestates, and maybe a few others.

packages.name: tools-wav2msu
packages.title: wav2msu
packages.description: wav2msu is a small tool made by Kawa; it makes conversion from  ordinary Windows .wav file to byuu's custom .pcm files (used for MSU-1 tracks), without the need for a hex editor.

packages.name: tools-xkas-0-06
packages.title: xkas 0.06.1
packages.description:
This version of xkas is romi's changes originally meant for the Variable Width Font Cutscene Tool.

Romi's changes from the normal xkas:
-PEA works with labels
-the base command works with branches
-can now use MVN $7E,$12 instead of MVN $127E

packages.name: tools-xkas-plus
packages.title: xkas-plus
packages.description:
xkas-plus is an assembler. It is an extension of xkas v14. It can apply assembly patches directly onto modified roms.

Supported architectures:
GBA THUMB CPU (ARM7TDMI THUMB)
SNES CPU (WDC 65816)
SNES SMP (Sony SPC700)
NES CPU (MOS 6502)
TG-16 / PC Engine CPU (Hudson HuC6280)
WDC 65C02 / 65SC02
CSG 65CE02

packages.name: tools-xkas2asar-v0
packages.title: xkas2asar v0.3
packages.description:
This tool converts xkas patches to asar patches. Should work on all basic patches and most complicated ones.

Warning: May not work with all patches. Always backup your ROM before using any file generated and avoid complex patches.

packages.name: tools-ycompress-1
packages.title: Ycompress 1.10
packages.description:
This program can decompress and dump most of the graphics in Yoshi's Island, so that they can be modified by your SNES tile editor of choice. The program can then be used to recompress and insert the graphics back into the ROM.

Instructions on using the program are within the readme.txt file included in the zip file.

Version 1.10 January 1, 2022
-added 64 bit build of the program, which you can find in the x64
folder.
-added support for unicode filenames/paths when running on a unicode
OS.
-added support for ROMs without a copier header.

packages.name: tools-yi-entrance-editor
packages.title: YI Entrance Editor
packages.description:
The Entrance Editor for SMW2: Yoshi's Island. This tool is created due to the lack of entrance position editing in both Eggvine and Golden Egg.

Inside contains:
-Midway entrance editor
-Regular entrance editor

packages.name: tools-yoshi-s-island-level-tool-v1
packages.title: Yoshi's Island Level Tool - v1.2
packages.description:
This tool can be used to export/import level data and entrances between any version (currently supports U1.0 and J1.0)

It includes a tool to apply ASAR patches (pre-included or custom files) on the ROM

Changelog - 1.2:
- Now it accepts romhacks with custom titles
- Updated pre-included patches: gsufix
- Added vanilla icons to levels list based on main entrance data

packages.name: tools-yy-chr-net-version-english-japanese
packages.title: YY-CHR (.NET Version, English/Japanese)
packages.description:
YY-CHR is a dot editor that can display and edit images contained in ROMs of old home games such as NES and SNES.
In addition, tools [ROM Palette Editor] and [PRG Pattern Editor] for editing palettes and BG patterns are included.

This is the .NET version. For the non-.NET version, see here.

This is the current build 2021/06/06

Changes since last update here:
2021/06/06
PRG Pattern Editor
Add 16x16(16x8) to sorted view

2021/06/05
No update of YY-CHR.net this time.

Palette Editor Tool [ROM Palette Editor].
Fixed a bug (UI collapse when switching address display, etc.)
Added support for MSX1/MSX2 palettes.
Simplified palette check setting to only ON/OFF.

PRG Pattern Editor
Fixed bugs (exceptions when changing editing size, wrong editing position when sorting and displaying, wrong movement and display around the end of the file, etc.)
CHR/PRG (ROM) files can now be opened by dragging and dropping files.
Added option to show CHR images in palette. ON by default.

packages.name: tools-yy-chr-v0-99-beta
packages.title: YY-CHR v0.99 Beta 2012
packages.description:
YY-CHR is a graphic editing program, which can edit bitplane formats of most of the consoles.

This is the most recent non-.NET version. For the .NET version, see here.

If everything is either Japanese or garbled characters, read this tutorial on how to fix it before asking questions!

packages.name: tools-zmz-v1
packages.title: ZMZ v1.08
packages.description:
ZMZ combines the GUI of ZSNES with a Libretro backend; this allows people who like ZSNES' interface but dislike its poor emulation accuracy to get the best of both worlds.

It ships with an intermediate Snes9x version (newer than 1.53) by default; if it's too slow, try Snes9x-Next, or if you prefer bsnes, grab one from the same source. Note that some features, like layer toggle and SPC dumping, may not work with non-default cores.

It is also only compatible with x86 cores; ignore x86_64 cores even if you have a 64bit cpu. To switch core, go to Misc->Libretro.

packages.name: uberasm-100-coin-prize
packages.title: 100 Coin Prize
packages.description:
This is the 100 Coin Prize patch, converted to UberASM. Instead of a 1‐up, Mario gets a star or a powerup when he gets 100 coins. You can configure what Mario is given upon collecting 100 coins, and you can optionally re‐enable the 1‐up reward in addition to the star/powerup prize.

Credit is unnecessary.

packages.name: uberasm-1up-or-code-at-certain-score-checkpoints-v1
packages.title: 1UP (or code) at Certain Score Checkpoints V1.1
packages.description:
This simple code grants the player an extra life at certain checkpoints in the score. More details in the .asm file.

Requested by LucasRCD.

Changelog
yoshifanatic's Update
- Made this compatible with asar 2.0.
- Fixed a bug where you wouldn't be given a reward unless all 3 score bytes were greater than the 3 current checkpoint score bytes (ie. 15,000 < 10,000 because the DC in #$05DC was less than the E8 in #$03E8).
- Changed the default reward code to one that spawns a 1-up score sprite instead of incrementing the life counter directly.
- Made this work for Luigi as well. Note that this requires an extra free RAM byte.

versions.title: 1UP (or code) at Certain Score Checkpoints V1.1

packages.name: uberasm-action-on-enemy-defeat
packages.title: Action on Enemy Defeat
packages.description:
This UberASM will run an action whenever Mario defeats an enemy (killed by jumping on them, with cape, shells, star, sliding etc.). You can choose between some premade options (switch ON/OFF, hurt Mario, give coins or time) or add your own code. Check the asm file for additional information.
Requires 12 bytes of freeram (22 on SA-1).
Note that it doesn't work for enemies burnt with fireballs (besides Chucks, because they don't turn into coins).

packages.name: uberasm-add-color
packages.title: Add Color 8 to Event Path Fade
packages.description: This UberASM will fade color 8 in palette rows 4-7 during events in the same way as colors 1-7. This allows you to add an additional color to layer 2 tiles that fade in and out during event path fade.

versions.title: Add Color 8 to Event Path Fade

packages.name: uberasm-aimed-bullet-bill-eerie-generator
packages.title: Aimed Bullet Bill / Eerie Generator
packages.description: This code generates Bullet Bills or Eeries from the side Mario is facing, and at his height, creating a totally predictable pattern as opposed to SMW's.

packages.name: uberasm-airjump-and-airspin
packages.title: Airjump and Airspin
packages.description:
Allows the player to jump in the air. You can also make it limited so that after a number of jumps in a row gets disabled (not the buttons, in case if something also uses the jump button).

Also includes a NSMBW styled airspin move that allows the player to do a short spin in midair (by pressing spinjump, much like shaking the wii remote)

packages.name: uberasm-airjump-with-jump-counter
packages.title: Airjump with Jump Counter
packages.description:
This is HammerBrother's Airjump uberASM code, but with a jump counter attached to the player that can count up to 9, or count down to 0, or just show infinity.

Credit is optional. Requested by 1UPdudes.

packages.name: uberasm-airship-camera-v1
packages.title: Airship Camera v1.1
packages.description:
This UberASM will make the camera move up and down similarly to SMB3 airships. Check out the asm file for customization options.

v1.1: fixed issue where the camera would drift away in some cases even if using symmetric speed and acceleration values.

packages.name: uberasm-allow-mario-to-pass-his-gas
packages.title: Allow Mario to Pass His Gas
packages.description:
Everyone has to pass their gas, even Mario.
Pressing (or holding) a configurable button will successfully pass Mario's gas, and his gas sound can be modified to the players liking before inserting the code with Asar.

versions.title: Allow Mario to Pass His Gas

packages.name: uberasm-allow-spinjump-from-vine-net-etc
packages.title: Allow Spinjump from Vine/Net/Etc.
packages.description:
This code allows player to spinjump from vine/net and etc. tiles.

Credit is optional.

packages.name: uberasm-alternating-double-jump
packages.title: Alternating Double Jump
packages.description:
A combination of double jump and motor skills.

Mario can jump or spin jump once in the air as long as he switches from jump to spin jump or spin jump to jump. Because the double jump is on a different button from the original jump, it is still possible to perform regrabs. There are sparkles which indicate whether the double jump is available.

packages.name: uberasm-always-wall-run
packages.title: Always Wall-run
packages.description:
Allows the player to wall-run on any wall at pretty much any time. No pink triangle needed!

Information on how to use can be found in "always_wallrun.asm" (the Uberasm file).

This is more or less the same code I used in zynnoir and I's KLDCX entry.

Note: Does not work properly with layer 2.

packages.name: uberasm-anticheat
packages.title: Anticheat
packages.description:
This is an UberASM port of worldpeace's old "Anticheat" patch. If a player tries to cheat at your ROM hack by enabling various debug features present in the vanilla SMW ROM, Mario will die when entering a level. This is to punish them for doing so. This conversion has a few improvements over the original, such as no longer needing free RAM and checking if more debug routines are enabled.

Insert on game mode 14.

packages.name: uberasm-automatic-alternating-jumps-v1
packages.title: Automatic Alternating Jumps V1.1
packages.description:
This makes the player alternate continuously between a normal jump and a spinjump.

yoshifanatic's update
- Made the sound effects configurable. Especially the jump sound, so it's easy to account for AddmusicK.
- Optimized the code a bit by utilizing tables.
- Added checks so the jump doesn't happen while in a lakitu cloud, P-Balloon, climbing, stunned, doing the victory pose, or while the game is paused.
- Made it so Mario displays the jump pose when doing the regular jump.
- Made it so the auto jump is more of an auto swim while underwater.

packages.name: uberasm-automatic-walking-v1
packages.title: Automatic Walking v1.1
packages.description:
This simple code disables buttons while giving Mario a fixed X speed. Fairly customizable. Be sure to read the instructions inside before using it.

v1.1
-----
Fixed a bug with input filtering. $0DAC and $0DAA are meant to be untouched so held down inputs aren't processed as newly pressed inputs.

packages.name: uberasm-autosave-bring-up-save-prompt-by-pressing-select
packages.title: Autosave + Bring Up Save Prompt by pressing Select
packages.description:
Following the trend of converting patches to UberASM I decided to convert two patches into one, the first one being Arinsu's save prompt patch, and the second, Alcaro's autosave patch. The main benefit of this patch is not only does both of these original patches work for UberASM now but this version also allows you to still view the overworld since it uses select now instead of the start button, and adds a bit more defines for extra customization like the ability to autosave.

v1.1
---
* Fixed a bug where the game could lag if multiple overworld codes were used along with the auto-save feature.

versions.title: Autosave + Bring Up Save Prompt by pressing Select

packages.name: uberasm-autotile
packages.title: Autotile
packages.description:
An autotile utility for SMW. This utility allows you to build shapes in Lunar Magic using a single tile and it will merge the tiles in-game using the correct edges.

Tutorial with screenshots here: https://github.com/CircleFriendo/AutotileUberasm

packages.name: uberasm-baby-yoshi-disappears-after-eating-too-much
packages.title: Baby Yoshi Disappears After Eating Too Much
packages.description:
Sequel to "Yoshi Disappears After Eating Too Much", this code does exactly what the title says, with a configurable amount of sprites that must be eaten. It also prevents Baby Yoshi from ever growing up, and there's an option so powerups also don't make him grow up instantly (but just count as 1 eat).

Requested by Sping Bot.

versions.title: Baby Yoshi Disappears After Eating Too Much

packages.name: uberasm-basic-numerical-air-meter-v1
packages.title: Basic Numerical Air Meter V1.1
packages.description:
This simple piece of code places a numerical air meter on the status bar, effectively replacing the stars counter (protip: change the star graphics to a bubble or something for a better impact).

Quite customizable, and SA-1 hybrid.

yoshifanatic's update:
- Fixed an oversight where pausing on the frame the meter updates will cause it to update every frame. You'd also softlock if this happened while in water.
- Created a define that does the effect described in the comments for reversing the air meter.
- Made it so the air meter tile is initialized in init so it displays during the fade in instead of popping in right after.
- Made a few minor code optimizations.

packages.name: uberasm-better-level-fade-in
packages.title: Better Level Fade In
packages.description:
Has this ever happened to you?
You remove the mosaic/pixelation effect because you think it looks ugly, but then you realize now that it's gone it's very obvious that sprites just *pop* into existence once the fade ends, so it just looks ugly again?

Well worry not! This pair of assembly files is here to fix that! This resource skips the "level: fade in" gamemode and handles the fading in the "level" gamemode, giving sprites' codes and other codes a chance to run!
This can not only fix sprites "popping in" but any other "first frame visual anomalies" like for example scrolling codes suddenly snapping layers.

Information on how to insert this can be found in the readme.
Customization options can be found inside "better_fade.asm", for example if you'd like the game to pause/freeze while fading, you can do that. ...and yes.. you can re-enable the mosaic if you want to...

For removing the mosaic from other transitions, a patch is included.

Note: this is most definitely incompatible with patches that change how fading in looks!

packages.name: uberasm-bonus-game-death-fix
packages.title: Bonus Game Death Fix
packages.description:
In vanilla SMW, dying in the level 000/100 bonus game will teleport the player back to the overworld and require them to re-play the level. It'll also reduce their lives counter and consume the 100 bonus stars needed to enter the bonus game.

With this (albeit simple) UberASM code, dying in a bonus game will not decrease the lives counter, but will simply teleport them back to the overworld and trigger events -- paying respect to the fact that they completed the actual level.
It will also play the "Bonus Game End" jingle.

Note that this is intended to be used in "bonus game" rooms only -- as in, the bonus game room entered after collecting 100 bonus stars.

packages.name: uberasm-boost-on-coin-collection
packages.title: Boost on Coin Collection
packages.description: A small and silly UberASM code which gives the player a small vertical boost when a coin gets collected.

packages.name: uberasm-bottomless-pit-code
packages.title: Bottomless Pit Code
packages.description: Also previously known as 'Floor Generator', this makes it so the player cannot move horizontally when offscreen from below, which is useful for people wanting to prevent players from skipping parts of a level from below. You can also set it to hurt or kill the player through a define.

packages.name: uberasm-bullet-time
packages.title: Bullet Time
packages.description:
Bullet Time lets the player (or the creator) intentionally lag the game. This can be used for either good or evil, so be responsible with your newfound power!

A control mechanism is provided that uses the L or R button to control the effect (either hold or press-to-toggle), but the means is provided to code your own, if desired. See the readme for further information.

The amount of slowdown is settable, and can be changed mid-level if writing your own controller. The coin counter in the screenshot shows the current value (60 when not active, 15 when active).

Requested by TheSpreee333 (who also gets the credit for the resource name...I would have picked something a lot more boring)

packages.name: uberasm-candle-flames-in-background
packages.title: Candle Flames in Background
packages.description:
This is a candle flame generator but in a uberASM form. One advantage is that you don't need to put a generator for each entrance in the same level.

Credit is unecessary.

packages.name: uberasm-cape-bug-fix-collection
packages.title: Cape Bug-Fix Collection
packages.description:
This is a collection of cape related bug fixes. Below you can find which ones are included in this patch.

Use as level code or gamemode 14.

-Cape Turnaround Fix: Allows you to always turn around when x or y are pressed during flight.

- Cape Climbing Fix: Fixes the bug where you could maintain flight after jumping off of nets or vines.

- Float Delay Fix: removes the delay between releasing the b button and actually floating with the cape.

- Cape Wallrunning Fix: Fixes the bug where you could twirl your cape while wall running.

Update (4/23/2020): fixed an issue where you couldn't get height when flying with winged Yoshi when !FloatDelayFix = !yes.

packages.name: uberasm-charged-fireball
packages.title: Charged Fireball
packages.description:
This UberASM makes mario shoot a Yoshi Fireball if you hold a fire button (and optionally an additional button, by default R), emulating a charged fireball, just like in many platformer games like Megaman.
Check out the ChargedFire.asm file for customization options.

It also includes a minor patch (to be applied with asar!) and GFX to make Yoshi Fireballs and Flopping Cheep-Cheeps swap tilemaps, so you can have Yoshi Fireballs in every level, optional but recommended (especially if using this in gamemode 14!).

You can find the patch version here.

packages.name: uberasm-configurable-amount-of-baby-yoshi-eats
packages.title: Configurable Amount of Baby Yoshi Eats
packages.description: This simple code will change the required amount of things Baby Yoshi has to eat to grow up for the level you put it in (or for all levels, if used in gamemode 14). Note that powerups will still make him grow immediately, and "double eats" still apply (if he eats 2 things in quick succession, it will count as 3).

versions.title: Configurable Amount of Baby Yoshi Eats

packages.name: uberasm-configurable-yoshi-swallow-timer
packages.title: Configurable Yoshi Swallow Timer
packages.description: This UberASM allows you to configure the Yoshi swallow timer.

packages.name: uberasm-consistent
packages.title: Consistent 8 Frame Cape Float Delay
packages.description:
This patch aims to simulate the vanilla float framerule, which can be between 0 and 16 frames, in a more consistent way. By waiting 8 frames after the input is registered to adjust Mario's falling speed.

So! What does this mean for you and when should you use this patch?

If you have very long falling sections, or just want the falling speed to be based on player input timing and not the float framerule, this patch will make those setups more consistent.

But keep in mind the vanilla float framerule is consistent based on when you jump. This means most kaizo setups will be perfectly consistent with the vanilla framerule...

~If you don't have the player floating/falling for extended periods of time you probably don't need this patch!~

Can be inserted per-level or globally via Gamemode 14.

Original code by xHF01x (please credit him).
SA-1 conversion DJLocks (you don't have to credit me).
Special thanks to NewPointless for help with SA-1 testing.

packages.name: uberasm-consistent-vanilla-walljumps
packages.title: Consistent Vanilla Walljumps
packages.description:
The walljump asm featured in KLDC 2021's entry #45 (Not Cataclysm). Now updated with layer 2 support and a customizable leniency for the walljump itself.

This walljump asm mimics the physics of the TAS-only walljumps that are frequently seen in pit hacks but makes them consistently performable for a human player. To be specific: Mario always clips the wall if he hits it with 29 or more horizontal speed while moving downwards and the window for the jump input has been increased from 1 to 5 frames (on default settings).

If you decide to use this, you should use a patch that disables the real vanilla walljumps as the player may get confused and frustrated otherwise.

This can be inserted per level or in gamemode 14.

packages.name: uberasm-controller-read-optimization
packages.title: Controller Read Optimization
packages.description:
Saves a little NMI time by moving the controller read to the start of the game loop.

Use this if you need more NMI time to change blocks, exanimate, upload dynamic graphics, etc. Running out of NMI time may appear as broken gradients and a black bar at the top of the screen.

Be sure to use FastROM and 'Lunar Magic's "VRAM Patch" Optimization' in addition to this.

packages.name: uberasm-counterbreak
packages.title: Counterbreak
packages.description:
This code allows you to reset various statuses and counters when the player returns to the overworld, including:
- Powerup
- Item box item
- Yoshi
- Coins
- Bonus stars
- Score
- Midway point
- Life count

To use, insert into game mode 0C.

Note: If you want to disable midpoints, this requires the "Bonus Game Midpoint Fix" patch to fix a vanilla quirk that will prevent events from running.

packages.name: uberasm-credits-utilities
packages.title: Credits Utilities
packages.description:
This UberASM provides some useful (optional) functions for when the player reaches the credits (which can be either the vanilla credits cutscene, or a credits sublevel they're teleported to or whatever):
- Mark the final level as beaten and increase the exits count.
- Run a (silent) event that will show as already run next time the OW is loaded (post-credits stuff?).
- Open a direction on the OW from the current level (probably best used in conjunction with the silent event).
- Change the current player's OW position (teleport back to the start of the game, or to a new map, etc.)
- Save the game.

See the ASM file for more info.

packages.name: uberasm-custom-layer
packages.title: Custom Layer 2 Rise/Sink
packages.description: This allows you to create simple layer 2 rise/sink commands. No credit needed. Everything you need to know is in the ASM file.

packages.name: uberasm-custom-scroll-limits-megaman-flip-screen-effect
packages.title: Custom Scroll Limits (+ Megaman Flip Screen Effect)
packages.description:
This ASM pack enables you to have custom scroll limits in your level.

It also comes with a feature of a flip-screen effect seen in Megaman, Metroid, Legend of Zelda, Celeste and many others to divide a level into rooms. These can easily be set by editing the table.

Of course, I also made a single screen version (but each zone will always be 256x256, not overlapping).

Very useful for designing levels to have areas where you don't want horizontal or vertical scrolls.

versions.title: Custom Scroll Limits (+ Megaman Flip Screen Effect)

packages.name: uberasm-customizable-high-and-low-tides
packages.title: Customizable "High and Low" Tides
packages.description: This UberASM allows you to have a different behavior for the "high and low" tides on a level basis. What you can change is: time between tide movements, Y speed, Y acceleration, high and low position. It requires 7 bytes of freeram and to apply the provided patch with Asar. For more info and instructions, check out the readme file.

packages.name: uberasm-customizable-layer
packages.title: Customizable Layer 2 Smash
packages.description:
This code replicates the behavior of the vanilla Layer 2 Smash sprites, meaning that it has 3 movement phases: "go up" phase, "go down a bit" phase and "smash down" phase.
You can customize its behavior by changing the position, speed and waiting time for each of the phases, and set different values for each screen. You can also change the "screen shake" timer (or disable it) for each screen. By changing these values you can also change the nature of the phases as well: for example, you could make it smash up and down without a middle phase, or make the middle phase go back up a bit instead of down.
You can also choose to move it horizontally or vertically, as well as moving layer 1 instead of layer 2.
Check out the asm file for more info. Comes with some example values (used for the first GIF) to show how they work.

packages.name: uberasm-cutscene-mode
packages.title: Cutscene Mode
packages.description:
An uberASM code that freezes Mario in place and locks most controller inputs to prevent pausing/LR scrolling/item dropping, which allows the creation of simple custom cutscenes, so you should either press a button or wait a certain amount of time to advance/end it. It's meant to be the best alternative over sprites that do similar function, because it will prevent wasting sprite slots, is more customizable, optimized, SA-1 compatible, and comes with even more functionalities. The ZIP file also includes an optional ASM file that should fix a certain issue related to OW level setting flags in case you're using a certain OW teleporting action in the cutscene code.

Be sure to read the Readme and the ASM files for more detailed information.

packages.name: uberasm-cycle-through-powerups
packages.title: Cycle through Powerups
packages.description:
This customizable UberASM changes Mario's powerup every X frames.

See ASM for more Defines options.
It uses 2 Bytes of FreeRAM addresses.

packages.name: uberasm-dark-glass-transparent-settings
packages.title: "Dark Glass" / Transparent Settings
packages.description: You can mess around with the CGADSUB settings with this - the way these work is that Layer 2 only appears behind Layer 1. I've provided a description of a few different settings.

packages.name: uberasm-dark-overworld
packages.title: Dark Overworld
packages.description:
This UberASM will create an effect similar to what can be seen in SMB3's Dark World, where the map will be pitch black with a small circle of light following Mario. Additionally, there's an optional feature where the light will increase in size when certain events are activated, and the effect will go away completely when another event is activated, inspired by Pokémon Emerald's Battle Pyramid gimmick.
By default it won't affect layer 3, so the border stays visible, but it can be changed. For all the possible settings look in the asm file.
Since it uses window 2, it works nicely with the original Overworld HDMA effects (save/2P prompt, submap switching transition), but it includes a hijack and some hex edits (applied automatically) to prevent those from disabling the effect. If you remove this UberASM from your ROM, patch the included "unpatch.asm" file with Asar to undo these edits.
By the way, the "increase light" effect happens as soon as the OW fades in: in the GIFs it happens after the event because of the Event Debug patch.

Note 1: if the circle is too large, it can cause the game to lag when it needs to be updated (not on SA-1), so keep that in mind. Additionally, very large circles may have some "glitchy" looking results at the very edge of the circle, which may be noticeable for a split second when the "make the effect go away" event triggers if Mario happens to be towards the top of the screen.
Note 2: if used on the main map, the circle will stay fixed in place during the "look around the map" state. Either disable it, or keep it to allow the player to look at what's ahead from a small view.
Note 3: if set to cover layer 3, it will also cover stuff like the save/2P prompt letters.
Note 4: it uses an HDMA channel, by default 6, and 453 bytes of free RAM (mostly for the windowing table).

packages.name: uberasm-different-gravity-code-v1
packages.title: Different Gravity Code V1.1
packages.description:
It's a Shog's "Diffrent Gravity Generator", except it's now uberASM code. Fixed and added extra option.

It makes player jump higher (or lower, depending on option).

packages.name: uberasm-disable-cape-flight
packages.title: Disable Cape Flight
packages.description:
This simple UberASM code will disable Mario's flight with the Feather Cape, but it will still be able to carry items and run.

Unlike the tweak that does that same function, this UberASM can be applied in a per-level basis! But you can also use it in all levels through GameMode 14.

packages.name: uberasm-disable-controller-buttons
packages.title: Disable Controller Buttons
packages.description:
This is a simple uberASM that allows you to disable any single or combination of controller inputs for the duration of a level.
You cannot disable combinations of buttons without also disabling them individually.
For example, if you wanted Y and B to function individually but disable Y+B pressed together, this is not possible with this patch in its current form.

Could be used to disable spin jump or regular jump in a level, or any directional input, or any combination of these.
Can also be used to disable L/R, so you could use this to disable screen scrolling on a per level basis if you so desired.

Credit is always appreciated :)

packages.name: uberasm-disable-death-scrolling
packages.title: Disable Death Scrolling
packages.description: This makes it so that when the player dies, the screen doesn't scroll vertically anymore.

packages.name: uberasm-disable-ducking-while-climbing
packages.title: Disable Ducking While Climbing
packages.description:
This is a small patch that fixes a glitch where if Mario ducks and climbs a fence or vine, he will stay ducked even if you release the key and jump.

It is so small that no credits are required.

packages.name: uberasm-disable-hdma-during-transitions
packages.title: Disable HDMA During Transitions
packages.description:
This simple code will prevent custom HDMA effects to carry over during black screen transitions (such as when going into a pipe, loading the Time Up/Game Over screen, going from the overworld to a level, going from a boss fight to a cutscene/credits, etc.). It's meant to be a less intrusive and non-buggy version of the "HDMA v3.5" patch.
Check out the readme for instructions.

packages.name: uberasm-disable-l-r-scroll
packages.title: Disable L/R Scroll
packages.description:
This simple UberASM code lets you disable screen scrolling if you press the L or R buttons.

Unlike the patch that does that same function, this UberASM lets you apply it in a per-level basis! But you can also use it in all levels through GameMode 14.

packages.name: uberasm-disable-powerup-powerdown-animations
packages.title: Disable Powerup/Powerdown Animations
packages.description:
This UberASM disables the Mushroom/FireFlower/Feather powerup animations and the hurt powerdown animation. You can also disable just one of the two if you want using the defines in the asm file.
Requested by MoghedienNinek.

packages.name: uberasm-disable-throwing-items-upwards
packages.title: Disable Throwing Items Upwards
packages.description:
When inserted, this makes it so you can't throw items upwards. Originally a patch, but it's been converted into an UberASM.

Insert on a per level basis or on game mode 14.

Requested by 35TCB77

packages.name: uberasm-discoshell-on-off
packages.title: Discoshell ON/OFF
packages.description: Change shells to a discoshell with an on/off switch.

packages.name: uberasm-dkc-blackout-basement-lights-on-off
packages.title: DKC - Blackout Basement: Lights On/Off
packages.description:
An UberASM to turn on and turn off lights.

Customizable, please open the file ".asm" to customize it.

You can change the time it lasts, how dark the level becomes, and the sound effect is uses.

Requested by Ayami.

packages.name: uberasm-dolphin-generator
packages.title: Dolphin Generator
packages.description:
This is a UberASM version of dolphin, left/right, generator, sprites CF and D0 in SMW.

Requested by RZRider.

packages.name: uberasm-donkey-kong-country
packages.title: Donkey Kong Country 2 Navigation Arrows
packages.description:
Remember carol's old DKC2 Navigation Arrows? They're back, in UberASM form!
What this resource does is show arrows in the directions Mario can walk in while on the overworld.
This originally shipped with carol's overworld sprite tool. When that tool was updated by Alcaro and wiiqwertyuiop, they updated the arrows for its use there as well. lx5 then converted them into a patch.
This version, by Arinsu, cleans some code up and adds support for Kevin's Custom Hardcoded Paths patch. Unlike the arrows in patch form, this also works with BOWSIE.

Insert as overworld * code, not as gamemode 0E code, else I've noticed they won't really work.

Requested by Samantha during C3 Winter 2025.

packages.name: uberasm-double-jump
packages.title: Double Jump
packages.description:
This will give Mario the ability to perform and store multiple midair jumps.

This ASM is customizable:
-When On Ground
+Clear stored jumps
+Set to one extra jump
+Keep stored jumps

-Gain an extra jump by collectiong a custom coin
-Set the max amount of jumps mario can store
-Allow spin jumping when holding an item
-Custom jump heights (spin and normal)

packages.name: uberasm-drop-power-ups-at-player-position
packages.title: Drop Power-ups at Player Position
packages.description:
This uberASM code is similar to Item Box to Player Position by HammerBrother. When dropping a power-up from the item box, it'll be placed at player's position.

Note that unlike the aformentioned patch, this code is exclusively for power-ups. The benefit of this is it allows you to have both vanilla item drop and dropping at player's position on a per-level basis (e.g. levels where an item from the item box would be unreachable otherwise).

packages.name: uberasm-duck-walking
packages.title: Duck Walking
packages.description: This code allows Mario to move while ducking without having to gain momentum. Note that Mario's GFX don't change of course, since there's no pose for duck walking originally.

packages.name: uberasm-dynamic-radius-circle-window-v1-1
packages.title: Dynamic Radius Circle Window v1.1.1
packages.description:
This is basically a piece of code to draw a circle window with a given radius. Unlike the one that comes with Effect Tool, this one generates the circle on the run, not using a pre-computed table, allowing you to change the radius anytime you want.

The ASM file comes with some customizable options, such as whether the circle is centered at a fixed position or at Mario, the initial radius and some other stuff.

Notes: don't use it with message boxes, and make sure your level end isn't in the same level of this effect, otherwise stuff will look glitched up when you cross the goal tape or use the keyhole.

If not using the SA-1 patch, turn on the interlacing setting! Otherwise, this will likely cause lag.

Changelog
yoshifanatic's update
- Changed the encoding of CircleWindow.asm to UTF-8 so it'll work in asar 2.0.
- Made this LoROM compatible.
- Added a setting that enables interlacing to save on performance at the cost of making the circle look blurrier in motion. Enabling this is recommended if not using the SA-1 patch.
- Made the HDMA channel customizable.
- Fixed a bug where the circle would not initialize if you exit a sublevel and the circle draws at the exact same on screen position before in the next sublevel.

packages.name: uberasm-earthquake
packages.title: Earthquake
packages.description:
This code will cause the ground to continuously shake. It can be set to play a sound effect, too.

Check the ASM file for customization options.

packages.name: uberasm-easy-chocolate-island
packages.title: Easy Chocolate Island 2 Gimmick
packages.description: This code will allow you to use screen exits to replicate the gimmick found in Chocolate Island 2 in the original Super Mario World, where the number of coins and Yoshi coins you collect and the value of the timer change which sublevels you get sent to.

packages.name: uberasm-easy-cloud-or-p-balloon-left-right
packages.title: Easy Cloud or P-Balloon Left-Right
packages.description: This UberASM allows you to utilize the glitch where holding down the left and right buttons simultaneously while being in a lakitu cloud or p-balloon will cause you to move right faster and clip through walls by using a configurable button.

packages.name: uberasm-end-level-with-dragon-coins
packages.title: End Level with Dragon Coins
packages.description:
This Uberasm will trigger the defined exit and goal march after 5 dragon coins have been collected.

This ASM is based on a request by Apple Boy

packages.name: uberasm-event-camera-pan
packages.title: Event Camera Pan
packages.description:
This UberASM allows you to make the camera scroll to a specified location when running an event (either at the start or before a certain step in the middle of the event), and then return back to its original position afterwards. You can also add a delay before scrolling to make it less abrupt. You can set a different position for every event, and of course set events to not scroll at all (also the effect only applies to the Main Overworld map for obvious reasons, so insert it as Overworld code 00).
Check out the asm file for more info.

packages.name: uberasm-exit-level-by-falling-offscreen
packages.title: Exit Level by Falling Offscreen
packages.description: The name is self-explanatory: this code will exit the level when Mario falls offscreen, similarly to what happens in the original game in the Yoshi wings levels. In the asm file you can choose which exit to trigger (exit without events, normal exit or one of the secret exits).

packages.name: uberasm-exit-percentage-on-the-overworld
packages.title: Exit Percentage on the Overworld
packages.description:
This UberASM will display the current progress in the hack (as percentage of exits gotten) on the overworld border. It can be paired with this patch for consistency. Check out the readme for more information.
This is the second part of Ondore's Lies' request for a percentage counter on file select and overworld.

packages.name: uberasm-exploding-death
packages.title: Exploding Death
packages.description:
This will make the player explode rather than the normal death animation.

Use in either the level(s) you want it to apply or in gamemode 14 to make it apply to every level.


Requested (sort of) by Daizo Dee Von.

packages.name: uberasm-explosive-mechakoopa
packages.title: Explosive Mechakoopa
packages.description:
Mechakoopas explode instead of getting up.

Requested by LadiesMan217.

packages.name: uberasm-fade-from-credits-to-title-screen
packages.title: Fade from Credits to Title Screen
packages.description:
This UberASM code allows the player to return from the credits to the title screen.
I included four possible points of return:
  1. After the credits roll: insert in game mode 1C.
  2. After Yoshi's House "Thank You!" message: insert in game mode 20.
  3. After the enemy credits: insert in game mode 26.
  4. After the "THE END" screen: insert in game mode 29.

Compatible with Kevin's Credits Utilities (and indeed, meant to be used with it): insert said code in game mode 19 to use it with this!

Requested by Bourbaki.

versions.title: Fade from Credits to Title Screen

packages.name: uberasm-fade-from-title-screen-to-file-select-menu
packages.title: Fade from Title Screen to File Select Menu
packages.description:
This resource allows you to slowly transition from the title screen to the file select menu.

There's two files, one of which is meant to be inserted always in game modes 06 and 07, and another you optionally need to insert in game mode 03.

versions.title: Fade from Title Screen to File Select Menu
versions.filename: Fade From Title Screen to File Select Menu.zip

packages.name: uberasm-fading-brightness-hdma-v1
packages.title: Fading Brightness HDMA v1.2
packages.description:
This HDMA code uses RAM instead of fixed values, all dependent on address $0DAE. That allows you to use brightness HDMA with a proper brightness fade instead of removing the fade and having the screen become instantly dark.

Coming with an example.

Read the readme for more information.

packages.name: uberasm-fading-lights-v1-1
packages.title: Fading Lights v1.1.2
packages.description:
This UberASM will fade the brightness in the level in and out. There's two different modes available:
- Constant fading in/out based on a timer.
- Fade based on a certain switch. This can also be of two types: lights go back to bright when hitting a switch, but fade immediately to dark; or they only fade to dark when the switch goes off. Possible switches are: ON/OFF, blue POW, silver POW, red ? block.
In the file you can customize some parameters: how bright/dark the lights go and how long the fade will take.

v1.1:
- Doesn't use a dedicated HDMA channel anymore (smh).
- Uses 2 bytes of freeram instead of 7.
- Smaller code.

v1.1.1:
- Fixed a bug where this causes flashing during level end.

v1.1.2
- Fixed an underflow bug that caused the screen to turn black if !DarkValue was set lower than the default.

packages.name: uberasm-fair-powerup-filters
packages.title: Fair Powerup Filters
packages.description:
This lets you set up 4 types of powerup filters in a per-level basis: small only, big only, no fire flowers and no feathers, taking in account your powerup status and item box item. Unlike most powerup filters though, this won't simply make you lose a filtered powerup, but will restore it once you return to the overworld, much like the Yoshi filters work. For that, 1 byte of free RAM is used.

Additional notes:
-Filtering a fire flower or a feather will replace it with a mushroom.
-There are 2 recovery options for fire flower and feather filters: they can always be recovered, or it can depend on whether the mushroom they got turned into has been preserved. More details in the readme and setup files.

Note that these aren't to be used as level code, but as game modes C and 12! An easy table to set up the activation of the filters is included.

packages.name: uberasm-fall-damage
packages.title: Fall damage
packages.description: Fall damage. I'm sorry.

packages.name: uberasm-fast-bg-scroll
packages.title: Fast BG Scroll
packages.description: This is a disassembly of sprite F4, the fast BG scroll, but as an UberASM. It has been optimized, cleaned, and it allows you to select when the code activates. Either whenever you enter the level or whenever Mario steps on the unused orange platform (sprite 5E) or the flying turn blocks (sprite C1), like the original sprite.

packages.name: uberasm-filter-yoshi
packages.title: Filter Yoshi
packages.description:
This simple uberasm will prevent Yoshi from appearing when spawning in the level, but will keep him in the overworld, basically acting as a No Yoshi Intro without the cutscene.
Requested by DrAnas.

packages.name: uberasm-flag-controlled-slower-music
packages.title: Flag Controlled Slower Music
packages.description: This UberASM will make the music go slower when a certain flag is set, and go back to normal when it's reset. By default it uses the P-Balloon flag (like in SMA2), but you can change it to whatever you want (like ON/OFF switch, ...). Make sure to check the readme for instructions and info. It uses 1 byte of freeram.

packages.name: uberasm-flashlight-effect
packages.title: Flashlight Effect
packages.description:
With this code and the included GFX resources, you can create a spotlight effect that follows the player. GFX includes small and big spotlight circles. It can be set be on layer 1 (not recommend), layer 2 or layer 3.

Make sure you set the scrolling in both directions to "None" for the affected layer.

Note that due to hardware limitations, sprite palettes 8-B are unaffected by the spotlight and will always appear in full visibility. In addition, the colors for the spotlight need to be inverted from how they'll appear in game if you intend on using a custom palette for the spotlight.

If you want to put the spotlight on layer 3 or while making use of mode 0, here are some graphics you can use.

packages.name: uberasm-flip-on-off-on-lr-v1
packages.title: Flip On/Off on LR v1.0
packages.description: Flips On/Off flag when you press either L or R.

packages.name: uberasm-flip-on-off-switch-every-x-frames
packages.title: Flip On/Off Switch Every X Frames
packages.description:
This is a simple LevelASM which makes it so that the on-off switch switches every X amount of frames (defaults to 60 frames = 1 second). The time between switches can be changed, along with some other customization options.

Uses two bytes of free RAM.

Requested by The_Uber_Camper.

versions.title: Flip On/Off Switch Every X Frames

packages.name: uberasm-floating-overworld-v1
packages.title: Floating Overworld v1.1
packages.description:
This code will make the current submap move up and down, like a floating island. Original code by yoshicookiezeus, I optimized it and made it work in any submap.

Note: this code works better in Yoshi's Island and Valley of Bowser. Other submaps are 8 pixels shorter, which causes the bottom row of the adjacent map to be visible when the OW scrolls down. You can avoid this issue by having empty tiles on that row.

v1.1 update: fixed position "drifting" after going in and out of the map repeatedly through a map transition (red path), showing cutoff pixels from the neighbouring maps.

packages.name: uberasm-flutter-jump
packages.title: Flutter Jump
packages.description:
The flutter jump in UberASM format. Works similar to YI's flutter jump. Can now be customized so only one player and/or Yoshi can flutter jump.

Insert as either level ASM to allow flutter jumps only in specific levels or on gamemode 14 so you can do it in all levels.

packages.name: uberasm-free-7e-0de0-7e-0ef4
packages.title: Free $7E:0DE0-$7E:0EF4
packages.description: This simple code frees up the 277 (0x115) bytes of RAM at $7E:0DE0-$7E:0EF4 (a.k.a. $0DE0-$0EF4) for usage in levels, so that it can be used as free RAM without messing up overworld sprites. This can be useful for resources that need a lot of free RAM in the $0000-$1FFF area.

packages.name: uberasm-free-vertical-scroll-no-horizontal-scroll
packages.title: Free Vertical Scroll + No Horizontal Scroll
packages.description:
This simple code includes two features that can turn out useful, especially for vertical levels: free vertical scrolling (which makes the camera always follow Mario, rather than waiting for him to land on something) and no horizontal scrolling (if you want to have a one screen wide vertical level).
Both settings can be turned on or off independently in the asm file. Make sure to enable "Vertical Scroll at Will" in Lunar Magic if using the free vertical scroll setting.

versions.title: Free Vertical Scroll + No Horizontal Scroll

packages.name: uberasm-freeze-sprites-with-l-r
packages.title: Freeze Sprites with L/R
packages.description:
This code will freeze all sprites on screen when L or R is pressed, while allowing the player to still move around and interact with the level as normal. You can control the duration sprites are frozen for, enable retriggering of the freeze, enable freezing of sprite behaviours as well as their position, and more. Has a lot of potential for interesting kaizo and puzzle setups.

Note that depending on the settings & ROM type, this code can use quite a lot of freeRAM (up to 639 bytes). See the .asm file for usage notes and customization options. To be inserted as level ASM (can be inserted in GM14, but probably not a mechanic that should be enabled for an entire hack).

Requested by Picayune.

packages.name: uberasm-graphical-air-meter-v2-0
packages.title: Graphical Air Meter v2.0.2
packages.description:
This is basically similar to the sprite version, but recoded from scratch, and more customizability. The amount of time the player can be in the water, unlike the sprite version, can be any value rather than restricted to powers of 2 "ticks" (which happens at every !CountDownFrequency+1 frames) starting at 255 units.

changelog
Code
2025-06-14 (v2.0.2) - small update
 - Removed some redundant code relating to storing EXB1 (Index
   0; the maximum air value) into scratch RAM.

   the displayed meter fills up from empty as the player loses
   air rather than decreases from full.
2025-05-04 (v2.0.1) - text info update
 - Explained clearly about when later you need to change the
   defines settings that you need to update its copies and
   reinsert.

   the corresponding pieces set to 0 in Level_AirMeter.asm.
   This was only mentioned in the defines file.
 - Clarify CTRL+F "Static end tiles option" inside
   AirMeterDefines.asm on that file rather than being vague.
 - Corrected a description about !Freeram_AirMeterAirState
   that previously stated the wrong extra byte.
 - Placed a note in this readme explaining where the info
   about the extra bytes is in "Level_AirMeter.asm".
2025-04-11 (v2.0.1) - description update
 - Updated several graphical bar's write to HUD routine's
   description explaining that writing vertical bars routine
   should not be used for stripe.
 - Did mention on the insertion process instructions about the
   list.txt for a demo level test.
 - Explained more about sprite positioning in the defines.
2025-04-06 (v2.0.1) - minor fixes and small features
 - Fixed a problem with the COURSE CLEAR! message when using
   stripe.

   sprite. This took me FOREVER making sure this works right.
2025-03-31 (v2.0) - BIG massive update
 - Uses updated version of the graphical bar system.
 - Vertical bar support.
 - Makes use of UAT v2.1's new features: extra bytes. This
   allows variations of the same level ASM without duplicates.
 --Included per-level different lengths of time of being in

 - Makes use of UAT's routines folder, really love that I can

 -Supports stripe image and sprite OAM (does not occupy

 -When set to use sprite OAM, supports multiple tilesets for
  the bar rather than having a single set so you can have a
  per-level sprite graphics without conflicts (assuming you
  have enough tiles) with other GFX.

packages.name: uberasm-ground-pound-yoshi-s-stomp-effect
packages.title: Ground Pound, Yoshi's Stomp Effect
packages.description:
This UberASM allows player to perform a ground pound with a defined button. It acts like Yoshi's stomp upon landing.

Credit is optional. Requested by Batata Douce.

packages.name: uberasm-hide-status-bar
packages.title: Hide Status Bar
packages.description:
A simple non-invasive code I (Anas) asked Ladida publicly on SnesLab half a year back to disable the status bar. The major advantage this code has is that via LM's tilemap editor, you can make any specific L3 tiles you want go over or behind L2! Before using, please note the following:

- The destination for the level's L3 BG tilemap must be set to 'Start of Layer 3'

- Works with MFG's parallax toolkit!

- Doesn't work with Mode 0 or anything using IRQ and layer 3 shenanigans like MFG's YI falling wall; for that you'll need Kevin's toggled per-level status bar instead. Don't merge that patch's UberASM code with this code though!

- The aforementioned patch is also necessary to fix a bug where layer 3 will jitter when the screen scrolls. Don't turn on the 'fix layer 3 scroll sync option' via LM in your level or the problem will be worse!

- Kevin's sprite item box patch is recommended, lest you have a floating reserve item with no border of any sort surrounding it. This patch includes an option to enable it in certain levels with a free RAM

packages.name: uberasm-hold-x-to-item-swim
packages.title: Hold X to Item Swim
packages.description:
While underwater, makes Mario act like he's holding an Item by holding X.

Intended purpose is for water levels, to make him Item-Swim without an item.
Also has the effect of letting him regular swim while holding an item (when not holding X).

packages.name: uberasm-horizontal-layer
packages.title: Horizontal Layer 3 Smashers
packages.description:
This piece of uberASM gives you an effect equivalent to the Vertical Layer 3 Smashers found in World 1's castle, but horizontal, the screen scrolling upwards.

To use, make your level vertical and only use the leftmost screen, no scrolling.
Insert the included layer 3 graphics files using the #lm{l3gfxby} Layer 3 GFX/Tilemap Bypass.
The settings for the tilemap are to start below the status bar and to be 512x512, as the filename says.

To change where the autoscroll stops, edit the define in the ASM.

packages.name: uberasm-horizontal-speed-limit
packages.title: Horizontal Speed Limit
packages.description:
Makes it so player can run only at certain speed, similar to Iceguy's patch.
Maximum speed values can be configured through ASM.
Credit is unecessary.

packages.name: uberasm-horizontal-vertical-autoscroll
packages.title: Horizontal/Vertical Autoscroll
packages.description:
This code will enable horizontal or vertical autoscrolling in the level it's inserted in. Check out the asm file for customization options, such as scroll direction, speed/fractional speed and when to start and stop the autoscroll.

Note: when using horizontal autoscrolling with a high speed, Mario will die instead of being pushed by the border of the screen.

Note 2: usage of this patch is recommended to solve spawning issues when using this.

Update:
- Added horizontal autoscroll option.
- Added option to teleport when the autoscroll stops (suggested by TheMorganah).

packages.name: uberasm-horizontal-vertical-level-wrap
packages.title: Horizontal/Vertical Level Wrap
packages.description:
This contains two level routines to wrap Mario/sprites when they cross certain edges of the screen.

One of the routines handles horizontal level wrapping (which links the top and bottom of the screen), while the other handles vertical level wrapping (which links the left and right edges). The latter requires a small additional patch in order to work correctly.

Tester's note: do not use the horizontal wrap with the vertical scroll enabled.

packages.name: uberasm-hurt-kill-on-button-press-v1
packages.title: Hurt/Kill on Button Press v1.1
packages.description:
This UberASM allows you to set up a combination of buttons that will hurt or kill Mario when pressed. You can set the logic to hurt/kill when any of the selected buttons are pressed, or when all of the selected buttons are pressed. If using the latter, keep in mind that some combinations may not be possible in practice due to controller/keyboard limitations.
By default, it is set to kill Mario when left or right are pressed.

Requested by DasFueller.

v1.1: A/B and X/Y are now separated, so B cannot be triggered by A, nor Y by X.
-Edit: Tweaked the code so it also works for player 2.

packages.name: uberasm-hurt-kill-on-sound-effect-trigger-v1
packages.title: Hurt/Kill on Sound Effect Trigger V1.1
packages.description:
Hurts or kills Mario when any sound effect starts playing (choose which option in the asm file).
Requested by Golden Yoshi.

yoshifanatic's Update:
- Made this use UberASMTool 2.0's end label to make this less janky.
- Added 3 tables that allow you to customize which sounds hurt/kill you. By default, the pause, time running out, the Yoshi drum commands, and AddmusicK's pause/echo commands don't hurt you.
- Made it so this UberASM doesn't run during level end or no Yoshi intros.

versions.title: Hurt/Kill on Sound Effect Trigger V1.1

packages.name: uberasm-hypothermia
packages.title: Hypothermia
packages.description:
With this code, the player will die from cold if they stand still for too long. They will begin to shake as a sign of warning before dying. They can also get hurt or instantly killed if they try to swim in water if set to do so.

Defines for the amount of frames it takes for the player to die, when to make the player shake, give immunity when star power is active, and whether to hurt or instantly kill or not when touching water are included.

packages.name: uberasm-infinite-star
packages.title: Infinite Star
packages.description:
Makes it so star power is infinite once a star is collected.
Includes two variants: one changes the music to the regular star theme, and another which keeps the level music intact.

packages.name: uberasm-input-combination-taunt
packages.title: Input Combination Taunt
packages.description:
This code makes the player strike a pose when certain inputs are held.
Uses 3 bytes of freeRAM.
You can find all the configuration options if you open the .asm file.

packages.name: uberasm-input-playback
packages.title: Input Playback
packages.description:
Pauses the game at the start of the level and records inputs until L or R is pressed. Then the recorded inputs are played back. If the inputs end before transitioning rooms or completing the level, Mario dies.

As seen in the Halo 14 Side B level MARCHROMT30A and the hack Memorabilia by LightAligns and Saela.

packages.name: uberasm-instant-death-on-powerup-loss-v2
packages.title: Instant Death on Powerup Loss v2.1
packages.description:
This uberASM can be inserted as level specific asm or as gamemode 14.

All it does, is, killing the player instantly, after getting hurt.

Update to Version 2.1:
-Small optimizations

Compatible with SA-1

versions.title: Instant Death on Powerup Loss v2.1

packages.name: uberasm-instant-special-world-palette
packages.title: Instant Special World Palette
packages.description: This UberASM will make the "special world level is passed" (as set in Lunar Magic's dialog) palette load as soon as the level is beaten, instead of having to refresh the overworld. Insert in gamemode D. Uses 1 byte of freeram.

packages.name: uberasm-invisible-mario
packages.title: Invisible Mario
packages.description:
This uberasm hides the player's graphic.

Credit is optional.

packages.name: uberasm-invisible-powerup
packages.title: Invisible Powerup
packages.description: This powerup will allow you to walk through enemies and walls for a period of time. Includes: the patch itself, a sprite, and a block. I think I tested it pretty well, so I hope it doesn't get rejected for that reason. Video. Ignore the status bar and one hit kill in the video.

packages.name: uberasm-jump-trigger-switch
packages.title: Jump Trigger Switch
packages.description:
A jump triggered gimmick that will change a switch's state. By default, it will flip the on/off flag, though this can be easily modified to work with exanimations as well. This also has a quality of life implementation to allow for frame perfect and/or buffered jumps to still trigger the switch. With other code, if the player jumps too early, the switch state will not be changed. This fixes that bug, which should make it quite useful for kaizo hacks and should hopefully mitigate any "jank".

Requested by zynnoir.

packages.name: uberasm-kill-at-a-certain-y-position
packages.title: Kill at a Certain Y-Position
packages.description:
This uberASM will kill the player once they reach certain Y-position. Originally made for Hackjam.

Credit is unecessary.

packages.name: uberasm-kill-player-on-button-press-v1-3
packages.title: Kill Player on Button Press v1.3.0
packages.description:
Kill the player after a button of your choice has been pressed a given amount of times.

This UberASM allows to configure which button(s) to detect, how many times you need to press them, if you want to hurt or kill Mario, and other things.

This comes with a status bar routine for drawing the button press counter in the status bar, and with an indicator sprite that follows Mario (both are optional).

Requested by The_Uber_Camper (request).

versions.title: Kill Player on Button Press v1.3.0

packages.name: uberasm-kill-sprites-in-bottomless-pits
packages.title: Kill Sprites in Bottomless Pits
packages.description:
This UberASM code makes it so if a sprite falls into a bottomless pit, it is killed off permanently, which means it won't respawn. Supports exceptions that can be configured, so that not all sprites are killed in pits.

Requested by AmperSam.

packages.name: uberasm-l-r-power-up-selector
packages.title: L/R Power-up Selector
packages.description: This code allows Mario to gain a configurable powerup after pressing L, R and/or both. Check the asm file for configuration options.

packages.name: uberasm-layer
packages.title: Layer 2 Falls
packages.description: This UberASM is basically a disassembly of the "Layer 2 Falls" sprite (sprite ED), with some customization options, such as speed, acceleration, movement direction (vertical up or down, horizontal left or right), etc. You can also change it to move layer 1 instead (basically acting as an autoscroller). With the default parameters it acts the same as the vanilla sprite.

packages.name: uberasm-layer-2-smash-savage
packages.title: Layer 2 Smash: Savage Version
packages.description: This is an version of the Layer 2 smasher which stuns the player in place if he's on the ground once it hits. Check the ASM file for more info.

packages.name: uberasm-level-progress-bar-v1
packages.title: Level Progress Bar v1.01
packages.description:
This is a combination of UberASM + Sprite, that will draw a bar to the screen which shows Mario's completion of the level as his position relative to the end screen edge. It works for horizontal levels of any size, and vertical levels. You can apply it globally, or make it specific to certain levels. You can also customize the screen position, and where in SP1/SP2/SP3/SP4 the graphics are placed. See the README for information, installation instructions and usage notes.

v1.01:
- Moved the GM13 code to GM12 to fix a graphical bug in Mode 7 Koopa Kid fights.

v1: Initial Release.

packages.name: uberasm-level-timer-air-meter
packages.title: Level Timer Air Meter
packages.description: This UberASM code reworks the level timer to be used as an air meter for the level it has been inserted, allowing for an easily insertable air meter.

packages.name: uberasm-level-warp-display-v1-1
packages.title: Level Warp Display v1.1.1
packages.description:
An easy to configure level code for creating warp hubs.
It displays a custom text in the top left corner, switching between values when pressing left or right. Pushing A or B sends you to the designated level.
The text displayed, destination level and amount of levels can be easily changed, just add or remove values from the tables.

Useful for debugging or actual in game hubs.

Changelog
yoshifanatic's update:
- Made this asar 2.0 compatible.
- Made this compatible with vertical levels and Lunar Magic 3.00's horizontal level modes.
- Fixed an oversight where this will run during No-Yoshi intros.
- Made it so the code doesn't run when the game is paused.
- Made it so layer 3 is given priority so the text is always visible.
- Fixed an oversight where the secondary entrance macro didn't calculate the format for $19D8 correctly for secondary entrances greater than FF.

packages.name: uberasm-lightning-generator-v1-0
packages.title: Lightning Generator v1.0.1
packages.description:
A visual generator which displays a lightning effect. It can be customised to write to any colour on the palette (it's 0 by default which affects the background) as well as customised in what colours the lightning will generate, how long it waits between each strike, etc.

Also included is a generator which can be inserted with PIXI if you prefer the old-school way.

packages.name: uberasm-lives-select-menu-on-title-screen
packages.title: Lives Select Menu on Title Screen
packages.description:
A couple of gamemode codes which add a custom life selection menu in the title screen. The amount of lives can be configured: check the readme for more info.
Additionally, the menu can be disabled when continuing an already saved game, as in the second gif.

Requested by E-man38.

versions.title: Lives Select Menu on Title Screen

packages.name: uberasm-lock-mario-in-place-with-l-or-r
packages.title: Lock Mario in Place With L or R
packages.description:
I was asked for this very simple level ASM multiple times so I think it is a good idea to upload it.

All this does is set mario's position next frame to his position this frame if L is pressed. That means momentum is stored and can be gained even when locked. You can gain p-speed that way and change your direction midair.

You can die if you lock mario during an autoscroll as the screen will go past him.

Works in vertical levels as well.

versions.title: Lock Mario in Place With L or R

packages.name: uberasm-low-gravity
packages.title: Low Gravity
packages.description:
Fancy low gravity mechanic which makes Mario a whole lot more floaty while in the Air.

That's 'bout it!

packages.name: uberasm-low-lives-indicator
packages.title: Low Lives Indicator
packages.description:
This UberASM can be configured to play a sound effect and/or blink the life count in the status bar when the player has a minimum number of lives. This is meant to be used as a visual or sound cue that the player has low lives and near a Game Over.

The blinking effect assume a vanilla status bar, it will not necessarily work with custom status bars or sprite status bars. I would not recommend having it play a sound with a high minimum life count, as a constant noise playing would be quite irritating (you'll have to imagine it in the GIF below).

This requires UberASM Tool 2.0, as it needs to run during end:.

packages.name: uberasm-magic-limit
packages.title: Magic Limit
packages.description:
Limits the number of spawned magikoopa magics (and sprites they turn into). If the limit is reached, the oldest sprite is despawned.

(Screenshot shows limit of 3)

packages.name: uberasm-make-stars-sparkle
packages.title: Make Stars Sparkle
packages.description:
A purely cosmetic UberASM code, which makes star power-ups emit sparkles.

Requested by Ayami during Summer C3 2023. Credit is unecessary.

packages.name: uberasm-mario-always-spins
packages.title: Mario Always Spins
packages.description:
A simple ASM with Mario constantly rotating.
No credits required.

Requested by KaidenThelens.

packages.name: uberasm-max-speed-gives-invincibility
packages.title: Max Speed Gives Invincibility
packages.description:
Max Speed gives Invincibility (with flashing palettes on the player and sparkles)
When decelerating the player is vulnerable again.
(requested by 1UPdudes)

packages.name: uberasm-mega-man-styled-scrolling-for-vertical-levels
packages.title: Mega Man Styled Scrolling for Vertical Levels
packages.description:
This code will make the camera in a Vertical Level act like one found
in vertical segments of Mega Man or Super Mario Bros. 2

For this feature to work, the level header must indicate either "No Vertical Scrolling" or "No Horizontal or Vertical Scrolling".
In addition, the Starting FG position must not be 0, or else the player will die when going down a screen.

Uses one byte of freeRAM (default $5E, which is unused in vertical levels).

No credit necessary.

versions.title: Mega Man Styled Scrolling for Vertical Levels

packages.name: uberasm-mid-air-jump-changer
packages.title: Mid-air Jump Changer
packages.description:
Allows player to change jump mid-air. Pressing A while jumping causes player to spin and pressing B while spin-jumping cancels spin. Not to be confused with Airjump and airspin.
Credit is optional.

Minor update: Fixed underwater.
Semi-major update: Added a check for AddMusicK-modified ROMs to avoid conflicting with custom music, and included an option for no jump change sound effect at all.

packages.name: uberasm-midway-point-pose
packages.title: Midway Point Pose
packages.description:
Makes Mario show a pose for a few seconds after touching the midway point, like in SM3DLand.


Credit is not needed.


Requested by Link13

05/09/2022
FINALLY added the missing stuff I mentioned, the resource should function correctly now

packages.name: uberasm-modern-starman-v1
packages.title: Modern Starman V1.1
packages.description:
This UberASM increases Mario's P-speed and reduces the amount of time required for P-speed while he has a Starman active. Check the asm file for customization options.

Note: Use this tweak to prevent a bug where Mario can rapidly turn while in an icy level.

yoshifanatic's update:
- Fixed an oversight where spin jumping/cape spinning causes Mario to rapidly alternate between moving left/right when he has P-speed.
- Fixed a bug where you could clip into walls while running with P-speed.
- Fixed a bug where you'd gain P-speed just by holding down X/Y without moving.
- Fixed a bug where you could fill your P-meter by running into a wall.
- Added checks to stop Mario from keeping his P-speed when climbing, ducking, swimming, stunned, sliding, and while using a P-balloon and lakitu cloud.
- Made it so the turning is not instant.
- Optimized the code a little.

packages.name: uberasm-modify-timers
packages.title: Modify Timers
packages.description:
This allows you to modify up to 11 different timers per level, making some faster or slower.

You must patch modifytimers_asar.asm with Asar.

Requires 11 bytes of empty space, its recommended that if you aren't going to use specific timers to remove them.

You'll have to remove them from both modifytimers_asar.asm and modifytimers_uber.asm for things to work.

Currently supports:
* Bullet Shooter Timer
* Bullet Generator Timer
* PBalloon Timer
* Falling Spike Timer
* Hit Invincibility Timer
* PSwitch Timer
* Keyhole Exit Timer
* Throwblock Timer
* Thwomp/Thwimp Timers
* Yoshi Swallow Timer

packages.name: uberasm-money-for-life
packages.title: Money for Life
packages.description:
A recreation of Superyoshi's Money for Life except optimised and more customisable (like different RAM addresses or initialisation).

Look in the ASM file to see what you can edit.

packages.name: uberasm-movement-boost-on-time-low
packages.title: Movement Boost on Time Low
packages.description:
This simple UberASM enhances Mario's speed and acceleration physics when the timer falls below 100. As well as making his P‐Speed faster, it also allows him to turn quicker, travel much faster in water, and gain flight with the cape much quicker.

Note: Be careful about using it in levels with the initial timer set to 0 by default, since it will not check for this and will give Mario a permanent boost for the whole level.

Credit is unnecessary but appreciated.

packages.name: uberasm-multi-step-autoscroll-v1
packages.title: Multi-step Autoscroll V1.1
packages.description:
This code allows you to create your own special autoscroll that goes where you want at the speed you want, much like the generator used in Butter Bridge 1 (level 00C) in the original game.

It works by using tables where you store X/Y speeds for each step of the autoscroll. It allows the use of fractional speeds and can be paused/resumed anytime you want using a flag. Plus, all the free RAM used can be easily changed to avoid conflicts, and the whole scrolling code can either stop or loop when it reaches the end of the tables.

UPDATE: You can now setup a custom code that will interrupt the autoscroll and be executed at certain points in time. This way, you force the player to progress only if a certain thing has been done.
Default code is the classic "advance if all sprites have been killed".

Details in .asm file.

yoshifanatic's update:
- Fixed a warning about LDA $XX,y not being a valid opcode when inserting this to non-SA-1 ROMs.
- Added mention of this patch in case users run into issues with sprites spawning.
- Made !ListLength automatic, so the user doesn't need to keep track of the size of the ignored sprite list.
- Fixed a bug where this runs during no Yoshi intros.
- Added throw blocks, Peach, the bonus game, winged cage, layer 3 smasher, side exit, ball n' chain, Bowser, wooden spikes, and Bowser statue to the list of ignored sprites.
- Fixed an oversight where the sprite check breaks when not using PIXI.
- Made various minor code optimizations.

packages.name: uberasm-music-playlist
packages.title: Music Playlist
packages.description:
This patch will allow you to create a playlist of custom or vanilla songs for individual levels. You can navigate between the songs by holding Select then pressing either L or R. Perfect for long grind levels or for audio leveling.

This is meant to be used along with AddMusicK and the retry patch. The included asar patch fixes an issue where the music would reset back to the level default on each death.

packages.name: uberasm-nerf-yoshi
packages.title: Nerf Yoshi
packages.description:
This Uberasm allows you to nerf Yoshi, by removing/restricting his various abilities, and/or by setting a timer that will destroy the Yoshi upon hitting zero. This makes it so that Yoshi's abilities/perks have a cost to them, and forces the player to use their Yoshi more strategically.

The Uberasm has a wide range of customizable effects, which both affect Yoshi's abilities, and the speed the timer decrements, should you choose to set it. Can be used on a per-level basis, or as Game Mode 14.

Uses 2 bytes of freeram as a main timer and a ticker timer.

See the included readme for detailed descriptions and usage of every effect/mechanic.

Please give credit if used.

packages.name: uberasm-new-super-mario-bros-wii-styled-secret-passages
packages.title: New Super Mario Bros. Wii Styled Secret Passages
packages.description: This UberASM will hide layer 2 while Mario is near it, which can be used to reveal secret passages like how New Super Mario Bros. Wii handles its secret passages. You can either have the spotlight around Mario always active or only appear when a certain trigger is activated (such as $14AF).

versions.title: New Super Mario Bros. Wii Styled Secret Passages

packages.name: uberasm-no-consecutive-score-awards
packages.title: No Consecutive Score Awards
packages.description:
Basically the same thing as this patch but as UberASM, so it can be applied on a per-level basis. There's options to enable/disable the effect for certain stuff like in the original patch.
Requested by KatMakes.

packages.name: uberasm-no-downward-swim-when-carrying-an-item
packages.title: No Downward Swim When Carrying an Item
packages.description:
This uberasm code simply disables downward swimming when carrying an item.

Credit is unecessary. Requested by buckaroodle610.

versions.title: No Downward Swim When Carrying an Item

packages.name: uberasm-no-fireballs-in-water
packages.title: No Fireballs in Water
packages.description: This uberASM code disables shooting fireballs when in water.

packages.name: uberasm-no-forward-momentum
packages.title: No Forward Momentum
packages.description:
This patch changes the game's physics. It makes Mario stop on a dime when you release left or right on the D-Pad on the ground, in the air, underwater, everywhere.
Now works with slopes.

packages.name: uberasm-no-item-swim
packages.title: No Item Swim
packages.description: This piece of code will disable Item Swimming. Requested by buckaroodle610.

packages.name: uberasm-no-overworld-v1
packages.title: No Overworld v1.3
packages.description:
Originally inspired by a resource from Alcaro, and does pretty much the same thing: disables returning to overworld after beating levels and instead has the player go through levels in a sequence, either in numerical order or in an order defined by you.

Changelog
v1.3 (by AmperSam)
- made compatible with UberASM Tool 2.0
- dropped the 'global_code' instructions in favour of gamemode
- generally made the options and instructions more understandable and readable

v1.2
- Fixed crash with retry patch
- Fixed graphic issue when using "VWF intro 1.22"
- Fixed Player 2 compatiblity with "Exit Block (no OW events)" and "Door exit"
- More info for coders.txt

Thanks to Darolac for pointing some of these issues and testing.

v1.1
- Supports two players
- Secret exits(advanced mode)
- various fixes
- clean.asm is now integrated in NoOverworld.asm

packages.name: uberasm-no-yoshi-intro-uberasm
packages.title: No-Yoshi Intro UberASM
packages.description: This UberASM enables the no-Yoshi/ghost house/castle intro upon touching it. Important conditions are inside the .asm file. Thanks to Karisa for the original code and yoshifanatic for info related to the 'mounting off Yoshi' animation! Requires this UberASM if you wanna filter Yoshi at the checkpoint.

packages.name: uberasm-nsmb-rising-water
packages.title: NSMB Rising Water
packages.description:
This will make the layer 3 tide water rise when a specified switch is activated.

Make sure to set the layer 3 settings to "low tide only".

Video

packages.name: uberasm-offscreen-indicator
packages.title: Offscreen Indicator
packages.description:
This will display an 8x8 or 16x16 sprite tile at the top or bottom of the screen at Mario's X position whenever he goes offscreen. This way, the player can tell where he is even though they can't see him.

This update makes it so you can optionally have the marker scale away from the edge of the screen based on how far Mario is offscreen, as well.

Note: due to the timing of how sprite graphical data is handled, this code only works in level ASM, not game mode ASM. If you want to apply this to all levels, use the patch version.

packages.name: uberasm-offscreen-indicator-for-sprites
packages.title: Offscreen Indicator for Sprites
packages.description: This UberASM will show an indicator for sprites that are offscreen vertically. Check out the asm file for customization options.

packages.name: uberasm-on-demand-reserve-powerup
packages.title: On-Demand Reserve Powerup
packages.description:
Allows the player to fill the reserve item box on the fly for a configurable currency (of lives, coins, or Dragon Coins) and rate. Which powerup given can be determined on a per-level basis with the extra byte.

Requested by bandicoot.
Requires UberASM 2.0 or higher.

Setting Powerup with the Extra Byte
: 01 gives a Mushroom
: 02 gives a Fire Flower
: 03 gives a Star*
: 04 gives a Cape Feather

*With the Star, be prepared to address the myriad of sprites that do not have proper kill frames.
